`i_{(k)} / i^{(k)}` (falling over rising factorial) and eigenvalue `-(k.choose 2)`.

articles.title: Tavaré's formula
articles.statement:
The transition probabilities of Kingman's block-counting process
from `i` to `j` lineages in time `t`, for `1 ≤ j ≤ i ≤ n`, are given by `tavareProb`.

## Sources

- Tavaré (1984). Proves the deferred entry `exp_blockCountingGenerator_apply`.

articles.title: Truncation consistency
articles.statement:
For `n ≤ N`, the top-left `(n + 1) × (n + 1)` block of the
transition matrix `exp (t • G)` of the block-counting process on `{0, …, N}` is the transition
matrix of the process on `{0, …, n}` (the process only moves down). Holds for every real `t`.

articles.title: The block-counting process never gains lineages
articles.statement:
The block-counting process never gains lineages: `exp (t • G) i j = 0` for `i < j`. Holds
for every real `t`.

articles.title: Spectral decomposition of the block-counting transition matrix
articles.statement:
The spectral decomposition of the transition matrix of the block-counting process:
`exp (t • G) = V diag(exp (-(k.choose 2) t)) W`.

articles.title: Tavaré's formula for the number of ancestral lineages
articles.statement:
Tavaré's closed form for the probability that `i` lineages of Kingman's coalescent have
`j` ancestors `t` time units (`2N` generations each) earlier, for `1 ≤ j ≤ i`.

articles.title: Scaled Wright–Fisher lineage matrix converges to Kingman's generator
articles.statement:
The scaled one-generation increment `M • (wfLineageMatrix n M - 1)` converges entrywise to
the block-counting generator: `k` lineages coalesce to `k - 1` with probability
`(k.choose 2) / M + o(1/M)`, and to fewer with probability `O(1/M²)`.

articles.title: Kingman's theorem for the lineage count
articles.statement:
For `t ≥ 0`, the `⌊t M⌋`-generation transition
matrix of the Wright–Fisher ancestral lineage count converges, as the population size `M`
tends to infinity, to the transition matrix `exp (t • G)` of the pure-death process with rates
`k.choose 2`.

## Sources

- Kingman (1982); Durrett (2008), ch. 1. Proves the deferred entry `tendsto_wfLineageMatrix_pow_floor`.

articles.title: Wright–Fisher transition matrix of the lineage count
articles.statement:
The one-generation transition matrix of the ancestral lineage count of a sample of at most
`n` gene copies in a Wright–Fisher population of `M` copies; row `k`, column `j` is
`wfLineageProb M k j`.

articles.title: Wright–Fisher transition probability of the lineage count
articles.statement:
One-generation transition probability of the ancestral lineage count in a neutral
Wright–Fisher population of `M` gene copies: `k` lineages pick their parents uniformly and
independently among `M` copies, and `j` distinct parents occur with probability
`stirlingSecond k j * M.descFactorial j / M ^ k`.

articles.title: Generator of the Λ-coalescent block-counting process
articles.statement:
The generator of the **block-counting process** of the Λ-coalescent on the states
`0, …, n` (state `b` means `b` blocks): from `b` blocks the process jumps to `j < b` blocks at
rate `(b.choose (b + 1 - j)) λ_{b, b + 1 - j}` (a `(b + 1 - j)`-merger), and the diagonal is
`-λ_b`. States `0` and `1` are absorbing (state `0` is never reached from `b ≥ 1`).

articles.title: Uniqueness in Pitman's representation
articles.statement:
A finite measure on `[0, 1]` is determined by
its merger rates; indeed by the rates `λ_{k,k} = ∫ x ^ (k - 2) Λ(dx)` of complete mergers,
which are its moments (Pitman 1999, Theorem 1).

articles.title: Pitman's representation theorem, existence half
articles.statement:
**Pitman's representation theorem, existence half** (Pitman 1999, Theorem 1): every
consistent family of nonnegative merger rates `r b k`, `2 ≤ k ≤ b`, is the family of merger
rates `λ_{b,k}` of some finite measure `Λ` on `[0, 1]`. (Uniqueness of `Λ` is
`LambdaCoalescent.eq_of_mergerRate_eq`.)

## Sources

- Pitman (1999), Theorem 1; Hausdorff (1921).

articles.title: Λ-coalescent block-counting generator is a rate matrix
articles.statement:
The block-counting generator is a rate matrix: its jump rates are nonnegative and each
row sums to `0`, since the jump rates out of `b` blocks add up to `λ_b`.

articles.title: Pitman's consistency relation
articles.statement:
**Pitman's consistency relation** `λ_{b,k} = λ_{b+1,k} + λ_{b+1,k+1}` for `2 ≤ k ≤ b`
(Pitman 1999; Berestycki 2009, §3.1): a given `k`-set of `b` blocks merges, with an extra
block present, either without it or together with it.

articles.title: Kingman's coalescent
articles.statement:
**Kingman's coalescent** is the Λ-coalescent with `Λ = δ₀`: only binary mergers occur,
each pair merging at rate `1` (Pitman 1999; Berestycki 2009, §3.1).

articles.title: Merger rates are bounded by the total mass of Λ
articles.statement: A merger rate is at most the total mass of `Λ`.

articles.title: Nonnegativity of Λ-coalescent merger rates
articles.statement: Merger rates are nonnegative.

articles.title: Pitman's integral formula for merger rates when $2 \le k \le b$
articles.statement: The merger rate inside its domain.

articles.title: Pair merger rate of a Λ-coalescent
articles.statement:
Two blocks merge at rate `Λ [0, 1]`; `Λ` is often normalized to a probability measure,
so that this pair rate is `1` as in Kingman's coalescent.

articles.title: Merger rates of the Bolthausen–Sznitman coalescent
articles.statement:
The **Bolthausen–Sznitman coalescent** (`Λ` = Lebesgue measure on `[0, 1]`) has merger
rates given by the Beta integral `λ_{b,k} = (k - 2)! (b - k)! / (b - 1)!` for `2 ≤ k ≤ b`
(Bolthausen–Sznitman 1998; Pitman 1999; Berestycki 2009, §3.1).

articles.title: Pitman's merger rate
articles.statement:
**Pitman's merger rate** `λ_{b,k} = ∫ x ^ (k - 2) (1 - x) ^ (b - k) Λ(dx)`: while there are
`b` blocks, the rate at which a given set of `k` of them merges into one block, for
`2 ≤ k ≤ b` (Pitman 1999, Theorem 1; Sagitov 1999). Powers are natural-number powers, so
`0 ^ 0 = 1`. Outside `2 ≤ k ≤ b` no such merger exists, and the rate is defined to be `0`.

articles.title: Binomial identity behind the total merger rate
articles.statement:
The polynomial identity behind the closed form of the total merger rate:
`x ^ 2 ∑_{k=2}^b (b.choose k) x ^ (k - 2) (1 - x) ^ (b - k) = 1 - (1 - x) ^ b -
b x (1 - x) ^ (b - 1)` for every real `x` and every `b` (binomial theorem).

articles.title: Total merger rate of Kingman's coalescent
articles.statement: For Kingman's coalescent the total merger rate is the number of pairs, `λ_b = b.choose 2`.

articles.title: The total merger rate in closed form
articles.statement:
**The total merger rate in closed form** (Berestycki 2009, §3.1):
`λ_b = (b.choose 2) Λ {0} + ∫_{(0,1]} (1 - (1 - x) ^ b - b x (1 - x) ^ (b - 1)) / x ^ 2 Λ(dx)`.
The atom at `0` (the Kingman part) is split off, so no division by `0` occurs.

articles.title: Monotonicity of the total merger rate
articles.statement: The total merger rate `λ_b` is nondecreasing in the number of blocks `b`.

articles.title: Nonnegativity of the total merger rate
articles.statement: The total merger rate is nonnegative.

articles.title: Recursion for the total merger rate
articles.statement:
Adding a block raises the total merger rate by `b λ_{b+1,2}`:
`λ_{b+1} = λ_b + b λ_{b+1,2}`. The new events are exactly the binary mergers of the new block
with one of the `b` old ones (a consequence of the consistency relation).

articles.title: Total merger rate of the Bolthausen–Sznitman coalescent
articles.statement: For the Bolthausen–Sznitman coalescent the total merger rate is `λ_b = b - 1` (`b ≥ 1`).

articles.title: Total merger rate of a Λ-coalescent
articles.statement:
The **total merger rate** `λ_b = ∑_{k=2}^b (b.choose k) λ_{b,k}` while there are `b`
blocks (Pitman 1999; Berestycki 2009, §3.1).

articles.title: Unordered pairs of blocks
articles.statement: The unordered pairs of positions `i < j` among `k` blocks.

articles.title: Random joining has finite support and iterates the join step
articles.statement:
The random-joining law has finite support, and the expectation of a statistic of the
`j`-th visited list (`j ≤ m`) is the `j`-th iterate of `joinStep`.

articles.title: Expected site frequency spectrum
articles.statement:
**Expected site frequency spectrum** (Fu 1995). Let the genealogy of a sample of `n` gene
copies consist of Kingman holding times `K.T` and an independent block-size history `τ` with
the random-joining law. If, given the genealogy (the σ-algebra generated by `τ` and the
holding times), the number `ξ i` of sites whose derived allele is carried by exactly `i`
copies is integrable and has conditional mean `(θ / 2) L_i` (neutral infinite-sites mutation,
`θ = 4Nu`), then `E ξ_i = θ / i` for `1 ≤ i ≤ n - 1`. (Integrability matters: Mathlib's
conditional expectation of a non-integrable function is `0`.)

## Sources

- Fu (1995); Griffiths & Tavaré (1998). Proves the deferred entry `integral_sfs`.

articles.title: Expected number of blocks of size `i`
articles.statement:
**Expected number of blocks of size `i`** when `k` blocks remain, for random joining
started from `n` singletons: `k · C(n-i-1, k-2) / C(n-1, k-1)` (Fu 1995; Griffiths–Tavaré
1998). Equivalently, a given one of the `k` blocks has size `i` with probability
`C(n-i-1, k-2) / C(n-1, k-1)`.

articles.title: Transition operator of random joining
articles.statement:
The transition operator of random joining acting on a statistic `g` of block-size lists:
the average of `g` over the lists obtained from `b` by merging a uniformly chosen pair of
blocks (`g []` once fewer than two blocks remain). By `exists_finset_randomJoining`, its `j`-th
iterate at `b` is the expectation of `g` at step `j` of random joining started from `b`.

articles.title: Merging two blocks of a block-size list
articles.statement:
Merge the blocks at positions `i < j` of the block-size list `b`: remove both and append a
block of size `b[i] + b[j]`.

articles.title: Random-joining law on block-size lists
articles.statement:
The **random-joining** law: `randomJoining m b ps` is the probability that `m` steps of
random joining started from the block-size list `b` visit the list of block-size lists `ps`
(starting with `b` itself). Each step merges a pair of blocks chosen uniformly among all
pairs; the process stops once fewer than two blocks remain.

articles.title: Total branch length subtending i sample copies
articles.statement:
The total length of the branches subtending exactly `i` of the `n` sample copies, for the
block-size history `ps` (entry `n - k` lists the block sizes while there are `k` lineages)
and holding times `T`: `∑_{k=2}^{n} #{blocks of size i among k} · T k`.

articles.title: Expected block counts weighted by coalescence times sum to $2/i$
articles.statement:
Summing the expected block counts against `E T_k = (k.choose 2)⁻¹` gives `2 / i`:
`∑_{k=2}^{n} k C(n-i-1, k-2) / C(n-1, k-1) · (k.choose 2)⁻¹ = 2 / i` for `1 ≤ i < n`.

articles.title: Validity of the bound
articles.statement:
**Validity of the bound** (Hudson–Kaplan 1985): a valid breakpoint set has at least as
many points as any family of pairwise disjoint four-gamete intervals, since each interval needs
its own breakpoint.

articles.title: Greedy optimality
articles.statement:
No family of pairwise disjoint four-gamete intervals has more than
`R_m` members.

articles.title: The sweep yields exactly $R_m$ distinct breakpoints
articles.statement: The right endpoints of the kept intervals are distinct, so there are `R_m` of them.

articles.title: Haplotypes carrying an allele at a site
articles.statement:
The haplotypes carrying allele `a` at site `i`; when `a` is the derived allele this is the
clade defined by the mutation at `i`.

articles.title: $R_m$ is the minimum size of a valid breakpoint set
articles.statement:
The bound is attained: some valid breakpoint set has exactly `R_m` points, so `R_m` is the
minimum size of a valid breakpoint set.

articles.title: $R_m$ is the maximum number of disjoint four-gamete intervals
articles.statement:
The sweep attains the maximum: `R_m` is the largest size of a family of pairwise disjoint
four-gamete intervals.

articles.title: Four-gamete condition for two sites
articles.statement:
Sites `i` and `j` show all four gametes: for every pair of alleles `(a, b)` some haplotype
carries `a` at `i` and `b` at `j`. This reuses
`Cslib.Bioinformatics.Phylogenetics.Splits.FourGametes` applied to the site columns
`(M · i)` and `(M · j)`; it is not a second definition of the four-gamete predicate.

articles.title: Sweep cuts form a valid breakpoint set
articles.statement:
Cutting immediately to the left of the right endpoint of every kept interval gives a valid
breakpoint set.

articles.title: Valid set of recombination breakpoints
articles.statement:
A set `B` of breakpoints is valid for the sample `M` when it separates every pair of sites
`i < j` showing all four gametes.

articles.title: Hudson–Kaplan sweep yields disjoint four-gamete intervals
articles.statement: The intervals kept by the sweep are pairwise disjoint four-gamete intervals.

articles.title: Disjoint family of four-gamete intervals
articles.statement:
A family `F` of site pairs `(i, j)` consists of four-gamete intervals (`i < j`, all four
gametes at `i` and `j`) that are pairwise disjoint: of two distinct intervals, one ends at or
before the start of the other, so no breakpoint separates both.

articles.title: Intervals kept by the Hudson–Kaplan sweep are distinct
articles.statement: The intervals kept by the sweep are distinct.

articles.title: Characterization of site pairs failing the four-gamete test
articles.statement:
Two sites miss one of the four gametes exactly when, for some choice of the alleles `a` at
`i` and `b` at `j` (the derived alleles), the carrier sets are nested or disjoint, as two clades
of one rooted tree are.

articles.title: `R_m` is a lower bound
articles.statement:
**`R_m` is a lower bound** (Hudson–Kaplan 1985): every valid breakpoint set has at least
`R_m` points.

articles.title: Hudson and Kaplan's bound for tree-like blocks
articles.statement:
Suppose the breakpoints `B` cut the
sequence into blocks such that, within a block, the derived-allele clades of every two sites are
nested or disjoint for some choice of the derived alleles (as for sites whose mutations sit on
one tree under the infinite-sites model). Then there are at least `R_m` breakpoints.

articles.title: Hudson and Kaplan's `R_m`
articles.statement: The number of intervals kept by the sweep.

articles.title: Breakpoint separating two sites
articles.statement:
A breakpoint `g` (a cut immediately to the left of site `g`) separates sites `i` and `j`
when `i < g ≤ j`.

articles.title: One step of the Hudson–Kaplan sweep
articles.statement:
One step of the sweep at right endpoint `j`. The list `acc` holds the intervals kept so far,
most recent first; the next interval must start at or after the right end of the most recent
one (at or after site `0` if none was kept). Among the admissible four-gamete intervals ending
at `j`, the shortest one is kept.

articles.title: Hudson–Kaplan left-to-right sweep
articles.statement: The intervals kept by Hudson and Kaplan's left-to-right sweep, most recent first.

articles.title: Positivity of the number of pairs
articles.statement: The number of pairs `k.choose 2` is positive for `k ∈ [2, n]`.

articles.title: Integrability of coalescent holding times
articles.statement: Each holding time is integrable.

articles.title: Integrability of the total branch length
articles.statement: The total branch length is integrable.

articles.title: Integrability of Watterson's estimator
articles.statement: Watterson's estimator `S / H_{n-1}` is integrable when `S` is.

articles.title: Expected number of segregating sites
articles.statement:
Infinite-sites mutation at rate `θ/2` per lineage per unit time: if the number of
segregating sites `S` is integrable and has conditional mean `(θ/2) L` given the genealogy
σ-algebra `m`, then `E S = θ H_{n-1}`. (Integrability matters: Mathlib's conditional
expectation of a non-integrable function is `0`.)

articles.title: Expected coalescent holding time
articles.statement: `E[T k] = (k.choose 2)⁻¹`.

articles.title: Expected time to the most recent common ancestor
articles.statement: The expected time to the most recent common ancestor is `2 (1 - 1/n)`.

articles.title: Expected total branch length of the coalescent
articles.statement: The expected total branch length is `2 H_{n-1}`.

articles.title: Holding times of Kingman's coalescent
articles.statement:
Kingman's coalescent for a sample of size `n`, through its holding times: `T k` is the
time (in units of `2N` generations) during which the genealogy has exactly `k` lineages,
for `2 ≤ k ≤ n`. These are independent, and `T k` is exponential with rate `k.choose 2`.
The values of `T k` for `k ∉ [2, n]` are irrelevant.

articles.title: No-coalescence probability as a falling factorial ratio
articles.statement: `noCoalProb M k` is the falling factorial `M (M-1) ⋯ (M-k+1)` divided by `M ^ k`.

articles.title: Probability of no coalescence in one Wright–Fisher generation
articles.statement:
In a Wright–Fisher population of `M` gene copies, the probability that `k` lineages,
choosing their parents independently and uniformly, have `k` distinct parents.

articles.title: Kingman coalescent from coordinate projections
articles.statement:
The coordinate projections of `piMeasure n` form a Kingman coalescent; in particular
`KingmanTimes` is inhabited for every sample size.

articles.title: Canonical probability space for Kingman holding times
articles.statement:
The canonical probability space for the Kingman holding times of a sample of size `n`:
the product of the exponential laws `Exp (k.choose 2)`, `2 ≤ k ≤ n`.

articles.title: Sum of reciprocals of binomial coefficients $\binom{k}{2}$
articles.statement: `∑_{k=2}^n (k.choose 2)⁻¹ = 2 (1 - 1/n)` for `n ≥ 1` (telescoping `2/(k(k-1))`).

articles.title: Weighted sum of reciprocals of $\binom{k}{2}$ is twice a harmonic number
Kingman's coalescence rate
articles.statement:
For `M` gene copies (`M = 2N`), the per-generation
probability that some of `k` lineages coalesce is `(k.choose 2) / M + o(1/M)`; i.e. in time
units of `M` generations, coalescences occur at rate `k.choose 2`.

articles.title: No-coalescence probability tends to one
articles.statement: `noCoalProb M k → 1` as `M → ∞`.

articles.title: Wright–Fisher coalescence times converge to exponential laws
articles.statement:
After `⌊t M⌋` Wright–Fisher generations (`t ≥ 0` coalescent time units), the probability
that `k` lineages have not coalesced tends to `exp (-(k.choose 2) t)`, the survival function
of the exponential law with rate `k.choose 2`.

articles.title: Time to the most recent common ancestor
articles.statement: Time to the most recent common ancestor of the sample.

articles.title: Total branch length of a coalescent genealogy
articles.statement: Total branch length of the sample genealogy: `k` branches during `T k`.

articles.title: Variance of the time to the most recent common ancestor
articles.statement:
The variance of the time to the most recent common ancestor is
`∑_{k=2}^n ((k.choose 2)⁻¹)²` (this uses independence).

articles.title: Watterson's estimator is unbiased
articles.statement:
`E[S / H_{n-1}] = θ` for a sample of size
`n ≥ 2`.

articles.title: Boundary of the four-species anomaly zone
articles.statement:
Degnan & Rosenberg (2006), eq. (4): the boundary `a(x)` of the four-species anomaly zone,
for a deeper internal branch of length `x > 0` (at `x = 0` the denominator vanishes and Lean's
`a / 0 = 0` gives the junk value `log (2/3 - 0)`; `a(x) → ∞` as `x → 0⁺`).

articles.title: Three-anomaly boundary is maximal at zero
articles.statement:
`b` is maximal at `0`: `b(x) ≤ log (7/6)` for `x ≥ 0`, so for `y ≥ log (7/6)` at most one
gene tree is anomalous.

articles.title: Value $\log(7/6)$ of the three-anomaly boundary at zero
articles.statement:
`b(0) = log (7/6)` (Degnan & Rosenberg 2006): if `y ≥ log (7/6)`, then `y ≥ b(x)` for every
`x ≥ 0` (`anomalyB_le_anomalyB_zero`).

articles.title: Boundary for three anomalous gene trees
articles.statement:
Degnan & Rosenberg (2006), eq. (5): the boundary `b(x)` below which the caterpillar species
tree has three anomalous gene trees (defined for `x ≥ 0`).

articles.title: No anomalous gene trees on the balanced four-species tree
articles.statement:
**No anomalous gene trees on the balanced four-species tree** (Degnan & Rosenberg 2006):
for nonnegative branch lengths, no gene tree is more probable than the one matching the
species tree `((0, 1), (2, 3))`. Given the numbers of lineages entering the root population,
the matching tree is already the most probable outcome of random joining.

articles.title: Balanced four-gene tree
articles.statement: The symmetric gene tree `((a, b), (c, d))` on four genes, as a set of clusters.

articles.title: Balanced four-species tree
articles.statement:
The symmetric (balanced) species tree `((0, 1), (2, 3))` with internal branch lengths `y₁`
(above the ancestor of `0, 1`) and `y₂` (above the ancestor of `2, 3`).

articles.title: Coalescence along one branch of the species tree
articles.statement:
One population of the multispecies coalescent along a branch of length `t`. It receives
`m` lineages `bs` (and the clusters `acc` formed below it). Under Kingman's coalescent the
number `j` of lineages left at the top of the branch has law `tavareProb m j t` (Tavaré's
formula, `exp_blockCountingGenerator_apply`), and, independently of the coalescence times, the
order of the `m - j` coalescences is the beginning of a random-joining history of the `m`
lineages (`randomJoining`). The continuation `k` receives the number of exiting lineages, the
lineages, and the clusters formed so far.

articles.title: Anomaly of ((A, C), (B, D)) and ((A, D), (B, C)) on the caterpillar
articles.statement:
On the caterpillar species tree with `x ≥ 0`, the gene trees `((A, C), (B, D))` and
`((A, D), (B, C))` are more probable than the matching gene tree if and only if `y < b(x)`.

articles.title: Anomalous gene tree on four species
articles.statement:
**Anomalous gene tree on four species** (Degnan & Rosenberg 2006): on the caterpillar
species tree with deeper branch `x > 0` and shallower branch `y`, the symmetric gene tree
`((A, B), (C, D))` is more probable than the gene tree matching the species tree if and only
if `y < a(x)`. With `caterpillar_le_matching` this gives `caterpillar_exists_anomalous_iff`.

articles.title: The four-species anomaly zone
articles.statement:
**The four-species anomaly zone** (Degnan & Rosenberg 2006, Definition 1 and Figure 2): the
caterpillar species tree with deeper branch `x > 0` and shallower branch `y ≥ 0` has an
anomalous gene tree, one strictly more probable than the gene tree matching the species
tree, if and only if `y < a(x)`.

articles.title: Only balanced gene trees can be anomalous on the caterpillar
articles.statement:
On the caterpillar species tree with nonnegative branch lengths, no asymmetric gene tree is
more probable than the matching one (Degnan & Rosenberg 2006): only the three balanced gene
trees can be anomalous.

articles.title: Caterpillar four-gene tree
articles.statement: The asymmetric gene tree `(((a, b), c), d)` on four genes, as a set of clusters.

articles.title: Caterpillar four-species tree
articles.statement:
The asymmetric (caterpillar) species tree `(((0, 1), 2), 3)`: `x` is the length of the
deeper internal branch (above the ancestor of `0, 1, 2`) and `y` that of the shallower one
(above the ancestor of `0, 1`), as in Degnan & Rosenberg (2006).

articles.title: Clusters formed along a ranked history
articles.statement:
The clusters formed during the first `t` coalescence events of `h` from the lineages `bs`:
every lineage present at some step `u ≤ t`, as the set of sampled genes it is ancestral to.

articles.title: Clusters of the caterpillar species tree
articles.statement: The species tree `(((0, 1), 2), 3)` has the clusters of the gene tree `(((0, 1), 2), 3)`.

articles.title: Clusters of the three-species tree
articles.statement: The species tree `((0, 1), 2)` has the clusters of the gene tree with cherry `{0, 1}`.

articles.title: Clusters of a species tree
articles.statement:
The clusters (clades) of a species tree: the sets of species below its vertices, including
the singletons and the full set of species.

articles.title: Gene tree displaying a quartet split
articles.statement:
A rooted gene tree on four genes `G` (a set of clusters) **displays the quartet split**
`ab | cd`, where `{c, d}` is the complement of `{a, b}`: forgetting the root, the internal edge
separates `{a, b}` from `{c, d}`; equivalently `{a, b}` or `{c, d}` is a cluster.

articles.title: Degnan–Rosenberg criterion: $f(x, y) < g(x, y)$ iff $y < b(x)$
articles.statement:
Degnan & Rosenberg (2006): for `x ≥ 0`, the gene tree `((A, C), (B, D))` (equivalently
`((A, D), (B, C))`) is more probable than the matching gene tree, `f(x, y) < g(x, y)`, if and
only if `y < b(x)`.

articles.title: The boundary `a(x)` of the anomaly zone
articles.statement:
**The boundary `a(x)` of the anomaly zone** (Degnan & Rosenberg 2006): for a deeper
internal branch `x > 0`, the symmetric gene tree `((A, B), (C, D))` is more probable than the
matching gene tree, `f(x, y) < h(x, y)`, if and only if `y < a(x)`.

articles.title: Degnan–Rosenberg probability of the matching caterpillar gene tree
articles.statement:
Degnan & Rosenberg (2006), eq. (1): `f(x, y)`, the probability of the matching gene tree
`(((A, B), C), D)` on the caterpillar species tree.

articles.title: $g(x, y) \le h(x, y)$ for a nonnegative shallower branch
articles.statement: `g(x, y) ≤ h(x, y)` for a nonnegative shallower branch (equality at `y = 0`).

articles.title: $g(x, y) < h(x, y)$ for a positive shallower branch
articles.statement:
For a positive shallower branch, the symmetric gene tree `((A, B), (C, D))` is strictly more
probable than `((A, C), (B, D))`: `g(x, y) < h(x, y)` (Degnan & Rosenberg 2006).

articles.title: Degnan–Rosenberg formula g for the gene tree ((A, C), (B, D))
articles.statement:
Degnan & Rosenberg (2006), eq. (2): `g(x, y)`, the probability of the gene tree
`((A, C), (B, D))` (and of `((A, D), (B, C))`) on the caterpillar species tree.

articles.title: Degnan–Rosenberg formula h for the gene tree ((A, B), (C, D))
articles.statement:
Degnan & Rosenberg (2006), eq. (3): `h(x, y)`, the probability of the gene tree
`((A, B), (C, D))` on the caterpillar species tree.

articles.title: Additivity of the exit law
articles.statement: `exitLaw` is additive in the continuation.

articles.title: Exit law of a constant continuation
articles.statement:
If a continuation takes the constant value `c` whenever at least one lineage exits, then
so does `exitLaw` (Tavaré's probabilities sum to one and random joining is a probability).

articles.title: Nonnegativity of the exit law
articles.statement:
On a species tree with nonnegative branch lengths, `exitLaw` of a continuation that is
nonnegative whenever at least one lineage exits is nonnegative (Tavaré's probabilities are
nonnegative, `tavareProb_nonneg`).

articles.title: Law of the lineages leaving a species-tree branch
articles.statement:
The law of the lineages leaving the top of the branch above a vertex of the species tree,
in continuation-passing form: `exitLaw T k` is the expectation of `k m bs acc`, where `m` is
the number of exiting lineages, `bs` the lineages and `acc` the clusters formed below. The two
daughter populations evolve independently, and their lineages enter the ancestral population
together.

articles.title: No anomalous unrooted quartets, balanced species tree
articles.statement:
**No anomalous unrooted quartets, balanced species tree** (Allman, Degnan & Rhodes 2011):
on `((0, 1), (2, 3))` the unrooted gene quartet matches `01 | 23` with probability
`1 - (2/3) e^{-(y₁ + y₂)}`, where `y₁ + y₂` is the internal edge of the unrooted species
quartet.

articles.title: Probability of quartet split 02|13 on the balanced tree
articles.statement:
On the balanced species tree the discordant unrooted gene quartet `02 | 13` has
probability `(1/3) e^{-(y₁ + y₂)}`.

articles.title: Probability of quartet split 03|12 on the balanced tree
articles.statement:
On the balanced species tree the discordant unrooted gene quartet `03 | 12` has
probability `(1/3) e^{-(y₁ + y₂)}`.

articles.title: Probability of the gene tree ((A, B), (C, D)) on the caterpillar
articles.statement:
The symmetric gene tree `((A, B), (C, D))` on the caterpillar species tree has probability
`h(x, y)` (Degnan & Rosenberg 2006, eq. (3)).

articles.title: Probability of the gene tree ((A, C), (B, D)) on the caterpillar
articles.statement:
The symmetric gene tree `((A, C), (B, D))` on the caterpillar species tree has probability
`g(x, y)` (Degnan & Rosenberg 2006, eq. (2)).

articles.title: Probability of the gene tree ((A, D), (B, C)) on the caterpillar
articles.statement:
The symmetric gene tree `((A, D), (B, C))` on the caterpillar species tree has probability
`g(x, y)`, the same as `((A, C), (B, D))` (Degnan & Rosenberg 2006).

articles.title: The matching gene tree
articles.statement:
**The matching gene tree** on the caterpillar species tree has probability `f(x, y)`
(Degnan & Rosenberg 2006, eq. (1)). An identity for all real `x, y`.

articles.title: No anomalous unrooted quartets, caterpillar species tree
articles.statement:
**No anomalous unrooted quartets, caterpillar species tree** (Allman, Degnan & Rhodes 2011):
the unrooted gene quartet matches the species quartet `01 | 23` with probability
`1 - (2/3) e^{-y}`, where `y` is the length of the internal edge of the unrooted species
quartet (the shallower internal branch).

articles.title: Probability of quartet split 02|13 on the caterpillar tree
articles.statement:
On the caterpillar species tree the discordant unrooted gene quartet `02 | 13` has
probability `(1/3) e^{-y}`.

articles.title: Probability of quartet split 03|12 on the caterpillar tree
articles.statement:
On the caterpillar species tree the discordant unrooted gene quartet `03 | 12` has
probability `(1/3) e^{-y}`.

articles.title: Total gene-tree probability is one
articles.statement: An event containing every gene tree has weight one, for every species tree.

articles.title: Gene-tree probabilities are at most one
articles.statement:
On a species tree with nonnegative branch lengths, every gene-tree probability is at most
one.

articles.title: Root branch length does not affect gene-tree probabilities
articles.statement: The branch length stored at the root of a species tree does not affect the gene tree.

articles.title: Gene-tree probabilities are nonnegative
articles.statement:
**Gene-tree probabilities are nonnegative** on species trees with nonnegative branch
lengths. (For a negative branch length they need not be.)

articles.title: Additivity
articles.statement:
The probabilities of two disjoint events of gene trees add up. With
`geneTreeProb_nonneg` and `geneTreeProb_true`, `geneTreeProb T` is a probability law when
`T.NonnegLengths`.

articles.title: Probability of the discordant three-species gene tree with cherry $\{0, 2\}$
articles.statement:
With one lineage per species and internal branch length $t$, the gene tree of the species tree
$((0, 1), 2)$ whose cherry is $\{0, 2\}$ has probability $\frac{1}{3} e^{-t}$. (An identity for every
real $t$; branch lengths are $t \ge 0$.)

articles.title: Probability of the discordant three-species gene tree with cherry $\{1, 2\}$
articles.statement:
With one lineage per species and internal branch length $t$, the gene tree of the species tree
$((0, 1), 2)$ whose cherry is $\{1, 2\}$ has probability $\frac{1}{3} e^{-t}$. (An identity for every
real $t$; branch lengths are $t \ge 0$.)

articles.title: Three-species concordance
articles.statement:
**Three-species concordance** (Hudson 1983; Pamilo & Nei 1988): with one lineage per
species and internal branch length `t`, the gene tree matches the species tree with
probability `1 - (2/3) e^{-t}`. (An identity for every real `t`; branch lengths are `t ≥ 0`.)

articles.title: Normalization
articles.statement:
For every species tree, the event "any gene tree" has weight one (an
identity for every real branch length). With `geneTreeProb_nonneg` and `geneTreeProb_or` this
makes `geneTreeProb T` a probability law when `T.NonnegLengths`.

articles.title: The multispecies coalescent
articles.statement:
**The multispecies coalescent** (Pamilo & Nei 1988; Degnan & Salter 2005), one lineage
sampled per species: the probability that the gene tree, given by its set of clusters, lies in
the event `E`. Below the root, each branch population runs Kingman's coalescent for the
branch length (`branchStep`); in the root population all remaining lineages coalesce by
random joining. The definition accepts any real branch lengths; it is a probability law on
species trees with nonnegative branch lengths (`geneTreeProb_nonneg`, `geneTreeProb_or`,
`geneTreeProb_true`), and only a signed weight otherwise (with internal branch `-1`, the
matching three-species gene tree gets `1 - (2/3) e < 0`).

articles.title: Rational-valued expectation under random joining
articles.statement:
`integral_randomJoining` for a rational-valued function, with a rational result (used to
evaluate random-joining probabilities by computation).

articles.title: Expectation under random joining as an average over histories
articles.statement:
An expectation under random joining is the average over the `∏_{k=2}^m C(k, 2)` ranked
histories.

articles.title: Balanced gene tree on four genes
articles.statement: `G` is one of the three balanced (symmetric) gene trees on four genes.

articles.title: Clade of a ranked history
articles.statement:
The set `S` of sampled genes is a **clade** of the ranked history `h`: it is a block of one
of the ancestral partitions of `h`, i.e. the set of descendants of some lineage.

articles.title: Merging lineages from singletons gives the ancestral blocks
articles.statement: Starting from the singletons, `mergeAlong` is `blocksAfter`.

articles.title: Lineages after the first coalescence events of a ranked history
articles.statement:
The lineages after the first `t` coalescence events of the ranked history `h` (of `m`
lineages), starting from the lineages `bs`, each given as the set of sampled genes it is
ancestral to. Events follow the encoding of `RankedHistory`: the pair `{a, b}` with `a < b`
merges into position `a`, and position `b` is removed (`mergeBlocks`). With the singletons as
starting lineages this is `blocksAfter` (`mergeAlong_singletons`).

articles.title: Species tree with nonnegative branch lengths
articles.statement:
Every branch length of the species tree, including the unused one stored at the root, is
nonnegative. On such trees `geneTreeProb` is a probability law; for a negative length it is
only a signed weight.

articles.title: Clade probability under random joining for at most five genes
articles.statement: The case `m ≤ 5` of `randomJoining_isClade`.

articles.title: Clade probability
articles.statement:
**Clade probability** (Rosenberg 2003): under random joining, a fixed set of `k` among `m`
genes, `1 ≤ k < m`, is a clade with probability `2m / (k (k + 1) C(m, k))`.

articles.title: Random-joining probability as a fraction of ranked histories
articles.statement: The probability of an event under random joining is the fraction of ranked histories in it.

articles.title: Topology of a species tree
articles.statement: The topology of a species tree, forgetting branch lengths, as a planar rooted binary tree.

articles.title: Rooted binary species tree with branch lengths
articles.statement:
A rooted binary **species tree** on the species `Fin n` with branch lengths: `leaf i` is
species `i`, and `node l r t` is the ancestral species of the species below `l` and `r`, where
`t` is the length, in coalescent units (`2N` generations), of the branch above the node, i.e.
the time during which the ancestral population of `l` and `r` exists before it merges with a
sister population. The length stored at the root node is not used: the root population lasts
until all lineages have coalesced. Leaf branch lengths are not recorded, because one gene
lineage is sampled per species and a single lineage cannot coalesce. A species tree on the
species `Fin n` labels each species by exactly one leaf; the type does not enforce this, and
the theorems below are about concrete trees with this property. The type accepts any real
branch length; the probabilistic statements assume nonnegative lengths (`NonnegLengths`).

articles.title: The species quartet maximizes quartet support
articles.statement:
**The species quartet maximizes quartet support** (Allman, Degnan & Rhodes 2011; Mirarab
et al. 2014): for a positive internal edge, the unrooted gene quartet matching the species
quartet is strictly the most probable of the three, on both four-species shapes. Since the
expected quartet support of a candidate four-species tree (one quartet) is the probability
of its quartet, the species tree maximizes it.

articles.title: Tavaré's probabilities sum to one
articles.statement:
From `m ≥ 1` lineages, the number of ancestors at
time `t` is one of `1, …, m`. (The rows of `exp (t • G)` restricted to the states `≥ 1` sum to
one because `G` kills the indicator of `{1, …, n}`; an identity for every real `t`.)

articles.title: Tavaré's probabilities are nonnegative
articles.statement:
**Tavaré's probabilities are nonnegative** for `t ≥ 0`: `exp (t • G)` is the entrywise limit
of powers of the Wright–Fisher transition matrix (`tendsto_wfLineageMatrix_pow_floor`), whose
entries are nonnegative. (For `t < 0` they can be negative or exceed one.)

articles.title: Three lineages have one ancestor at time $t$
articles.statement:
Three lineages have one ancestor at time `t` with probability
`1 - (3/2) e^{-t} + (1/2) e^{-3t}`.

articles.title: Three lineages remain distinct with probability $e^{-3t}$
articles.statement: Three lineages are still distinct after time `t` with probability `e^{-3t}`.

articles.title: Three lineages have two ancestors at time $t$
articles.statement: Three lineages have two ancestors at time `t` with probability `(3/2)(e^{-t} - e^{-3t})`.

articles.title: Two lineages coalesce with probability $1 - e^{-t}$
articles.statement: Two lineages have coalesced within time `t` with probability `1 - e^{-t}`.

articles.title: Two lineages remain distinct with probability $e^{-t}$
articles.statement: Two lineages are still distinct after time `t` with probability `e^{-t}`.

articles.title: Species below a node of a species tree
articles.statement: The species below a node.

articles.title: Anomaly-zone boundary blows up for short deep branches
articles.statement:
`a(x) → ∞` as `x → 0⁺` (Degnan & Rosenberg 2006): very short deep branches produce an
anomalous gene tree however long the shallower branch is.

articles.title: Wright–Fisher limit of the no-coalescence probability
articles.statement:
The three-species probabilities come from the Wright–Fisher model: in a population of `M`
gene copies, the lineages of species `0` and `1` have distinct parents in each of the
`⌊t M⌋` generations of the internal branch (`t ≥ 0` coalescent units) with probability
`noCoalProb M 2 ^ ⌊t M⌋`, which tends to `tavareProb 2 2 t = e^{-t}`, the weight of the case
in which three lineages reach the root population.

articles.title: No anomalous gene trees for three species
articles.statement:
**No anomalous gene trees for three species** (Degnan & Rosenberg 2006): for a positive
internal branch, each discordant gene tree is strictly less probable than the matching one.

articles.title: Three-gene tree with a given cherry
articles.statement: The gene tree on three genes with cherry `c` (a pair of genes), as a set of clusters.

articles.title: Three-species tree ((0, 1), 2)
articles.statement: The three-species tree `((0, 1), 2)` with internal branch length `t`.

articles.title: Kingman's formula intertwines the block-counting generator with the partition rate matrix
articles.statement:
**Kingman's formula intertwines the block-counting generator with the partition rate
matrix**: `G * Λ = Λ * Q`. This is the backward equation `sum_kingmanProb_isMerge` in matrix
form.

articles.title: Mergers
articles.statement:
A partition with `k` blocks has exactly `k.choose 2` partitions that arise
from it by merging two blocks.

articles.title: Partition coalescent transition matrix is row-stochastic
articles.statement: For `t ≥ 0` the transition matrix `exp (t • partitionRate n)` is row-stochastic.

articles.title: Partition obtained by merging two blocks
articles.statement:
`π'` arises from `π` by merging two blocks: `π` refines `π'` and has exactly one more
block (so exactly two blocks of `π` lie in one block of `π'`, and the others are blocks of
`π'`).

articles.title: Partition rate matrix is a rate matrix
articles.statement:
The partition rate matrix is a rate matrix: off-diagonal entries are `0` or `1`, and each
row sums to `0` (`sum_partitionRate`).

articles.title: Exchangeability
articles.statement:
**Exchangeability** of the jump chain: for `m < n`, relabeling the sample does not change
the probability of a partition after `m` coalescences.

articles.title: Kingman's formula
articles.statement:
**Kingman's formula** (Kingman 1982; Durrett 2008, ch. 1). For `m < n`, after `m`
coalescences the jump chain started from singletons is at a partition `π` with probability
`kingmanProb n π = (n - k)! k! (k - 1)! ∏_{B ∈ π} |B|! / (n! (n - 1)!)` if `π` has `k = n - m`
blocks, and `0` otherwise. (For `m ≥ n - 1` the chain has been absorbed at the one-block
partition.)

articles.title: Law of Kingman's jump chain after m jumps
articles.statement:
The law of the jump chain after `m` jumps, started from the partition into singletons:
`jumpLaw n m π` is the probability that the partition after `m` coalescences is `π`.

articles.title: Kingman's jump-chain matrix is row-stochastic
articles.statement: The jump-chain transition matrix is row-stochastic.

articles.title: Jump chain of Kingman's coalescent
articles.statement:
The transition matrix of the jump chain of Kingman's coalescent: from a partition with
`k ≥ 2` blocks, move to each of the `k.choose 2` partitions obtained by merging two blocks with
probability `1 / k.choose 2`; a partition with at most one block is absorbing.

articles.title: Last row of Kingman's matrix is the singleton point mass
articles.statement: Row `n` of `kingmanMatrix n` is the point mass at the partition into singletons.

articles.title: Kingman's formula arranged by number of blocks
articles.statement:
Kingman's formula arranged by number of blocks: entry `(k, π)` is `kingmanProb n π` if `π`
has `k` blocks and `0` otherwise. For `1 ≤ k ≤ n`, row `k` is the law of the jump chain after
`n - k` jumps (`jumpLaw_eq`).

articles.title: Kingman's formula at the partition into singletons
articles.statement: Kingman's formula gives probability `1` to the partition into singletons.

articles.title: Kingman's formula is invariant under relabeling
articles.statement:
Relabeling the sample by a permutation (`Finpartition.comap`) preserves Kingman's
formula.

articles.title: Kingman's formula for a partition with k blocks
articles.statement: Kingman's formula for a partition with `k` blocks.

articles.title: Kingman's formula
articles.statement:
The probability `(n - k)! k! (k - 1)! ∏_{B ∈ π} |B|! / (n! (n - 1)!)`
of a partition `π` with `k` blocks of a sample of size `n` (meaningful for `1 ≤ k ≤ n`; for
the empty sample it gives `1` to the empty partition).

articles.title: Number of blocks of a sample partition
articles.statement:
The number of blocks of a partition of a sample of `n`, as an element of `Fin (n + 1)` (a
state of the block-counting process).

articles.title: Lumpability of restriction
articles.statement:
**Lumpability of restriction** (Kingman 1982): restricting to the first `n` genes
intertwines the rate matrices of the `(n + 1)`- and `n`-coalescents.

articles.title: Rate matrix of Kingman's partition-valued coalescent
articles.statement:
The rate matrix of Kingman's partition-valued coalescent: each pair of blocks merges at
rate `1`, so a partition with `k` blocks is left at total rate `k.choose 2` (time in units of
`2N` generations).

articles.title: Path probability of the Kingman coalescent jump chain
articles.statement:
The probability that the jump chain of Kingman's `n`-coalescent, started from the partition
into singletons, follows the list of partitions `l`: `0` unless `l` starts at the partition
into singletons, and otherwise the product of the one-step transition probabilities
`jumpMatrix n` along `l`. The empty list has probability `0`.

articles.title: Restriction matrix on sample partitions
articles.statement: The restriction map as a `0/1` matrix: entry `(π, ρ)` is `1` iff `π.comap Fin.castSucc = ρ`.

articles.title: Set partitions of a labeled sample
articles.statement: The set partitions of a sample of `n` labeled genes `{0, …, n - 1}`.

articles.title: Jump-chain law sums to one
articles.statement:
The jump chain's law after `m` jumps sums to one (its entries are nonnegative by
`jumpMatrix_mem_rowStochastic`).

articles.title: Backward equation of Kingman's formula
articles.statement:
For a partition `π'` with `k` blocks,
`1 ≤ k < n`, the Kingman probabilities of the partitions merging to `π'` sum to
`(k + 1).choose 2` times the Kingman probability of `π'`.

articles.title: Kingman's formula is a probability distribution
articles.statement:
**Kingman's formula is a probability distribution** on the partitions with `k` blocks, for
`1 ≤ k ≤ n`. Equivalently, `∑_{π, k blocks} ∏_{B ∈ π} |B|! = n! (n - 1)! / ((n - k)! k! (k - 1)!)`,
the Lah number `L(n, k)`.

articles.title: Rows of the partition rate matrix sum to zero
articles.statement:
Each row of the partition rate matrix sums to `0`: a partition with `k` blocks has
`k.choose 2` mergers (`card_isMerge`), each at rate `1`.

articles.title: Consistency of the jump chains
articles.statement:
**Consistency of the jump chains** (Kingman 1982): for `n ≥ 1`, restricting each
partition of a path of the `(n + 1)`-jump chain (a list of `n + 1` partitions) to the first `n`
genes and deleting consecutive repetitions gives a list of `n` partitions of `Fin n` distributed
as the path of the `n`-jump chain.

## Sources

- Kingman (1982); Durrett (2008), ch. 1.

articles.title: Consistency
articles.statement:
**Consistency** (Kingman 1982): the time-`t` law of the restriction of the
`(n + 1)`-coalescent to the first `n` genes is the time-`t` law of the `n`-coalescent.

articles.title: Time-t marginal sums to one
articles.statement:
The time-`t` marginal sums to one over all partitions: `∑_π timeLaw n t π = 1` (for every
real `t`, since the rows of the rate matrix sum to `0`).

articles.title: Exchangeability
articles.statement: **Exchangeability** of the time-`t` marginal.

articles.title: Time-t marginal as a continuous-time chain transition
articles.statement:
`timeLaw` is a row of the transition function `P t = exp (t • partitionRate n)` of the
continuous-time chain with rate matrix `partitionRate n`.

articles.title: Time-t marginal via Tavaré's formula
articles.statement:
The time-`t` marginal with Tavaré's closed form for the block-counting factor: for a
partition `π` of a sample of `n` (so `π` has at least one block when `n ≥ 1`),
`P(Π_t = π) = tavareProb n k t · kingmanProb n π` with `k = #π.parts`.

articles.title: The time-`t` marginal of the partition-valued coalescent
articles.statement:
**The time-`t` marginal of the partition-valued coalescent** (Kingman 1982): for
every real `t`, the probability of a partition `π` with `k` blocks is the probability that the
block-counting process goes from `n` to `k` lineages in time `t`, times Kingman's formula.

articles.title: Nonnegativity of the time-t marginal
articles.statement:
For `t ≥ 0` the time-`t` marginal is nonnegative; with `sum_timeLaw` it is a probability
distribution on the partitions of the sample.

articles.title: Time-t marginal of Kingman's coalescent
articles.statement:
The time-`t` marginal of Kingman's `n`-coalescent started from singletons:
`timeLaw n t π = exp (t • partitionRate n) ⊥ π` is the probability that the ancestral partition
of the sample at time `t ≥ 0` (in units of `2N` generations) is `π`. The matrix exponential is
defined for every real `t`; the identities below hold for every real `t`.

articles.title: Splitting identity
articles.statement:
Summing `∏_{B ∈ π} |B|!` over the partitions `π` that merge to
`π'` gives `(n - #π'.parts) / 2 · ∏_{B ∈ π'} |B|!`: a block of size `b` has
`(2^b - 2) / 2` splits into two blocks, and `∑_{∅ ≠ A ⊊ B} |A|! |B \ A|! = (b - 1) b!`.

articles.title: Lineage blocks after the first coalescence events
articles.statement:
The lineages (as blocks of sampled genes, indexed by lineage label) after the first `t`
coalescence events of a history, starting from the singletons `{0}, …, {n - 1}`.

articles.title: Ancestral partitions along a history, indexed by lineage label
articles.statement:
The ancestral partitions of the sample along a history, as lists of blocks indexed by
lineage label; entry `t` (for `t < n`) is the partition after `t` coalescence events.

articles.title: Number of pairs of lineages
articles.statement: The number of pairs of `k` lineages is `k.choose 2`.

articles.title: Number of ranked labeled histories
articles.statement:
`#histories * 2^{n-1} = n! (n - 1)!`, i.e. there are
`n! (n - 1)! / 2^{n-1}` ranked labeled histories of `n` labeled genes (Edwards 1970).

articles.title: Number of ranked labeled histories
Unordered pairs of lineages
articles.statement: The unordered pairs of lineages when there are `k` lineages labeled `0, …, k - 1`.

articles.title: Merging two lineage blocks
articles.statement:
Merge the lineages (blocks of sampled genes) at positions `a < b` of a list of blocks: the
merged block replaces position `a`, and position `b` is removed.

articles.title: Ancestral partitions along a history as sets of blocks
articles.statement:
The ancestral partitions of the sample along a history, as sets of blocks (forgetting the
lineage labels): the ranked labeled history in the sense of Edwards (1970).

articles.title: Product of pair counts times a power of two is $n!(n-1)!$
Reindexing the product of pair counts
articles.statement: Reindexing: `∏_{i < n - 1} C(n - i, 2) = ∏_{k=2}^n C(k, 2)`.

articles.title: Every ranked history is equally likely under random joining
articles.statement: Under random joining each history has probability `∏_{k=2}^n C(k, 2)⁻¹`.

articles.title: Each ranked labeled history has probability `2^{n-1} / (n! (n - 1)!)`
articles.statement:
**Each ranked labeled history has probability `2^{n-1} / (n! (n - 1)!)`** under random
joining (Edwards 1970; Tajima 1983).

articles.title: Random joining
articles.statement:
**Random joining** (Edwards 1970; Kingman 1982): the pair merging at each step is uniform
among the current `(n - i).choose 2` pairs and independent of the earlier steps. Kingman (1982)
shows that this is the law of the tree topology of the coalescent.

articles.title: Ranked labeled history
articles.statement:
A **ranked labeled history** of `n` labeled genes, encoded by its coalescence events: at
step `i < n - 1` there are `n - i` lineages and the step records the pair that merges (the
merged lineage takes the smaller label; the others keep their relative order).

articles.title: Covariance of `π` and `S`
articles.statement:
`Cov(π, S) = θ + (n + 2) θ² / (2 n)` for `n ≥ 2`, if
`τ s ~ Exp(1)`, `E[τ s L] = 2 a₁ + (n + 2) / n` (`L` the total branch length),
`E[D s | m] = θ τ s`, `E[S | m] = (θ / 2) L` and `E[D s S | m] = (θ² / 2) τ s L + θ τ s` (the
path of each pair lies in the tree). This is the covariance behind Tajima's (1989) `c₁, c₂`.

articles.title: Expected pairwise differences
articles.statement:
**Expected pairwise differences** (Tajima 1983): if, for each pair `s` of sampled genes,
the coalescence time `τ s` of the pair is exponential with rate `1` and the number `D s` of
differences has conditional mean `θ τ s` given the genealogy σ-algebra `m` (mutations at rate
`θ / 2` on each of the two branches of length `τ s`), then `E π = θ`.

articles.title: Pair coalescence time against the total branch length
articles.statement:
If the coalescence time of a
pair is `τ = ∑_{k=2}^n χ k T k`, where `χ k` indicates that the pair is still in two distinct
lineages while there are `k` lineages, and the topology is independent of the holding times in
the sense `E[χ k T k T k'] = p k E[T k T k']` with `p k = pairSeparateProb n k`, then
`E[τ L] = 2 a₁ + (n + 2) / n` for `n ≥ 2`. Only this factorization is used, so `χ k` need not
be an indicator in the statement.

articles.title: Tajima's numerator has mean zero
articles.statement:
**Tajima's numerator has mean zero** (Tajima 1989): under the hypotheses of
`integral_meanPairDiff` and Watterson's (`E[S | m] = (θ/2) L`),
`E[π - S / a₁] = 0` for a sample of size `n ≥ 2`.

articles.title: Unbiased estimator of Tajima's variance term
articles.statement:
**Unbiased estimator of Tajima's variance term** (Tajima 1989): with `S` as in
`variance_segSites`, `E[e₁ S + e₂ S (S - 1)] = c₁ θ + c₂ θ²` for `n ≥ 2`. (By Tajima's
analysis `c₁ θ + c₂ θ²` is `Var(π - S / a₁)`.)

articles.title: Mean number of pairwise differences
articles.statement:
The mean number of pairwise differences `π = C(n, 2)⁻¹ ∑_{i<j} D_{ij}` (Tajima 1983), where
`D s` is the number of sites at which the two sequences of the pair `s` differ.

articles.title: Probability that a pair lies in separate lineages
articles.statement:
The probability `(k - 1) (n + 1) / ((n - 1) (k + 1))` that a given pair of a sample of
size `n` is still in two distinct lineages while the genealogy has `k` lineages
(`2 ≤ k ≤ n`, `n ≥ 2`; at `n = 1` the definition divides by zero and returns `0`).

articles.title: Pairs of genes in a sample
articles.statement: The pairs of genes in a sample of size `n`.

articles.title: Sum of pair-separation probabilities over squared pair counts
Mean coalescence time of a pair is one
articles.statement: `∑_{k=2}^n p_k / C(k, 2) = 1`: the mean coalescence time of a pair is `1`.

articles.title: Counting sample pairs by overlap with a given pair
articles.statement:
Among the pairs of a sample of size `n`, one equals a given pair `s`, `2 (n - 2)` share
exactly one gene with it and `C(n - 2, 2)` are disjoint from it.

articles.title: Tajima's $a_1$ is a harmonic number
articles.statement: `a₁` is the harmonic number `H_{n-1}`.

articles.title: Tajima's constant $a_1$
Tajima's constant $a_2$
Tajima's constant $b_1$
Tajima's constant $b_2$
Tajima's constant $c_1$
articles.statement: `c₁ = b₁ - 1/a₁` (Tajima 1989), for `n ≥ 2`.

articles.title: Tajima's constant $c_2$
articles.statement: `c₂ = b₂ - (n + 2)/(a₁ n) + a₂/a₁²` (Tajima 1989), for `n ≥ 2`.

articles.title: Tajima's constant $e_1$
articles.statement: `e₁ = c₁ / a₁` (Tajima 1989), for `n ≥ 2`.

articles.title: Tajima's constant $e_2$
articles.statement: `e₂ = c₂ / (a₁² + a₂)` (Tajima 1989), for `n ≥ 2`.

articles.title: Variance of the mean number of pairwise differences
articles.statement:
**Variance of the mean number of pairwise differences** (Tajima 1983):
`Var π = b₁ θ + b₂ θ²` for a sample of size `n ≥ 2`, under the conditional-moment model of the
module docstring: `τ s ~ Exp(1)`, `E[τ s τ t] = 4/3` (one shared gene), `11/9` (disjoint
pairs); the shared path lengths `ℓ`; `E[D s | m] = θ τ s` and
`E[D s D t | m] = θ² τ s τ t + (θ / 2) ℓ s t`.

articles.title: Variance of the number of segregating sites
articles.statement:
**Variance of the number of segregating sites** (Watterson 1975;
Tajima 1989): if, given the genealogy σ-algebra `m`, the number `S` of
segregating sites has conditional mean and conditional variance `(θ/2) L` (as for a Poisson
count with mean `θ L / 2`), then `Var S = θ a₁ + θ² a₂`.

articles.title: Tajima's variance identity
articles.statement:
**Tajima's variance identity** (Tajima 1989): `Var(π - S / a₁) = c₁ θ + c₂ θ²` for a
sample of size `n ≥ 2`, under the hypotheses of `variance_meanPairDiff`,
`covariance_meanPairDiff_segSites` and `variance_segSites`.

articles.title: Variance of the total branch length
articles.statement:
**Variance of the total branch length** (Watterson 1975):
`Var L = ∑_{k=2}^n k² Var T_k = 4 ∑_{j=1}^{n-1} 1/j²` (uses independence of the holding
times).

articles.title: Closed form of the first-coalescence times
articles.statement:
For a history with `K ≥ 1` pieces and
`m ≥ 2`, writing `a = C(m,2)` and `R = cumRate h.sizeFn`,
`a c_m = size 0 + ∑_{j=1}^{K-1} (size j - size (j-1)) exp(-a R(start j))`. In particular the
integral defining `c_m` converges.

articles.title: Dual cumulative rate inverts the cumulative rate
articles.statement: The dual cumulative rate inverts the cumulative rate.

articles.title: Cumulative rate is affine on each piece
articles.statement:
On piece `j` (including its right end), `1 / sizeFn` is integrable on `[0, s]` and the
cumulative rate is affine: `R(s) = R(start j) + (s - start j) / size j`.

articles.title: Coalescent-time breakpoints are strictly increasing
articles.statement: The coalescent-time breakpoints `R(start j)` are strictly increasing.

articles.title: Cumulative rate is strictly increasing
articles.statement: The cumulative rate is strictly increasing on `[0, ∞)`.

articles.title: Cumulative coalescence intensity
articles.statement:
The cumulative coalescence intensity `R(s) = ∫_0^s 1/η` of a relative population-size
function `η` (pairs coalesce at rate `1/η(s)` at time `s` before the present). Meaningful for
positive `η` with `1/η` locally integrable.

articles.title: Dual history in coalescent time
articles.statement:
The dual history in coalescent time: piece `j` starts at `R(start j)` and has size
`1 / size j`.

articles.title: The expected SFS determines the mean holding times
articles.statement:
If two vectors of mean holding
times give the same expected SFS for some `θ ≠ 0`, they agree at every `k = 2, …, n`. This is
a direct consequence of `sfsKernel_eq_zero_of_lt` and `sfsKernel_diag_pos` (the kernel is
triangular with nonzero diagonal); it is recorded here as an observation, not as a cited
theorem.

articles.title: Size function lies between the extreme piece sizes
articles.statement: On `[0, ∞)` the size function lies between the smallest and the largest piece size.

articles.title: Non-identifiability from a bounded sample size
articles.statement:
For every `n` there are two measurable
population-size functions, bounded between positive constants and different on a set of
positive measure in `[0, ∞)`, with the same `c_m` for `2 ≤ m ≤ n` (two `(n + 2)`-piece
histories from `PiecewiseHistory.exists_ne_firstCoalMean_eq_of_lt`, extended to `s < 0` by
their size at `0`). This is the finite-sample shape of the statement of Myers, Fefferman &
Patterson (2008); their theorem gives one pair of functions with equal `c_m` for **every** `m`.

articles.title: Non-identifiability of general histories
articles.statement:
**Non-identifiability of general histories** (Myers, Fefferman & Patterson 2008): there
are two measurable population-size functions, bounded between positive constants, that differ
on a set of positive Lebesgue measure in `[0, ∞)` and have the same expected first-coalescence
time `c_m` for every `m ≥ 2` (hence the same expected SFS for every sample size).

## Sources

- Myers, Fefferman & Patterson (2008).

articles.title: Tightness of `n ≥ 2K`
articles.statement:
**Tightness of `n ≥ 2K`** (Bhaskar & Song 2014, Corollary 7): for every `K ≥ 2` there are
two piecewise-constant histories with `K` pieces whose sizes differ at some time `s ≥ 0` but
whose first-coalescence times `c_m` agree for `2 ≤ m ≤ 2K - 1`; so
`sizeFn_eq_of_firstCoalMean_eq` fails for `n = 2K - 1`. The construction is explicit: with
`z = 2^{-C(m,2)}`, the two histories have coalescent-time breakpoints `(2j - 1) log 2` and
`2j log 2`, so `C(m,2) (c_m - c'_m)` is a polynomial of degree `2K - 2` in `z`; its
coefficients are those of `∏_{m=2}^{2K-1} (X - 2^{-C(m,2)})`, which vanishes at the `2K - 2`
points and has a nonzero constant term (the sizes at time `0` differ).

articles.title: Distinct two-piece histories with equal first-coalescence times
articles.statement: The two-piece case of `exists_ne_firstCoalMean_eq_of_lt`.

articles.title: Every nonnegative time lies in some piece
articles.statement: Every time `s ≥ 0` lies in some piece.

articles.title: Size function is locally constant to the right
articles.statement: The size function is constant on an interval to the right of every `s ≥ 0`.

articles.title: Fay and Wu's H statistic
articles.statement: Fay & Wu's `H = θ_π - θ_H` (Fay & Wu 2000).

articles.title: First-coalescence times depend only on sizes at nonnegative times
articles.statement: Only the values on `[0, ∞)` enter the first-coalescence times.

articles.title: Expected time to the first coalescence
articles.statement:
The expected time to the first coalescence among `m` lineages,
`c_m = ∫_0^∞ exp(-C(m,2) R(s)) ds`, in a population of relative size `η`
(Bhaskar & Song's `E[T_{m,m}]`). When the integrand is not integrable (for example `η ≡ 0`),
this is Lean's junk value `0`; for piecewise-constant histories it is integrable
(`choose_two_mul_firstCoalMean`).

articles.title: Numerator of Fu and Li's D
articles.statement:
The numerator `S - a₁ ξ₁` of Fu & Li's `D` with an outgroup, where `S = ∑_i ξ_i` and the
external-branch mutations are the derived singletons `ξ₁` (Fu & Li 1993).

articles.title: Numerator of Fu and Li's F
articles.statement:
The numerator `θ_π - ξ₁` of Fu & Li's `F` with an outgroup (Fu & Li 1993), with `θ_π` in
its SFS form.

articles.title: Fay and Wu's H has mean zero at constant size
articles.statement: Fay & Wu's `H` has mean zero under the constant-size spectrum (`n ≥ 2`).

articles.title: Numerator of Fu and Li's D has mean zero at constant size
articles.statement:
The numerator of Fu & Li's `D` has mean zero under the constant-size spectrum
(`n ≥ 2`).

articles.title: Numerator of Fu and Li's F has mean zero at constant size
articles.statement:
The numerator of Fu & Li's `F` has mean zero under the constant-size spectrum
(`n ≥ 2`).

articles.title: Expected SFS under a variable population size
articles.statement:
**Expected SFS under a variable population size** (Griffiths & Tavaré 1998; Polanski &
Kimmel 2003). Let the genealogy of a sample of `n` copies consist of holding times `T k`
(integrable for `2 ≤ k ≤ n`, otherwise arbitrary) and an independent block-size history `τ`
with the random-joining law. If, given the genealogy, the count `ξ i` is integrable with
conditional mean `(θ / 2) L_i`, then `E ξ_i = (θ / 2) ∑_k k C(n-i-1,k-2)/C(n-1,k-1) E T_k`
for `1 ≤ i ≤ n - 1`. Independence of the holding times and the topology holds for the
time-changed Kingman coalescent of any deterministic population-size history (a standard property of that model; here it is a hypothesis).

articles.title: Achaz's estimator is unbiased under Kingman's coalescent
articles.statement:
Achaz's unbiasedness under Kingman's coalescent, with the hypotheses of
`SiteFrequencySpectrum.integral_sfs`.

articles.title: Achaz's unbiasedness
articles.statement:
**Achaz's unbiasedness** (Achaz 2009): if `E ξ_i = θ / i` for `1 ≤ i ≤ n - 1` (the
constant-size spectrum, `SiteFrequencySpectrum.integral_sfs`), every weighted estimator with
`∑_i ω_i = 1` has mean `θ`.

articles.title: Measurability of the piecewise size function
articles.statement: The size function is measurable.

articles.title: Piecewise-constant population-size history
articles.statement:
A **piecewise-constant population-size history with `K` pieces**: piece `j < K` starts at
time `start j` (backward from the present, `start 0 = 0`, strictly increasing) and has
relative size `size j > 0`; the last piece extends to infinity. Adjacent pieces may have equal
sizes, so this also covers histories with fewer than `K` distinct pieces. Values at indices
`j ≥ K` are unused. The case `K = 0` is degenerate (its size function is `0`); the theorems
about `c_m` assume `0 < K` where it matters.

articles.title: Positivity of the Griffiths–Tavaré kernel on the diagonal
articles.statement: The kernel entry at `k = n - i + 1` is `(n - i + 1) / C(n-1, i-1) > 0`.

articles.title: Griffiths–Tavaré kernel vanishes beyond the diagonal
articles.statement:
The kernel row `i` vanishes beyond `k = n - i + 1`: a branch subtending `i` copies cannot
exist while more than `n - i + 1` lineages remain.

articles.title: Griffiths–Tavaré kernel
articles.statement:
The **Griffiths–Tavaré kernel** `k C(n-i-1, k-2) / C(n-1, k-1)`: the expected number of
branches subtending exactly `i` of the `n` sample copies while `k` lineages remain
(`SiteFrequencySpectrum.joinStep_iterate_count`). Meaningful for `1 ≤ i < n`, `2 ≤ k ≤ n`;
outside that range the natural-number subtractions give junk values.

articles.title: Size function is the inverse of the dual size in coalescent time
articles.statement:
The size at time `s` is the inverse of the dual history's size at coalescent time
`R(s)`.

articles.title: Bhaskar–Song identifiability
articles.statement:
**Bhaskar–Song identifiability** (Bhaskar & Song 2014, Corollary 7, "determined" half,
stated for the first-coalescence times): two piecewise-constant histories with `K` pieces whose
expected first-coalescence times `c_m` agree for `2 ≤ m ≤ n`, with `n ≥ 2K`, have the same
population size at every time `s ≥ 0`. The proof writes `C(m,2) c_m` as an exponential sum in
`C(m,2)` over at most `2K - 1` rates (`choose_two_mul_firstCoalMean`), identifies the
coefficients with `Real.eq_zero_of_sum_mul_exp_eq_zero`, recovers the size as a function of
coalescent time (the `dual` history) and inverts `R` (`cumRate_dual_cumRate`).

articles.title: Size function on a piece equals the piece size
articles.statement: On piece `j` the size function equals `size j`.

articles.title: Positivity of the piecewise size function
articles.statement: The size function is positive on `[0, ∞)`.

articles.title: Size function of a piecewise-constant history
articles.statement:
The population-size function of a piecewise-constant history: at time `s ≥ 0` it is the
size of the piece `j` with `start j ≤ s < start (j + 1)` (the last piece has no end). Equal to
`0` for `s < 0` (junk; only `s ≥ 0` is meaningful).

articles.title: Monotonicity of piece start times
articles.statement: The start times are monotone on the pieces.

articles.title: Nonnegativity of piece start times
articles.statement: Every piece starts at a nonnegative time.

articles.title: Fay and Wu's $\theta_H$
articles.statement: Fay & Wu's `θ_H = ∑_i i² ξ_i / C(n,2)` (weights `i / C(n,2)`).

articles.title: Tajima's $\theta_\pi$ in site frequency spectrum form
articles.statement: Tajima's `θ_π` in its SFS form `∑_i i (n - i) ξ_i / C(n,2)` (weights `(n - i) / C(n,2)`).

articles.title: Achaz's weighted estimator of $\theta$
articles.statement:
Achaz's weighted estimator `θ_ω = ∑_{i=1}^{n-1} ω_i i ξ_i` (Achaz 2009, with the
weights already normalized).

articles.title: Variable-size spectrum reduces to Fu's $\theta/i$ at constant size
articles.statement:
With the constant-size means `E T_k = 1 / C(k,2)`, the variable-size SFS is Fu's
`θ / i`.

articles.title: Expected site frequency spectrum under variable population size
articles.statement:
The expected SFS entry `(θ / 2) ∑_{k=2}^{n} sfsKernel n i k · t k` of a sample of size
`n` whose mean holding times are `t k = E T_k` (Griffiths & Tavaré 1998, Polanski & Kimmel
2003).

articles.title: The skyline estimates are independent
articles.statement: **The skyline estimates are independent** across intervals.

articles.title: The skyline estimate is unbiased
articles.statement: `E[C(k, 2) T k] = θ k`.

articles.title: Coordinate projections form a skyline model
articles.statement:
The coordinate projections of `skylinePiMeasure n θ` form a skyline model whenever the
`θ k` are positive; in particular `SkylineTimes` is inhabited.

articles.title: Classic skyline estimate of population size
articles.statement: The classic skyline estimate `θ̂_k = C(k, 2) w_k` for the interval with `k` lineages.

articles.title: Uniqueness of the skyline maximizer
articles.statement:
For `c, w, θ > 0`, `ℓ(θ) = ℓ(c w)` iff
`θ = c w`.

articles.title: The skyline estimate maximizes the interval likelihood
articles.statement:
**The skyline estimate maximizes the interval likelihood** (Pybus, Rambaut & Harvey 2000):
for `c, w, θ > 0`, `ℓ(θ) ≤ ℓ(c w)`.

articles.title: Log-likelihood of one coalescent interval in the skyline model
articles.statement:
The log-likelihood of `θ` for one coalescent interval of length `w` with `c = C(k, 2)`
pairs of lineages: the log-density `log (c / θ) - c w / θ` of `Exp(c / θ)` at `w`.

articles.title: Canonical probability space for the skyline model
articles.statement:
The canonical probability space for the skyline model: the product of the exponential laws
`Exp(C(k, 2) / θ k)`, `2 ≤ k ≤ n`.

articles.title: Coalescent intervals under the classic skyline model
articles.statement:
The coalescent intervals of a sample of `n` genes under the classic skyline model with
piecewise-constant population-size parameter `θ k` while there are `k` lineages: `T k` is
exponential with rate `C(k, 2) / θ k`, independently over `2 ≤ k ≤ n`.

articles.title: Uniqueness of the joint maximizer
articles.statement:
Equality in `sum_skylineLogLik_le` holds iff
`θ i = c i w i` for every interval.

articles.title: The skyline estimates jointly maximize the likelihood
articles.statement:
For positive `c i`, `w i`,
`θ i` over a finite set of intervals, `∑ ℓ_i(θ_i) ≤ ∑ ℓ_i(c_i w_i)`.

articles.title: Variance of the skyline estimate
articles.statement: `Var[C(k, 2) T k] = θ k²`.

articles.title: Mean coalescence time between demes
articles.statement:
The mean coalescence time `T₁ = d + (d - 1) / M` of two lineages in different demes (units of
`2N` generations). Meaningful for `M > 0`; `betweenTime d 0 = d` is a junk value (the true mean
is infinite).

articles.title: Exit rate of a structured-coalescent state
articles.statement: The total rate `qₛ = ∑ₜ q(s, t)` of leaving the state `s`.

articles.title: Mean coalescence times in the finite island model (Strobeck 1987; Slatkin 1991)
articles.statement:
For
`d ≥ 2` demes and `M = 4Nm > 0`, the first-step equations have the unique solution
`T₀ = d`, `T₁ = d + (d - 1) / M`. In particular `T₀` does not depend on the migration rate.

articles.title: First-step equations for mean coalescence time
articles.statement:
The first-step (backward Kolmogorov) equations for the mean time to coalescence:
`h coalesced = 0`, and at each transient state `s`, `∑ₜ q(s, t) (h t - h s) = -1`. (The vector
of mean absorption times of a finite absorbing continuous-time Markov chain satisfies these
equations; this file does not construct the chain.)

articles.title: First-step analysis in jump-chain form
articles.statement:
At each transient state `s` the exit rate is
positive and the mean coalescence time is the mean holding time `1 / qₛ` plus the mean time from
the next state, `h s = 1 / qₛ + ∑ₜ (q(s, t) / qₛ) h t`.

articles.title: Closed-form mean coalescence times in the island model
articles.statement:
The closed-form mean time to coalescence from each state: `T₀`, `T₁`, and `0` once
coalesced. `firstStepEquations_iff` shows it is the unique solution of the first-step
equations.

articles.title: State of two lineages in the island model
articles.statement:
The state of two ancestral lineages in the island model: in the same deme, in different
demes, or coalesced (absorbing).

articles.title: Transition rates of the two-lineage structured coalescent
articles.statement:
The transition rates `q(s, t)` (`s ≠ t`) of the two-lineage structured coalescent in the
finite island model with `d` demes and `M = 4Nm`, time in units of `2N` generations: same deme →
coalesced at rate `1`, same deme → different demes at rate `M`, different demes → same deme at
rate `M / (d - 1)`; all other rates (and the diagonal) are `0`. Meaningful for `d ≥ 2` and
`M ≥ 0`.

articles.title: Slatkin's `F_ST` for the finite island model (Slatkin 1991)
articles.statement:
For `d ≥ 2` demes and
`M = 4Nm > 0`, `F_ST = 1 / (1 + M d² / (d - 1)²)`.

articles.title: Slatkin's F_ST lies strictly between 0 and 1
articles.statement: Slatkin's `F_ST` lies in `(0, 1)` for `d ≥ 2` and `M > 0`.

articles.title: Slatkin's F_ST for the finite island model
articles.statement: Slatkin's (1991) `F_ST = (T̄ - T₀) / T̄` for the finite island model.

articles.title: Sum over the island-model pair states
articles.statement: A sum over the three states.

articles.title: Many demes (Slatkin 1991)
articles.statement:
As the number of demes grows, Slatkin's `F_ST` tends to
Wright's `1 / (1 + M) = 1 / (1 + 4Nm)` for every `M > 0`.

articles.title: Closed form of Slatkin's mean total coalescence time
Positivity of Slatkin's mean total coalescence time
articles.statement: The denominator of Slatkin's `F_ST` is positive: `0 < T̄` for `d ≥ 1` and `M > 0`.

articles.title: Slatkin's mean total coalescence time
articles.statement:
Slatkin's mean coalescence time `T̄ = T₀ / d + (d - 1) T₁ / d` of two genes drawn from two
demes chosen independently and uniformly at random.

articles.title: Mean coalescence time within a deme
articles.statement:
The mean coalescence time `T₀ = d` of two lineages in the same deme (units of `2N`
generations).

articles.title: Two-locus covariance decreases with recombination rate
articles.statement: The covariance decreases with the recombination rate.

articles.title: Coalescence indicator at locus A
articles.statement: Whether locus `A` has found its most recent common ancestor.

articles.title: Coalescence indicator at locus B
articles.statement: Whether locus `B` has found its most recent common ancestor.

articles.title: Covariance of the coalescence times, path form
articles.statement:
**Covariance of the coalescence times, path form** (Hudson 1983; Kaplan & Hudson 1985):
for the two-locus ancestral process started from two linked sequences,
`E (T_A T_B) - E T_A E T_B = (ρ + 18) / (ρ² + 13ρ + 18)`, with all three expectations finite
lower Lebesgue integrals of the hitting times.

articles.title: Covariance of coalescence times
articles.statement:
**Covariance of coalescence times** (Hudson 1983; Kaplan & Hudson 1985). Let `mA`, `mB`
solve the mean equations of the two loci and `f` the product-moment equations (`f i = 0` where
either locus has coalesced, `(Q f) i = -(mA i + mB i)` where neither has). Then `f - mA mB` is
`(ρ + 18) / (ρ² + 13ρ + 18)` from `linked`, `6 / (ρ² + 13ρ + 18)` from `partlySplit` and
`4 / (ρ² + 13ρ + 18)` from `split`. This is a statement about the backward equations; that their
solutions are the path-space moments of the chain is proved in `TwoLocusCoalescentPath`.

articles.title: Linkage disequilibrium polynomial
articles.statement: The linkage disequilibrium `D = x_AB x_ab - x_Ab x_aB` as a polynomial.

articles.title: Weighted disequilibrium polynomial $D(1-2p)(1-2q)$
articles.statement: `D (1 - 2p)(1 - 2q)` as a polynomial.

articles.title: Mean coalescence time at locus `A`
articles.statement:
For `ρ ≥ 0`, the backward equations of `E_i T_A`
(`m i = 0` where `A` has coalesced, `(Q m) i = -1` elsewhere) force `m i = 1` in every state where
`A` has not coalesced: locus `A` alone is Kingman's coalescent of two genes.

articles.title: Mean coalescence time at locus `B`
articles.statement: **Mean coalescence time at locus `B`** (the mirror image of `eq_one_of_meanTimeA`).

articles.title: Second moment of `T_A`
articles.statement:
If `m` solves the mean equations of `eq_one_of_meanTimeA` and
`g` the second-moment equations (`g i = 0` where `A` has coalesced, `(Q g) i = -2 m i`
elsewhere), then `g i = 2` where `A` has not coalesced, so the variance read off from these
equations is `2 - 1² = 1`.

articles.title: Frequency of allele A as a polynomial
articles.statement: The frequency `p = x_AB + x_Ab` of allele `A` as a polynomial.

articles.title: Frequency of allele B as a polynomial
articles.statement: The frequency `q = x_AB + x_aB` of allele `B` as a polynomial.

articles.title: Product of heterozygosities polynomial
articles.statement: `Π = p (1 - p) q (1 - q)` as a polynomial.

articles.title: The two-locus coalescent rate matrix is a rate matrix
articles.statement: For `ρ ≥ 0`, `twoLocusRate ρ` is a rate matrix.

articles.title: Stationary law of the two-locus diffusion
articles.statement:
A **stationary law** of the two-locus diffusion in the weak (basic adjoint) sense: a
probability measure on the gamete-frequency simplex with `∫ L f dμ = 0` for every polynomial
`f`.

articles.title: Product moment of the two coalescence times, path form
articles.statement:
**Product moment of the two coalescence times, path form** (Hudson 1983; Kaplan & Hudson
1985): from two linked sequences, `E (T_A T_B) = 1 + (ρ + 18) / (ρ² + 13ρ + 18)`.

articles.title: Mean coalescence time at locus `A`, path form
articles.statement:
For the two-locus ancestral process
started from two linked sequences, the hitting time `T_A` of the states where locus `A` has
coalesced has mean `1`.

articles.title: Mean coalescence time at locus `B`, path form
articles.statement:
From two linked sequences, the hitting
time `T_B` of the states where locus `B` has coalesced has mean `1`.

articles.title: Mean coalescence time at locus A
articles.statement: The mean coalescence time at locus `A`: `1` before `A` coalesces, `0` after.

articles.title: Mean coalescence time at locus B
articles.statement: The mean coalescence time at locus `B`: `1` before `B` coalesces, `0` after.

articles.title: The explicit two-locus moments solve the moment equations
articles.statement:
The systems of `covariance_of_productMoment` are solvable: `meanTimeA`, `meanTimeB` and
`productMoment ρ` satisfy them.

articles.title: Solution of the two-locus product-moment equations
articles.statement:
The explicit solution of the product-moment equations: `1 + Cov` in the three states where
neither locus has coalesced, `0` elsewhere.

articles.title: Ohta–Kimura `σ_d²`
articles.statement:
For a stationary law with `ρ, ν ≥ 0` and `E Π > 0`,
`E D² / E[p (1 - p) q (1 - q)] = sigmaDSq ρ ν`.

articles.title: Ohta–Kimura formula for $\sigma_d^2$ without mutation
articles.statement: The low-mutation value `σ_d² = (10 + ρ) / (22 + 13ρ + ρ²)` (Ohta & Kimura 1971).

articles.title: Stationary standardized linkage disequilibrium $\sigma_d^2$
articles.statement:
The stationary standardized disequilibrium
`σ_d² = (10 + ρ + 16ν) / (22 + 13ρ + ρ² + 128ν + 24ρν + 128ν²)`.

articles.title: Sum over the two-locus ancestral states
articles.statement: A sum over the six states.

articles.title: Low-mutation limit of $\sigma_d^2$
articles.statement: `σ_d² → (10 + ρ) / (22 + 13ρ + ρ²)` as the mutation rate tends to `0`, for `ρ ≥ 0`.

articles.title: Two-locus covariance vanishes under free recombination
articles.statement: Free recombination: `Cov(T_A, T_B) → 0` as `ρ → ∞`.

articles.title: Two-locus covariance is at most one
articles.statement:
The covariance is at most `Var T_A = 1` for `ρ ≥ 0` (outside this domain the formula can
exceed `1`; e.g. `twoLocusCov (-1) = 17 / 6`).

articles.title: Positivity of the two-locus covariance
articles.statement: The covariance is positive for `ρ ≥ 0`.

articles.title: Two-locus covariance under complete linkage
articles.statement: Complete linkage: `Cov(T_A, T_B) = 1 = Var T_A`.
