articles.title: The Maruyama effect (Kiezun et al. 2013)
articles.statement:
For `σ ≠ 0` and `x ∈ (0, 1)`, an allele under
selection, advantageous or deleterious, is on average strictly younger than a neutral allele at
the same frequency.

articles.title: Symmetry
articles.statement: The mean age is the same for `σ` and `-σ`.

articles.title: Kimura and Ohta (1973)
articles.statement:
The mean age of a neutral allele at frequency `x ∈ (0, 1)` is
`-2 x log x / (1 - x)` in units of `2N` generations (`-4N x ln x / (1 - x)` generations).

articles.title: Mean age of an allele at a given frequency
articles.statement:
The mean age of an allele at current frequency `x` (the paper's `a(x)`), in units of `2N`
generations: `∫₀^x Ψ₁(z) dz + ∫_x^1 Ψ₂(z) dz`.

articles.title: Neutral case of the sojourn density
articles.statement: For `σ = 0` and `0 < x < 1` the sojourn density is the neutral Green's function.

articles.title: Sojourn density of the Wright–Fisher diffusion with selection
articles.statement:
The sojourn density (Green's function) of the Wright–Fisher diffusion with genic selection,
time in units of `2N` generations, `σ = 2Ns`. With `u = kimuraFixation σ` and
`u'(x) = kimuraSlope σ · e^{-2σx}`,

`Ψ(p, x) = 2 u(min p x) (1 - u(max p x)) / (x (1 - x) u'(x))`,

which is `2 S(min p x) (S(1) - S(max p x)) / (S(1) x (1 - x) e^{-2σx})` in terms of the scale
function `S(y) = (1 - e^{-2σy}) / (2σ)` (`S(y) = y` if `σ = 0`). The neutral case is handled by
the neutral branches of `kimuraFixation` and `kimuraSlope` (`selectionGreen_zero`). It is
meaningful for `0 < x < 1`; at `x = 0, 1` the denominator vanishes and division by `0` gives `0`
(a null set for integrals in `x`). In the diffusion reading, `Ψ(p, x) dx`
is the expected time an allele started at frequency `p` spends in `(x, x + dx)` before loss or
fixation (Ewens 2004, Chapter 4; the paper's `Ψ(p, x)` divided by `2N`).

articles.title: Kimura's fixation probability is strictly increasing
articles.statement: Kimura's fixation probability is strictly increasing in the initial frequency.

articles.title: Mean age as the limit of conditional sojourn times
articles.statement:
**Mean age as the limit of conditional sojourn times** (Maruyama 1974; Kiezun et al. 2013,
Methods): for `x ∈ (0, 1)`, the total conditional sojourn time `∫₀¹ Ψ_z(p, z) dz` of a path
from initial frequency `p` to current frequency `x` tends to the mean age `a(x)` as `p → 0⁺`
(an allele arises at frequency close to `0`).

articles.title: Continuous modification selected by Kolmogorov's theorem
articles.statement: The continuous modification selected by Kolmogorov's theorem.

articles.title: Continuous realization of the raw Wright–Fisher process
articles.statement:
A selected continuous modification of the raw Wright--Fisher process,
with all pathwise properties stated on every sample.

articles.title: Kolmogorov continuity condition for the raw Wright–Fisher process
articles.statement:
The normalized raw coordinate process satisfies the explicit fourth-moment
Kolmogorov condition with `p=4`, `q=2`, and `M=3/16`.

articles.title: Kolmogorov constant for the Wright–Fisher continuity bound
articles.statement: The explicit Kolmogorov constant `3/16`.

articles.title: One-time marginals of the raw Wright–Fisher path measure
articles.statement: One-time marginals of the canonical raw path measure.

articles.title: Time-zero marginal of the raw path measure is the initial state
articles.statement:
The time-zero coordinate of the canonical path law is the prescribed
initial state.

articles.title: Two-time law of the raw Wright–Fisher path measure
articles.statement:
The ordered two-time law is the first marginal followed by the
transition over the time gap.

articles.title: Modified process has the canonical coordinate laws
articles.statement:
The modified finite-dimensional laws also equal the original canonical
coordinate laws after coercion from `I` to `ℝ`.

articles.title: Modified process has the raw finite-dimensional laws
articles.statement:
The modified process has the raw finite-dimensional laws, proved on each
finite set by intersecting its fixed-time modification events.

articles.title: Continuous modified Wright–Fisher process
articles.statement: The concrete continuous process used by the final realization.

articles.title: Chapman–Kolmogorov for the nonnegative-time Wright–Fisher kernel
articles.statement: Chapman--Kolmogorov for the nonnegative-time specialization.

articles.title: Neutral Wright–Fisher transition kernel at nonnegative time
articles.statement: The neutral Wright--Fisher transition kernel at nonnegative time.

articles.title: Canonical path measure of the raw Wright–Fisher process
articles.statement: The canonical probability measure on `NNReal → I`.

articles.title: Normalized raw process agrees with the coordinates almost surely
articles.statement: Exact normalization changes no fixed-time law.

articles.title: Raw Wright–Fisher coordinate process
articles.statement:
The raw real-valued coordinate process, normalized at time zero on every
sample rather than merely almost surely.

articles.title: Canonical sample paths of the raw Wright–Fisher process
articles.statement: Canonical sample paths before continuous modification.

articles.title: One Wright–Fisher generation as a Bernstein approximation
articles.statement:
For `M` gene copies and
current frequency `x`, the expected value of `f` at the next frequency, `∫ k, f (k / M) ∂Bin(M, x)`,
is the `M`-th Bernstein approximation of `f` on `[0, 1]` evaluated at `x`.

articles.title: Wright–Fisher diffusion limit, generator form (Feller 1951; Voronovskaya 1932)
articles.statement:
For `f`
of class `C²` and `x ∈ [0, 1]`, the one-generation generator of the neutral Wright–Fisher chain
with `M` gene copies, sped up by the factor `M` (time in units of `M` generations), converges
to the neutral Wright–Fisher diffusion generator `(L_0 f)(x) = x (1 - x) / 2 · f''(x)`.

articles.title: Absorption time of a frequency path
articles.statement:
The absorption time of a `[0, 1]`-valued path: the first time it is at `0` or `1`
(the infimum of the empty set is `0` in `ℝ≥0`; the path is absorbed almost surely, see
`ae_exists_absorbed`).

articles.title: Absorption in finite time
articles.statement:
A solution of the Wright–Fisher martingale problem is
almost surely absorbed: from some time on it is constantly `0` or constantly `1`.

## Sources

- Ethier & Kurtz (1986), ch. 10; Karlin & Taylor (1981), ch. 15. Proves the deferred entry `ae_exists_absorbed`.

articles.title: Kimura's fixation probability is twice continuously differentiable
articles.statement: Kimura's fixation probability is a `C²` function of the initial frequency on all of `ℝ`.

articles.title: Kimura–Ohta mean absorption time, process form
articles.statement:
For a solution of the neutral
Wright–Fisher martingale problem started at frequency `x`, the expected time to loss or
fixation, in units of `2N` generations, is `-2 (x log x + (1 - x) log (1 - x))`.

## Sources

- Kimura & Ohta (1969); Ewens (2004), ch. 4. Proves the deferred entry `integral_absorptionTime`.

articles.title: Martingale problem for the Wright–Fisher diffusion
articles.statement:
`X` solves the **martingale problem for the Wright–Fisher diffusion** with scaled genic
selection coefficient `σ = 2Ns` (time in units of `2N` generations) with respect to the
filtration `ℱ` and the measure `μ`: `X` takes values in `[0, 1]`, has continuous paths, is
adapted to `ℱ`, and for every `C²` function `f` the process
`f (X t) - f (X 0) - ∫₀ᵗ generator σ f (X s) ds` is an `ℱ`-martingale.

articles.title: Positivity of Kimura's slope constant
articles.statement: The slope constant of Kimura's formula is positive.

articles.title: Kimura's fixation probability, process form
articles.statement:
For a solution of the Wright–Fisher
martingale problem with scaled selection coefficient `σ = 2Ns` started at frequency `x`, the
probability that the allele is eventually fixed is `(1 - e^{-2σx}) / (1 - e^{-2σ})` (`x` when
`σ = 0`).

## Sources

- Kimura (1962); Ewens (2004), ch. 4. Proves the deferred entry `measureReal_fixation`.

articles.title: Strict monotonicity of Kimura's fixation probability
articles.statement: Kimura's fixation probability is strictly increasing in the initial frequency.

articles.title: Probability current
articles.statement:
On `(0, 1)` the current `J = σ F - F' / 2` of the stationary
forward equation, for the weighted density `F(x) = x (1 - x) φ(x)`, is the constant
`θ · u_σ'(0) / 2` (`u_σ'(0) = kimuraSlope σ = 2σ / (1 - e^{-2σ})`, and `1` for `σ = 0`), so
`J = θ σ / (1 - e^{-2σ})`, and `J = θ / 2` in the neutral case: the mutational input of
frequency at `0`, carried through `(0, 1)` to fixation at `1`.

articles.title: ODE characterization of the Poisson-random-field density
articles.statement:
Let `θ ≠ 0` and let `φ` be
a density on `(0, 1)` whose weighted density `x (1 - x) φ(x)` extends to a function `F`
continuous on `[0, 1]`, twice differentiable on `(0, 1)`, solving the stationary forward
equation `½ F'' - σ F' = 0` there, with boundary normalizations `F(0) = θ` and `F(1) = 0`.
Then `φ` is the Sawyer–Hartl density on `(0, 1)`.

articles.title: Expected number of sites derived in the whole neutral sample
articles.statement:
With `σ = 0` the expected number of sites at which all `n ≥ 1` sampled copies carry the
derived allele is `θ / n`. These sites are monomorphic in the sample, so this is not a class of
the site-frequency spectrum.

articles.title: Neutral site-frequency spectrum (Fu 1995)
articles.statement:
With `σ = 0`, for the segregating classes
`1 ≤ i < n` the expected number of sites with `i` derived copies in a sample of `n` is
`θ / i`.

articles.title: Expected site frequency spectrum under the Poisson random field
articles.statement:
The expected unfolded site-frequency spectrum of a sample of `n` gene copies under the
Poisson random field: the expected number of sites where exactly `i` of the `n` sampled copies
carry the derived allele, `E ξ_i = ∫ x in 0..1, C(n, i) x ^ i (1 - x) ^ (n - i) φ(x)`.
The site-frequency spectrum consists of the segregating classes `1 ≤ i < n`. The value at
`i = n` is the expected number of sites at which every sampled copy is derived (monomorphic in
the sample, `expectedSFS_neutral_self`); for `i = 0` the integrand is not integrable at `0` (the
expected number of ancestral-monomorphic sites is infinite) and Lean's integral returns its junk
value `0`.

articles.title: Stationary forward equation (Sawyer–Hartl 1992)
articles.statement:
On `(0, 1)` the weighted density
`F(x) = x (1 - x) φ(x)` of the Poisson-random-field density solves the stationary
Fokker–Planck equation `½ F'' - σ F' = 0` of the Wright–Fisher diffusion with genic selection
`σ` (the forward equation `½ (x (1 - x) φ)'' - (σ x (1 - x) φ)' = 0`).

articles.title: Closed form of the Poisson random field density with selection
articles.statement:
The Poisson-random-field density with selection, explicitly:
`θ (1 - e^{-2σ(1 - x)}) / ((1 - e^{-2σ}) x (1 - x))` for `σ ≠ 0`.

articles.title: The neutral density from the Green's function
articles.statement:
A new neutral mutation enters at a
small frequency `p`; with mutations arriving at rate `θ / (2p)` per unit time (so that the
mutational input of frequency is `θ / 2`), the expected sojourn density at `x ≥ p` is
`θ / (2p) · G(p, x) = θ / x`, the neutral Poisson-random-field density.

articles.title: Neutral Poisson random field density
articles.statement: The neutral Poisson-random-field density is `θ / x` (for `x ≠ 1`).

articles.title: Sawyer–Hartl Poisson random field density
articles.statement:
The Sawyer–Hartl (1992) Poisson-random-field density: the expected number of sites per unit
frequency at which the derived allele has frequency `x`, for scaled mutation rate `θ = 4Nu`
and scaled genic selection `σ = 2Ns`:
`θ · u_σ(1 - x) / (x (1 - x))` with `u_σ = kimuraFixation σ`, i.e.
`θ (1 - e^{-2σ(1 - x)}) / ((1 - e^{-2σ}) x (1 - x))`, and `θ / x` when `σ = 0`.
The model domain is `θ > 0` and `x ∈ (0, 1)`; at `x = 0, 1` Lean's `a / 0 = 0` gives the junk
value `0`.

articles.title: Boundary normalization at `1`
articles.statement:
As `x → 1⁻` the weighted density `x (1 - x) φ(x)` tends
to `0`.

articles.title: Boundary normalization at `0`
articles.statement:
As `x → 0⁺` the weighted density `x (1 - x) φ(x)` tends
to `θ`. (This is not the probability current, which is `current_prfDensity`.)

articles.title: Generator of the ancestral selection graph line-counting process
articles.statement:
The generator of the line-counting process of the ancestral selection graph with scaled
selection coefficient `σ` (time in units of `2N` generations, the scaling of `generator`):
from `n` lines, branching `n → n + 1` at rate `n σ` and coalescence `n → n - 1` at rate
`C(n, 2)`.

articles.title: Detailed balance
articles.statement:
**Detailed balance** of the ancestral-selection-graph chain:
`π_k · (k σ) = π_{k+1} · C(k + 1, 2)` for every `k` (the flux `k → k + 1` equals the flux
`k + 1 → k`). This is an identity for every real `σ`.

articles.title: Global balance
articles.statement:
**Global balance** (stationarity `π Q = 0`) of the ancestral-selection-graph chain at
state `k + 1`: the outflow `π_{k+1} ((k + 1) σ + C(k + 1, 2))` equals the inflow
`π_k (k σ) + π_{k+2} C(k + 2, 2)` (for `k = 0` the inflow from the unreachable state `0`
vanishes).

articles.title: Stationary weights under selection are nonnegative
articles.statement: For `σ > 0` the stationary weights are nonnegative.

articles.title: Stationary law of the ancestral selection graph line counts
articles.statement:
The stationary law of the ancestral-selection-graph line-counting process with `σ > 0`:
`π_k = (2σ)^k / k! / (e^{2σ} - 1)` for `k ≥ 1` and `π_0 = 0`, a Poisson`(2σ)` law conditioned
to be positive. For `σ = 0` the stationary law is `δ₁`: branching vanishes, coalescence
reaches state `1`, and state `1` is absorbing, so `π_1 = 1` and `π_k = 0` otherwise (the
limit of the `σ > 0` formula as `σ → 0`).

articles.title: Sojourn density conditioned on fixation
articles.statement:
The sojourn density conditioned on fixation, the Doob `h`-transform of the Green's function
by the fixation probability `u`: `G(p, x) u(x) / u(p)` (Kimura–Ohta 1969; Ewens 2004, Chapter 4).
At `p = 0` it is the junk value `0`.

articles.title: Continuity of the scale density on $(0, 1)$
articles.statement: The scale density is continuous on `[0, 1]`.

articles.title: Continuity of the scale function on $(0, 1)$
articles.statement: The scale function is continuous on `[0, 1]`.

articles.title: Kimura (1962)
articles.statement:
The scale-function ratio `S / S(1)` solves the backward equation
`a / 2 · u'' + b · u' = 0` on `(0, 1)`.

articles.title: Green's representation (Ewens 2004, Chapter 4; Karlin–Taylor 1981, Chapter 15)
articles.statement:
Let `g` be
continuous on `(0, 1)` and assume the two halves of the Green integral are integrable away from
the opposite boundary: `S g / (a ψ)` on `[0, q]` and `(S(1) - S) g / (a ψ)` on `[q, 1]` for every
`q ∈ (0, 1)` (true for every `g` continuous on `[0, 1]` under genic selection, where
`S / (a ψ)` is bounded near `0` and `(S(1) - S) / (a ψ)` near `1`). Then
`v(q) = ∫₀¹ G(q, x) g(x) dx` solves `L v = -g` on `(0, 1)`.

articles.title: Conditional mean time to fixation, backward equation
articles.statement:
Under the hypotheses of
`diffusionGenerator_integral_greenFunction` for `g = u` (the fixation probability), the
function `w(q) = u(q) · ∫₀¹ G*(q, x) dx`, with `G*` the conditional sojourn density, solves
`L w = -u` on `(0, 1)` (Ewens 2004, Chapter 4).

articles.title: Wright–Fisher generator with genic selection as a general diffusion
articles.statement:
The general generator with drift `σ x (1 - x)` and variance `x (1 - x)` is the Wright–Fisher
generator with genic selection.

articles.title: Backward generator of a one-dimensional diffusion
articles.statement:
The backward generator of a one-dimensional diffusion with drift `b` and infinitesimal
variance `a`: `(L u)(x) = a(x) / 2 · u''(x) + b(x) · u'(x)`.

articles.title: Drift of an allele under selection with dominance
articles.statement:
The drift `2 c x (1 - x) (h + (1 - 2h) x)` of an allele at frequency `x` with genotype
fitnesses `1`, `1 + h s`, `1 + s` (for zero, one and two copies), `c = N s`, time in units of
`2N` generations (Kimura 1962). For `h = 1/2` it is genic selection with `σ = c`.

articles.title: Uniqueness of the scale-function ratio (Kimura 1962)
articles.statement:
A function continuous on
`[0, 1]`, differentiable on `(0, 1)` with derivative differentiable on `(0, 1)`, solving
`L u = 0` on `(0, 1)` with `u(0) = 0` and `u(1) = 1` equals `S / S(1)` on `[0, 1]`.

articles.title: Solutions of `L u = 0`
articles.statement:
If `u` is continuous on `[0, 1]`, differentiable on `(0, 1)`
with derivative differentiable on `(0, 1)`, and `L u = 0` on `(0, 1)`, then
`u = u(0) + (u(1) - u(0)) · S / S(1)` on `[0, 1]`.

articles.title: Uniqueness for the Dirichlet problem
articles.statement:
Two functions continuous on `[0, 1]`,
differentiable on `(0, 1)` with derivatives differentiable on `(0, 1)`, with `L u = L v` on
`(0, 1)` and the same values at `0` and `1`, agree on `[0, 1]`. Together with
`diffusionGenerator_integral_greenFunction` this identifies the Green integral as the solution
of `L v = -g`, `v(0) = v(1) = 0` whenever it has this regularity.

articles.title: Kimura's scale-function ratio with dominance (Kimura 1962)
articles.statement:
With `D = 2h - 1`, for
`p ∈ [0, 1]`,
`u(p) = ∫₀^p e^{-2cDx(1-x) - 2cx} dx / ∫₀¹ e^{-2cDx(1-x) - 2cx} dx`.

articles.title: Dirichlet ratio lies in $(0, 1)$
articles.statement: The scale-function ratio lies in `[0, 1]`.

articles.title: Dirichlet ratio equals one at $p = 1$
articles.statement: A fixed allele stays fixed.

articles.title: Kimura's formula as a corollary
articles.statement:
For genic selection the general scale-function ratio
is `kimuraFixation σ p` on `[0, 1]`.

articles.title: Dirichlet ratio vanishes at $p = 0$
articles.statement: An absent allele is never fixed (for every `b`, `a`).

articles.title: Dirichlet ratio $S(p)/S(1)$ of the scale function
articles.statement:
The analytic Dirichlet ratio `S(p) / S(1)` for drift `b` and variance `a` (Kimura 1962;
Ewens 2004, Chapter 4). This is the solution of the backward boundary-value problem
`L u = 0`, `u(0) = 0`, `u(1) = 1` (see `eq_fixationProb_of_diffusionGenerator_eq_zero`).
It is the hitting probability `P_p(hit 1 before 0)` only when both boundaries are
Feller-accessible; that is not implied by `IsRegularDiffusion` (see the module docstring for
the `a x = x² (1 - x)²` counterexample).

articles.title: Backward equation for the neutral conditional fixation time
articles.statement:
The neutral conditional fixation time satisfies the conditioned backward equation
`L_0 (p · t̄₁(p)) = -p` on `(0, 1)`.

articles.title: Selection duality in operator form
articles.statement:
The selection duality in operator form: `L_σ` applied to `y ↦ (1 - y) ^ n` equals the
ancestral-selection-graph generator applied to `k ↦ (1 - x) ^ k` at `n`.

articles.title: Selection duality (Mano 2009)
articles.statement:
**Selection duality (Mano 2009)** at generator level, with the line-counting process of the
ancestral selection graph (Krone–Neuhauser 1997) as the dual: the
Wright–Fisher generator with genic selection maps `y ↦ (1 - y) ^ n` to
`C(n, 2) ((1 - x)^(n-1) - (1 - x)^n) + n σ ((1 - x)^(n+1) - (1 - x)^n)`. This identity holds for
every real `σ`; the dual is a Markov chain only for `σ ≥ 0`.

articles.title: General Green's function agrees with the neutral Wright–Fisher one
articles.statement:
The general Green's function of the neutral Wright–Fisher diffusion (`b = 0`,
`a = x (1 - x)`) is the neutral Green's function of `Sojourn.lean` for `x ∈ (0, 1)`.

articles.title: Dirichlet Green's function of a one-dimensional diffusion
articles.statement:
The Green's function (analytic Green kernel) of `-L` with Dirichlet conditions at `0` and `1`
(Ewens 2004, Chapter 4; Karlin–Taylor 1981, Chapter 15):
`G(p, x) = 2 S(min p x) (S(1) - S(max p x)) / (S(1) a(x) ψ(x))`. In the diffusion reading (which requires Feller-accessible boundaries), `G(p, x) dx` is the expected time
spent in `(x, x + dx)` before absorption.

articles.title: Derivative of the scale density
articles.statement: `ψ' = -(2 b / a) ψ` inside the interval.

articles.title: Derivative of the scale function is the scale density
articles.statement: `S' = ψ` inside the interval.

articles.title: Loss probability from the stationary ancestral selection graph
articles.statement:
**Loss probability from the stationary ancestral selection graph** (Mano 2009): for
`σ > 0`, `∑ₖ π_k (1 - x)^k = 1 - kimuraFixation σ x`, i.e. the loss
probability of the favoured allele at frequency `x` is the probability that all lines of the
stationary ancestral selection graph carry the unfavoured allele. Only the series identity is
formalized; the sampling interpretation is not.

articles.title: Neutral stationary law is the point mass at one
articles.statement: The neutral stationary law is `δ₁`: its generating function is `y`.

articles.title: Generating function of the stationary law under selection
articles.statement:
The probability generating function of the stationary law: for `σ > 0` and every real `y`,
`∑ₖ π_k y^k = (e^{2σy} - 1) / (e^{2σ} - 1)`.

articles.title: Neutral stationary weights sum to one
articles.statement: The neutral stationary weights sum to `1`.

articles.title: Stationary weights under selection sum to one
articles.statement: For `σ > 0` the stationary weights sum to `1`.

articles.title: The general `h`-transform specializes to Kimura–Ohta
articles.statement:
For the neutral Wright–Fisher
diffusion (`b = 0`, `a = x (1 - x)`) and `p ∈ (0, 1)`, the total conditional sojourn time
`∫₀¹ G(p, x) u(x) / u(p) dx` is `-2 (1 - p) log (1 - p) / p`.

articles.title: Dirichlet condition of the Green's function at one
articles.statement: Dirichlet condition at `1`: `∫₀¹ G(1, x) g(x) dx = 0` (for every `b`, `a`, `g`).

articles.title: Dirichlet condition of the Green's function at zero
articles.statement: Dirichlet condition at `0`: `∫₀¹ G(0, x) g(x) dx = 0` (for every `b`, `a`, `g`).

articles.title: Neutral conditional fixation time as an `h`-transformed sojourn integral
articles.statement:
For
`p ∈ (0, 1)`, `∫₀¹ G(p, x) · x / p dx = -2 (1 - p) log (1 - p) / p`, with `G` the neutral
Green's function and `u(x) = x` the neutral fixation probability.

articles.title: Neutral conditional loss time
Diffusion with dominance is regular
articles.statement: The diffusion with dominance is regular.

articles.title: Wright–Fisher diffusion with genic selection is regular
articles.statement: The Wright–Fisher diffusion with genic selection is regular.

articles.title: Standing regularity hypotheses for a diffusion on $(0, 1)$
articles.statement:
Regularity hypotheses for a diffusion on `(0, 1)` with drift `b` and variance `a`: `a` is
positive and continuous on `(0, 1)`, `b / a` is continuous on `(0, 1)` and integrable on
`[0, 1]` (so the scale function is finite up to both boundaries). The values of `b` and `a` at
`0` and `1` are irrelevant. These are standing hypotheses for this file, not Feller's
classification of regular boundaries: they do **not** imply that either endpoint is
accessible (finite scale–speed integrals), so the hitting-probability reading of
`fixationProb` needs that extra hypothesis.

articles.title: Total expectation
articles.statement:
For `p ∈ (0, 1)`,
`p · t̄₁(p) + (1 - p) · t̄₀(p) = -2 (p log p + (1 - p) log (1 - p))`, the unconditional mean
absorption time.

articles.title: Neutral conditional mean time to fixation
articles.statement:
The neutral conditional mean time to fixation `t̄₁(p) = -2 (1 - p) log (1 - p) / p`, in
units of `2N` generations (Kimura–Ohta 1969). It is meaningful for `p ∈ (0, 1)`; at `p = 0`
the division gives the junk value `0` (the limit is `2`, see
`tendsto_neutralFixationTime_zero`).

articles.title: Neutral loss time equals fixation time at $1 - p$
articles.statement: Loss of an allele at frequency `p` is fixation of the other allele at `1 - p`.

articles.title: Neutral conditional mean time to loss
articles.statement:
The neutral conditional mean time to loss `t̄₀(p) = -2 p log p / (1 - p)`, in units of
`2N` generations (Kimura–Ohta 1969). It is meaningful for `p ∈ (0, 1)`.

articles.title: Loss probability in Kimura's fixation formula
articles.statement:
The loss probability in Kimura's formula, written with positive exponents: for `σ ≠ 0`,
`1 - kimuraFixation σ x = (e^{2σ(1 - x)} - 1) / (e^{2σ} - 1)`.

articles.title: Positivity of the scale density
articles.statement: The scale density is positive.

articles.title: Scale density of the Wright–Fisher diffusion with genic selection
articles.statement:
The scale density of the Wright–Fisher diffusion with genic selection is `e^{-2σy}` on
`[0, 1]`.

articles.title: Scale density of a one-dimensional diffusion
articles.statement:
The scale density `ψ(y) = exp (-∫₀^y 2 b(z) / a(z) dz)` of the diffusion with drift `b`
and variance `a` (Karlin–Taylor 1981, Chapter 15).

articles.title: Scale function is positive at one
articles.statement:
`S(1) > 0`, so the scale-function ratio and the Green's function have a positive
denominator.

articles.title: Scale function vanishes at zero
articles.statement: The scale function vanishes at `0`.

articles.title: Scale function of a one-dimensional diffusion
articles.statement: The scale function `S(p) = ∫₀^p ψ(y) dy`, normalized by `S(0) = 0`.

articles.title: Scale function is strictly increasing
articles.statement: The scale function is strictly increasing on `[0, 1]`.

articles.title: `t̄₁(0⁺) = 2`
articles.statement:
A new neutral mutation that is destined to fix takes on average `2`
units (`4N` generations) to do so (Kimura–Ohta 1969).

articles.title: Green's representation (Ewens 2004, Chapter 4)
articles.statement:
For continuous `g` and `p ∈ (0, 1)`, the
function `u(q) = ∫ x in 0..1, G(q, x) g(x)` solves the neutral backward equation `L_0 u = -g`
at `p`. In the diffusion reading, `u(p)` is the expected value of
`∫₀^T g(X_t) dt` up to the absorption time `T`.

articles.title: Sojourn integral vanishes for an absent allele
articles.statement:
Boundary value at `0`: an allele that is absent spends no time in `(0, 1)`, so
`∫ x in 0..1, G(0, x) g(x) = 0`.

articles.title: Sojourn integral vanishes for a fixed allele
articles.statement:
Boundary value at `1`: a fixed allele spends no time in `(0, 1)`, so
`∫ x in 0..1, G(1, x) g(x) = 0`.

articles.title: Mean absorption time as a sojourn integral
articles.statement:
For `p ∈ [0, 1]`, the total expected
sojourn time `∫ x in 0..1, G(p, x)` is the Kimura–Ohta mean absorption time
`-2 (p log p + (1 - p) log (1 - p))` (units of `2N` generations).

articles.title: Neutral Wright–Fisher Green's function
articles.statement:
The neutral Wright–Fisher Green's function (sojourn density), time in units of `2N`
generations (Ewens 2004, Chapter 4): `G(p, x) = 2 (1 - p) / (1 - x)` for `x ≤ p` and
`G(p, x) = 2 p / x` for `p < x`. In the diffusion reading, for
`0 < x < 1`, `G(p, x) dx` is the expected time a neutral allele started at frequency `p` spends
at frequencies in `(x, x + dx)` before loss or fixation.

articles.title: Beta density as Wright's stationary density
articles.statement:
On `(0, 1)` the Beta`(θ₁, θ₂)` density is Wright's unnormalized density in the scaled rates
`α = θ₁ / 2`, `β = θ₂ / 2`, divided by the Beta function `B(θ₁, θ₂)`.

articles.title: Smoothness of the Beta density on the open unit interval
articles.statement:
The Beta`(θ₁, θ₂)` density is analytic (`C^ω`), in particular smooth, on `(0, 1)`, so the
derivatives in `flux_betaPDFReal` and `forwardEquation_betaPDFReal` exist.

articles.title: Zero probability flux (Wright 1931)
articles.statement:
On `(0, 1)` the Beta`(θ₁, θ₂)` density `π`
satisfies `½ (x (1 - x) π)' - (θ₁ (1 - x) - θ₂ x) / 2 · π = 0`. The identity holds for all real
`θ₁, θ₂` (it is linear in `π`; Mathlib's density is identically `0` when `B(θ₁, θ₂) = 0`);
`π` is a probability density when `θ₁, θ₂ > 0` (`isProbabilityMeasureBeta`).

articles.title: Stationary forward equation (Wright 1931)
articles.statement:
On `(0, 1)` the Beta`(θ₁, θ₂)` density `π`
solves the stationary Fokker–Planck equation `½ (a π)'' - (b π)' = 0` with `a(x) = x (1 - x)` and
`b(x) = (θ₁ (1 - x) - θ₂ x) / 2`. Holds for all real `θ₁, θ₂` (see `flux_betaPDFReal`).

articles.title: Integrability of the mutation generator under Wright's stationary law
articles.statement:
For `θ₁, θ₂ > 0` and `f` twice continuously differentiable on `[0, 1]`, `L f` is integrable
against Wright's stationary law `Beta(θ₁, θ₂)`.

articles.title: Drift of the Wright–Fisher chain with mutation (Ewens 2004, ch. 4)
articles.statement:
One generation of the
Wright–Fisher chain on `M` gene copies (`M = 2N`): mutation moves the frequency `x` to
`p' = mutatedFreq u₁ u₂ x`, then the new count is `Binomial(M, p')`. With `u₁ = θ₁ / (2M)`,
`u₂ = θ₂ / (2M)` (`θᵢ = 4N uᵢ`), the expected change of frequency per `2N = M` generations is
exactly the drift coefficient of `mutationGenerator`:
`M · (E[k / M] - x) = (θ₁ (1 - x) - θ₂ x) / 2`, for every `M`.

articles.title: Infinitesimal variance of the Wright–Fisher chain with mutation
articles.statement:
In the setting of
`integral_binomial_mutatedFreq_drift`, the scaled second moment of the frequency change is
`M · E[(k / M - x) ^ 2] = p' (1 - p') + (θ₁ (1 - x) - θ₂ x) ^ 2 / (4M)` with
`p' = mutatedFreq u₁ u₂ x = x + (θ₁ (1 - x) - θ₂ x) / (2M)`. As `M → ∞` with `θ₁, θ₂, x` fixed
this tends to `x (1 - x)`, the diffusion coefficient of `mutationGenerator` (the limit itself is
not stated here).

articles.title: Weak stationarity of Wright's law (Wright 1931; Ewens 2004, ch. 4)
articles.statement:
For `θ₁, θ₂ > 0`
and every `f` twice continuously differentiable on `[0, 1]`, `∫ L f d(Beta(θ₁, θ₂)) = 0`.

articles.title: Weak stationarity of Wright's law (density form)
articles.statement:
For `θ₁, θ₂ > 0` and every `f` twice
continuously differentiable on `[0, 1]`, `∫₀¹ (L f)(x) π(x) dx = 0` for the Beta`(θ₁, θ₂)`
density `π`. (`L f` uses `deriv`, which agrees with the one-sided derivatives inside `(0, 1)`;
its values at the endpoints do not affect the integral.) The proof is integration by parts:
`L f · π = (x ^ θ₁ (1 - x) ^ θ₂ f' / (2 B(θ₁, θ₂)))'` on `(0, 1)` because the flux vanishes, and
this boundary term is `0` at both endpoints since `θ₁, θ₂ > 0`.

articles.title: Integrability of the mutation generator against the Beta density
articles.statement:
For `θ₁, θ₂ > 0` and `f` twice continuously differentiable on `[0, 1]`, `L f · π` is
integrable on `[0, 1]`, so the integral in `integral_mutationGenerator_mul_betaPDFReal` is a
genuine (not junk) value.

articles.title: Allele frequency after one generation of two-way mutation
articles.statement:
Allele frequency after one generation of two-way mutation, before random sampling: an `a`
copy mutates to `A` with probability `u₁` and an `A` copy to `a` with probability `u₂`, so the
frequency `x` of `A` becomes `(1 - u₂) x + u₁ (1 - x) ∈ [0, 1]`.

articles.title: Mutation generator applied to heterozygosity
articles.statement:
The generator applied to the heterozygosity `H(x) = 2x (1 - x)`:
`L H = -2x (1 - x) + (θ₁ (1 - x) - θ₂ x) (1 - 2x)` (drift decreases `H` at rate `1`, mutation
restores it).

articles.title: Mutation generator applied to the allele frequency
articles.statement:
The generator applied to the frequency itself is the mutation drift:
`L x = (θ₁ (1 - x) - θ₂ x) / 2`.

articles.title: Mutation generator without mutation is the neutral generator
articles.statement: Without mutation the generator is the neutral Wright–Fisher generator `generator 0`.

articles.title: Wright–Fisher generator with two-way mutation
articles.statement:
The backward generator of the Wright–Fisher diffusion with two-way mutation, time in units of
`2N` generations and scaled mutation rates `θ₁ = 4N u₁` (towards the allele) and `θ₂ = 4N u₂`
(away from it): `(L f)(x) = x (1 - x) / 2 · f''(x) + (θ₁ (1 - x) - θ₂ x) / 2 · f'(x)`.

articles.title: Continuity of Kimura's fixation probability
articles.statement: Kimura's fixation probability is continuous in the initial frequency.

articles.title: Wright's stationary density (zero-flux form)
articles.statement:
On `(0, 1)`, with infinitesimal variance
`a(x) = x (1 - x)` and mutation drift `b(x) = α (1 - x) - β x`, Wright's density
`π(x) = x ^ (2α - 1) (1 - x) ^ (2β - 1)` satisfies `(a π)' = 2 b π`, i.e. the stationary
forward (Fokker–Planck) equation `½ (a π)' - b π = 0` with zero probability flux.

articles.title: Derivative of Kimura's fixation probability as a function
articles.statement: The derivative of Kimura's fixation probability, as a function.

articles.title: Uniqueness of the fixation probability
articles.statement:
**Uniqueness of the fixation probability**, `C²` form: a function continuous on `[0, 1]`,
`C²` on `(0, 1)`, solving `L_σ u = 0` on `(0, 1)` with `u 0 = 0`, `u 1 = 1` equals Kimura's
fixation probability on `[0, 1]`.

articles.title: Uniqueness of the fixation probability (Kimura 1962)
articles.statement:
If `u` is continuous on `[0, 1]`,
differentiable on `(0, 1)` with derivative `u'` differentiable on `(0, 1)`, solves the backward
equation `L_σ u = 0` on `(0, 1)`, and satisfies `u 0 = 0`, `u 1 = 1`, then `u` is Kimura's
fixation probability on `[0, 1]`.

articles.title: Decay of heterozygosity
articles.statement:
`H(x) = 2x(1 - x)` is an eigenfunction of the neutral
generator with eigenvalue `-1`, so `E[H_t] = H_0 e^{-t}` (time in units of `2N` generations).

articles.title: Kimura (1962)
articles.statement:
The fixation probability solves the backward equation
`x (1 - x) / 2 · u'' + σ x (1 - x) · u' = 0` (everywhere).

articles.title: Kimura–Ohta (1969)
articles.statement: The neutral mean absorption time solves `L_0 T = -1` on `(0, 1)`.

articles.title: Moment duality with Kingman's coalescent
articles.statement:
**Moment duality with Kingman's coalescent** at generator level: the neutral generator maps
`y ↦ y ^ n` to `C(n, 2) (x ^ (n - 1) - x ^ n)`, which is the generator of the block-counting
process (jumps `n → n - 1` at rate `C(n, 2)`) applied to `n ↦ x ^ n`.

articles.title: Backward generator of the Wright–Fisher diffusion with selection
articles.statement:
The backward generator of the Wright–Fisher diffusion with genic selection, time in units
of `2N` generations and scaled selection coefficient `σ = 2Ns`:
`(L_σ u)(x) = x (1 - x) / 2 · u''(x) + σ x (1 - x) · u'(x)`.

articles.title: Derivative of Kimura's fixation probability at a point
articles.statement: The derivative of Kimura's fixation probability: `u'(x) = K σ · e^{-2σx}`.

articles.title: Derivative of the neutral mean absorption time
Heterozygosity decay in one Wright–Fisher generation
articles.statement:
If the number `X` of copies of an
allele among `M` gene copies (`M = 2N` for diploids) is `Binomial(M, x)`, then the new frequency
`p' = X / M` satisfies `E[2 p' (1 - p')] = (1 - 1/M) · 2x(1 - x)`.

articles.title: Wright's density has finite positive total mass
articles.statement: For `α, β > 0` Wright's density has a finite, positive total mass on `(0, 1)`.

articles.title: Normalization of Wright's density
articles.statement:
For `α, β > 0` the stationary density integrates to
the Beta function `B(2α, 2β) = Γ(2α) Γ(2β) / Γ(2α + 2β)`, so
`wrightDensity α β x / B(2α, 2β)` is the Beta`(2α, 2β)` probability density on `(0, 1)`.

articles.title: Integrability of Wright's density on the unit interval
articles.statement: For `α, β > 0` Wright's density is integrable on `[0, 1]`.

articles.title: Kimura's fixation probability is at most one
articles.statement:
Kimura's fixation probability is at most `1` at frequencies `y ≤ 1`, for every selection
coefficient `σ`.

articles.title: Kimura's fixation probability lies in the unit interval
articles.statement: Kimura's fixation probability is a probability on `[0, 1]`.

articles.title: Neutral fixation probability equals the initial frequency
articles.statement: Neutral case: the fixation probability equals the initial frequency.

articles.title: Nonnegativity of Kimura's fixation probability
articles.statement:
Kimura's fixation probability is nonnegative at nonnegative frequencies, for every
selection coefficient `σ`.

articles.title: Kimura's fixation probability equals one at frequency one
articles.statement: An allele that is already fixed stays fixed.

articles.title: Kimura's fixation probability vanishes at frequency zero
articles.statement: An allele that is absent is never fixed.

articles.title: Kimura's fixation probability
articles.statement:
Kimura's fixation probability of an allele at initial frequency `x` with scaled selection
coefficient `σ = 2Ns`: `(1 - e^{-2σx}) / (1 - e^{-2σ})`, and `x` in the neutral case.

articles.title: Slope constant of Kimura's formula is nonzero
articles.statement: The slope constant of Kimura's formula never vanishes.

articles.title: Slope constant of Kimura's fixation probability
articles.statement:
The constant `K σ` such that `(kimuraFixation σ)' x = K σ · e^{-2σx}`:
`1` if `σ = 0`, and `2σ / (1 - e^{-2σ})` otherwise.

articles.title: Advantageous alleles fix more often than their initial frequency
articles.statement:
Advantageous alleles (`σ > 0`) are fixed with probability strictly larger than their
initial frequency `x ∈ (0, 1)`.

articles.title: Neutral mean absorption time vanishes at frequency one
articles.statement: The neutral mean absorption time vanishes at `x = 1`.

articles.title: Neutral mean absorption time vanishes at frequency zero
articles.statement: The neutral mean absorption time vanishes at `x = 0`.

articles.title: Kimura–Ohta mean absorption time of a neutral allele
articles.statement:
Kimura–Ohta mean time to absorption (loss or fixation) of a neutral allele at frequency `x`,
in units of `2N` generations: `-2 (x log x + (1 - x) log (1 - x))`. In generations this is
`-4N (x ln x + (1 - x) ln (1 - x))`.

articles.title: Denominator of Kimura's formula is nonzero
articles.statement: For `σ ≠ 0` the denominator `1 - e^{-2σ}` of Kimura's formula does not vanish.

articles.title: Wright's stationary density of the Wright–Fisher diffusion
articles.statement:
Wright's (unnormalized) stationary density of the Wright–Fisher diffusion with scaled
mutation rates `α` (towards the allele) and `β` (away from it):
`x ^ (2α - 1) (1 - x) ^ (2β - 1)` (real powers).

articles.title: Cauchy property of uniform contractions extends from a dense set
articles.statement: Uniformly contractive operators that are Cauchy on a dense set are Cauchy everywhere.

articles.title: Rescaled Wright–Fisher iterates form a Cauchy sequence
articles.statement:
For every continuous `f`, the sequence `(wfStep M)^⌊tM⌋ f` is Cauchy in `C([0, 1], ℝ)`: it
converges on the dense set of polynomials and the operators are contractions.

articles.title: Weierstrass approximation theorem on the unit interval
articles.statement: Weierstrass approximation: polynomial functions are dense in `C([0, 1], ℝ)`.

articles.title: Dual moment polynomial of Kingman's coalescent
articles.statement:
The dual moment polynomial `∑_k P_t(n → k) X^k`, where for `t ≥ 0`,
`P_t(n → k) = exp (t • G) n k` is the probability that `n` lineages of Kingman's coalescent have
`k` ancestors time `t` earlier (time in units of `M = 2N` generations); evaluated at `x` it is
`E_n[x^{A_t}]` for the block-counting process `A`.

articles.title: Polynomial generator agrees with the neutral Wright–Fisher generator
articles.statement: `polyGenerator` is the neutral Wright–Fisher generator `generator 0` evaluated on `p`.

articles.title: Natural floor of a nonpositive multiple is zero
articles.statement: If `t ≤ 0`, then the natural floor of `t * M` is zero.

articles.title: Polynomial semigroup dynamics
articles.statement:
At every positive time, differentiating the existing
Wright–Fisher semigroup on a polynomial equals applying the semigroup to its generator.

articles.title: Moment duality, one generation
articles.statement:
If the allele count after one neutral Wright–Fisher
generation with `M ≥ 1` gene copies is `Bin(M, x)`, then
`E_x[(X₁)^n] = ∑_k wfLineageProb M n k · x^k`, where `X₁` is the new frequency and
`wfLineageProb M n k` is the probability that `n` genes have `k` distinct parents.

articles.title: Kernel form of Wright–Fisher moment duality
articles.statement:
Kernel form of Wright–Fisher moment duality: transition-kernel moments are the transition
probabilities of Kingman's block-counting process.

articles.title: Wright–Fisher transition kernel represents the semigroup
articles.statement:
Integration against the transition kernel agrees with the Wright–Fisher semigroup on every
continuous test function and every initial allele frequency.

articles.title: Contraction
articles.statement: `sup_{[0,1]} |wfSemigroup t f| ≤ sup_{[0,1]} |f|`.

articles.title: One Wright–Fisher generation is a sup-norm contraction
articles.statement: One Wright–Fisher generation is a contraction for the sup norm.

articles.title: Iterated Wright–Fisher generations are sup-norm contractions
articles.statement: Any number of Wright–Fisher generations is a contraction for the sup norm.

articles.title: Neutral Wright–Fisher generator on polynomials
articles.statement: The neutral Wright–Fisher generator on polynomials, `x (1 - x) / 2 · p''`.

articles.title: Semigroup law
articles.statement:
**Semigroup law** on polynomials, from `exp ((s + t) • G) = exp (t • G) * exp (s • G)` and
truncation consistency; holds for all real `s`, `t`.

articles.title: Dual semigroup fixes the constant polynomial one
articles.statement: The dual semigroup fixes the constant polynomial `1` (zero lineages stay zero).

articles.title: Dual semigroup on a monomial
articles.statement: The dual semigroup on a monomial is the dual moment polynomial.

articles.title: Dual semigroup at time zero is the identity
articles.statement: At time `0` the dual semigroup is the identity.

articles.title: Wright–Fisher semigroup on polynomials by moment duality
articles.statement:
The neutral Wright–Fisher diffusion semigroup on polynomials, defined by moment duality on
the monomial basis: `polySemigroup t (X ^ n) = dualMomentPoly t n`. It is meaningful for
`t ≥ 0`; the formula is defined, and the group law holds, for every real `t`.

articles.title: Powers of a unital endomorphism fix the constant function
articles.statement: Every power of a continuous linear endomorphism fixing `1` also fixes `1`.

articles.title: Powers of a positive endomorphism are positive
articles.statement: Every power of a positive continuous linear endomorphism is positive.

articles.title: Moment duality, one generation (polynomial identity)
articles.statement:
For `M ≥ 1` gene copies,
`∑_i C(M, i) x^i (1 - x)^(M - i) (i/M)^n = ∑_k S(n, k) M_(k) / M^n · x^k`: the `n`-th moment of
the frequency after one generation equals the generating function of the number of distinct
parents of `n` sampled genes. Holds for every real `x`.

## Sources

- Ethier & Griffiths (1993); Durrett (2008), §7.

articles.title: Limits of uniform contractions extend from a dense set
articles.statement: Limits of uniformly contractive operators extend from a dense set to the whole space.

articles.title: Strong continuity
articles.statement:
`wfSemigroup t f → f` uniformly as `t → 0⁺`, for every continuous
`f`.

articles.title: Generator on polynomials
articles.statement:
For every polynomial `p`,
`(wfSemigroup t p - p) / t → x (1 - x) / 2 · p''` uniformly on `[0, 1]` as `t → 0⁺`.

## Sources

- Ethier & Kurtz (1986), ch. 10; Durrett (2008), §7.

articles.title: Convergence on polynomials
articles.statement:
For `t ≥ 0` and every polynomial `p`, `⌊tM⌋` generations
of the Wright–Fisher chain with `M` gene copies applied to `p` converge uniformly on `[0, 1]` to
`polySemigroup t p` as `M → ∞` (moment duality plus Kingman's theorem for the lineage count).

articles.title: Diffusion approximation of the transition operators (Trotter–Kato, concrete form)
articles.statement:
For
every continuous `f`, `⌊tM⌋` generations of the neutral Wright–Fisher chain with `M` gene copies
applied to `f` converge uniformly on `[0, 1]` to `wfSemigroup t f`.

## Sources

- Ethier & Kurtz (1986), ch. 1, §6 (approximation theorems), and ch. 10.

articles.title: Semigroup law
articles.statement: **Semigroup law** for `s, t ≥ 0`.

articles.title: Wright–Fisher diffusion semigroup fixes constants
articles.statement: The diffusion semigroup fixes constants (it is Markov: total mass `1`).

articles.title: Fourth-moment Kolmogorov bound for the Wright–Fisher semigroup
articles.statement:
The fourth centered increment of the neutral Wright–Fisher semigroup satisfies the uniform
Kolmogorov bound `T_t[(y-x)⁴](x) ≤ (3/16)t²`.

articles.title: Positivity
articles.statement: The diffusion semigroup maps nonnegative functions to nonnegative functions.

articles.title: Wright–Fisher semigroup at nonpositive times is the identity
articles.statement:
For `t ≤ 0`, `wfSemigroup t` is the identity (at `t = 0` by definition of a semigroup; for
`t < 0` this is a junk value of the definition).

articles.title: Semigroup law for the positive Wright–Fisher operator
articles.statement: The positive-operator form of the Wright–Fisher semigroup law.

articles.title: Positive Wright–Fisher operator fixes constants
articles.statement: The positive Wright–Fisher operator fixes the constant function `1`.

articles.title: Action of the positive Wright–Fisher operator
articles.statement: Bundling the operator as positive leaves its action on continuous functions unchanged.

articles.title: Wright–Fisher semigroup as a positive operator
articles.statement: The Wright–Fisher semigroup bundled as a positive continuous linear operator.

articles.title: Second-moment bound for the Wright–Fisher semigroup
articles.statement: The centered second moment grows at most linearly: `T_t[(y-x)²](x) ≤ t/4`.

articles.title: Diffusion semigroup agrees with the dual semigroup on polynomials
articles.statement: On polynomials the diffusion semigroup is the dual semigroup, for `t ≥ 0`.

articles.title: Moment duality for the diffusion
articles.statement:
**Moment duality for the diffusion** (Ethier & Griffiths 1993). For `t ≥ 0`, the semigroup
applied to `x ↦ x ^ n` is `∑_k P_t(n → k) x^k`, with `P_t = exp (t • G)` the transition matrix of
Kingman's block-counting process `A`; in process language `E_x[(X_t)^n] = E_n[x^{A_t}]` (the
processes themselves are not constructed here).

articles.title: Wright–Fisher diffusion semigroup at time zero is the identity
articles.statement: At time `0` the diffusion semigroup is the identity.

articles.title: Neutral Wright–Fisher diffusion semigroup
articles.statement:
The neutral Wright–Fisher diffusion semigroup on `C([0, 1], ℝ)`, time in units of `M = 2N`
generations: `wfSemigroup t f` is the uniform limit of `(wfStep M)^⌊tM⌋ f` as `M → ∞`
(`tendsto_wfStep_pow_floor`). For `t < 0` it is the identity (a junk value: `⌊tM⌋₊ = 0`).

articles.title: One Wright–Fisher generation fixes constants
articles.statement: One Wright–Fisher generation fixes the constant function `1`.

articles.title: Wright–Fisher step is the Bernstein operator
articles.statement: `wfStep M` is the Bernstein approximation operator.

articles.title: One Wright–Fisher generation preserves nonnegativity
articles.statement: One Wright–Fisher generation maps nonnegative functions to nonnegative functions.

articles.title: Moment duality, `m` generations
articles.statement:
For `M ≥ 1` and `n ≤ N`, `m` generations of the
Wright–Fisher chain map `x ^ n` to `∑_k ((wfLineageMatrix N M)^m) n k · x^k`: the `n`-th moment
of the frequency after `m` generations is the generating function of the number of ancestors,
`m` generations back, of `n` sampled genes.

articles.title: One Wright–Fisher generation acting on monomials
articles.statement: One generation maps `x ^ n` to `∑_k wfLineageProb M n k x ^ k`.

articles.title: One generation of the neutral Wright–Fisher chain
articles.statement:
One generation of the neutral Wright–Fisher chain with `M` gene copies, acting on continuous
functions of the allele frequency: `(wfStep M f)(x) = ∑_k f(k/M) C(M, k) x^k (1 - x)^(M - k)`,
which for `M ≥ 1` is the expected value of `f` at the next frequency `Bin(M, x) / M` (the `M`-th
Bernstein operator, Mathlib's `bernsteinApproximation`; the expectation is
`ProbabilityTheory.integral_binomial`). It is a linear
contraction. At `M = 0` it returns the constant `f 0` (Lean's `k / 0 = 0`; no population).

articles.title: Chapman–Kolmogorov equation for the Wright–Fisher diffusion
articles.statement:
Chapman–Kolmogorov law for the Wright–Fisher transition kernels. With Mathlib's convention,
`K_t ∘ₖ K_s` first evolves for time `s` and then for time `t`.

articles.title: Wright–Fisher transition kernel is the identity at nonpositive times
articles.statement: For nonpositive times, the Wright–Fisher transition is the identity kernel.

articles.title: Wright–Fisher transitions at time zero are Dirac masses
articles.statement: Pointwise identity law for the transition kernel at time zero.

articles.title: Wright–Fisher transition kernel is the identity at time zero
articles.statement: At time zero the Wright–Fisher transition is the identity kernel.

articles.title: Transition kernel of the neutral Wright–Fisher diffusion
articles.statement:
The transition kernel of the neutral Wright–Fisher diffusion at time `t`. For nonnegative `t`
it is the probabilistic transition corresponding to `wfSemigroup t`; for negative `t`, both the
operator and kernel are the identity junk value inherited from `wfSemigroup`.

articles.title: Allelic partition of a set partition
articles.statement:
The allelic partition of a set partition of `Fin n`: the multiset of its block sizes, a
partition of the integer `n`.

articles.title: Removing the last customer undoes a seating
articles.statement:
Removing the last customer undoes every seating: restricting `seat π c` to the first `n`
customers gives back `π`.

articles.title: Law of the Chinese restaurant process
articles.statement:
**Law of the Chinese restaurant process** (Pitman 2006, §3.1):
`P(π) = θ^{|π|} ∏_{B ∈ π} (|B| - 1)! / θ^{(n)}`.

articles.title: Exchangeability
articles.statement:
**Exchangeability**, pointwise: relabeling the customers by a permutation `σ` does not
change the probability of a partition.

articles.title: The block sizes follow Hoppe's urn
articles.statement:
The law of the multiset of block sizes after `n`
customers is the law `Ewens.hoppeLaw` of Hoppe's urn on allelic partitions after `n` draws.

articles.title: The allelic partition of the Chinese restaurant process follows the Ewens sampling formula
articles.statement:
**The allelic partition of the Chinese restaurant process follows the Ewens sampling
formula** (Ewens 1972; Hoppe 1984): the multiset of block sizes after `n` customers has law
`Ewens.ewensProb θ`.

articles.title: Exchangeability of the Chinese restaurant process
articles.statement:
**Exchangeability of the Chinese restaurant process** (Aldous 1985, §11): the law of the
partition relabeled by any permutation of the customers is the law of the partition.

articles.title: Consistency for every sample size
articles.statement:
Restricting the random partition of `Fin n` to the
first `m ≤ n` customers gives the process with `m` customers.

articles.title: Consistency of the Chinese restaurant process
articles.statement:
Restricting the random partition of
`Fin (n + 1)` to the first `n` customers gives the process with `n` customers.

articles.title: Seating multiplies the closed-form law by the seating probability
articles.statement: One seating multiplies the closed-form law by the seating probability.

articles.title: Closed-form law of the Chinese restaurant process
articles.statement:
The closed-form law of the Chinese restaurant process,
`θ^{|π|} ∏_{B ∈ π} (|B| - 1)! / θ^{(n)}` (Pitman 2006, §3.1). Every block is nonempty,
so `|B| - 1` is never a truncated natural subtraction.

articles.title: One step of the Chinese restaurant process
articles.statement:
One step of the Chinese restaurant process: the law of the partition of `Fin (n + 1)`
given the partition `π` of the first `n` customers.

articles.title: Chinese restaurant process law as a real number
articles.statement: The law of the Chinese restaurant process as a real number.

articles.title: Chinese restaurant process
articles.statement:
The **Chinese restaurant process** with parameter `θ > 0`: the law of the random
partition of the customers `Fin n` into tables, built one customer at a time by `crpStep`
(Aldous 1985, §11; Pitman 2006, ch. 3).

articles.title: Nonnegativity of the Ewens sampling formula
articles.statement:
The Ewens sampling formula is nonnegative for `θ > 0`; with `sum_ewensProb` it is a
probability distribution on the partitions of `n`.

articles.title: Ewens sampling formula
articles.statement:
The **Ewens sampling formula**: the probability, under the neutral infinite-alleles model
with scaled mutation rate `θ = 4Nu`, that a sample of `n` genes has allelic partition `π`
(`π.parts.count j` alleles carried by exactly `j` genes each):
`n! * (∏ j, (θ / j) ^ (a j) / (a j)!) / θ^{(n)}` (Ewens 1972), for `θ > 0`.

articles.title: Every partition arises from seating the last customer
articles.statement:
Every partition of `Fin (n + 1)` arises by seating customer `n` into its restriction to
the first `n` customers.

articles.title: Hoppe's urn generates the Ewens sampling formula
articles.statement:
**Hoppe's urn generates the Ewens sampling formula** (Hoppe 1984): after `n` draws, the
allelic partition has law `ewensProb θ`.

articles.title: Nonnegativity of the Hoppe urn law
articles.statement: The law of Hoppe's urn after `n` draws is nonnegative for `θ > 0`.

articles.title: Law of the allelic partition from Hoppe's urn
articles.statement:
The law of the allelic partition after `n` draws from Hoppe's urn, started from the empty
sample: `hoppeLaw θ (n + 1) π' = ∑ π, hoppeLaw θ n π * hoppeStep θ π π'`.

articles.title: Hoppe urn transition probabilities are nonnegative
articles.statement: Hoppe-urn transition probabilities are nonnegative.

articles.title: One step of Hoppe's urn
articles.statement:
One step of **Hoppe's urn** on allelic partitions (Hoppe 1984): from a partition `π` of
`k`, the next gene carries a new allele with probability `θ / (θ + k)` (target parts
`1 ::ₘ π.parts`), and copies an allele carried by `j` genes with probability
`j * a j / (θ + k)`, where `a j = π.parts.count j` (target parts
`(j + 1) ::ₘ π.parts.erase j`). The value is the transition probability from `π` to `π'`.

articles.title: Seating a customer at an occupied table
articles.statement:
Seat customer `n` at the occupied table `B` of `π`: the block `B` becomes `B ∪ {n}` and
the other blocks are unchanged.

articles.title: Seating a customer at a new table
articles.statement:
Seat customer `n` at a new table: the partition of `Fin (n + 1)` whose blocks are the
blocks of `π` (relabeled into `Fin (n + 1)`) together with the singleton `{n}`.

articles.title: Blocks of the partition after joining a table
articles.statement: The blocks of `joinTable π B hB`.

articles.title: Blocks of the partition after opening a new table
articles.statement: The blocks of `newTable π`.

articles.title: Seating choice distribution of a customer
articles.statement: The seating choice of customer `n`, as a probability distribution.

articles.title: Injectivity of seating
articles.statement: Different seating choices give different partitions.

articles.title: Nonnegativity of seating probabilities
articles.statement: The seating probabilities are nonnegative for `θ > 0`.

articles.title: Seating probabilities in the Chinese restaurant process
articles.statement:
The probability of each seating choice for customer `n` given the partition `π` of the
first `n` customers: `θ / (n + θ)` for a new table, `|B| / (n + θ)` for the table `B`.

articles.title: Seating a customer by a seating choice
articles.statement:
Seat customer `n` according to the choice `c`: `none` opens a new table, `some B` joins
the occupied table `B`.

articles.title: Expected number of tables
articles.statement:
**Expected number of tables** (expected number of alleles in a sample of `n` genes,
Ewens 1972): `E[|π|] = ∑_{i < n} θ / (θ + i)`.

articles.title: Expected number of alleles
articles.statement:
**Expected number of alleles** in a sample of `n` genes under the Ewens sampling formula:
`E[K_n] = ∑_{i < n} θ / (θ + i)` (Ewens 1972).

articles.title: The Ewens sampling formula is a probability distribution
articles.statement:
**The Ewens sampling formula is a probability distribution** on the partitions of `n`
(Ewens 1972; equivalently, Cauchy's cycle-type formula `∑_{σ ∈ S_n} θ^{#cycles σ} = θ^{(n)}`).

articles.title: Hoppe urn transition is stochastic
articles.statement:
The Hoppe-urn transition is stochastic: from every partition of `k` the probabilities of
the partitions of `k + 1` sum to one.

articles.title: Seating probabilities sum to one
articles.statement: The seating probabilities sum to one for `θ > 0`.

articles.title: Mean of the Poisson distribution
articles.statement: The Poisson(`r`) law has mean `r`.

articles.title: Haldane's equation for the survival probability
articles.statement: `π(s)` solves Haldane's equation `1 - π = exp (-(1 + s) π)`.

articles.title: Generating function of the Poisson distribution
articles.statement: The Poisson(`r`) generating function: `∑ e^{-r} r^k / k! x^k = exp (r (x - 1))`.

articles.title: Survival probability is less than one
articles.statement:
The survival probability is less than `1`: the mutant leaves no copies with positive
probability `exp (-(1 + s))`. (For `s < -1`, outside the model, `π(s) = 0`.)

articles.title: Nonnegativity of the survival probability
articles.statement: The survival probability is non-negative.

articles.title: Beneficial mutant survives with positive probability
articles.statement: A beneficial mutant survives with positive probability.

articles.title: Haldane's survival probability of a mutant
articles.statement:
Haldane's survival probability `π(s) = 1 - q(s)` of a mutant with selective advantage `s`
per generation, whose number of copies in the next generation is Poisson with mean `1 + s`.
The model needs `s ≥ -1`; for `s < -1` the mean is truncated to `0` (`Real.toNNReal`), the
mutant leaves no copies, and `π(s) = 0`.

articles.title: Haldane's approximation $\pi(s) \approx 2s$
articles.statement: Haldane's approximation (Haldane 1927): `π(s) / s → 2` as `s → 0⁺`.

articles.title: The two allele frequencies sum to one
articles.statement: The two allele frequencies sum to one: `p + q = 1`.

articles.title: Gamete law equals the allele frequency
articles.statement:
The gamete law is the allele frequency: `gamete G a = ½ ∑ b, G (a, b) + ½ ∑ b, G (b, a)`,
half the expected number of copies of `a` in a parental genotype.

articles.title: Allele frequencies are conserved
articles.statement:
**Allele frequencies are conserved** under random mating: the gamete law of the offspring
equals that of the parents.

articles.title: Law of a random gamete
articles.statement:
The law of a random gamete of a generation with genotype law `G`: pick a parent from `G`,
then one of its two alleles by `transmit`. Its mass at `a` is the frequency of allele `a`
(`gamete_apply`).

articles.title: Hardy–Weinberg proportions after one generation of random mating
articles.statement:
The deviation from Hardy–Weinberg proportions vanishes after one generation of random
mating, whatever the parental genotype law.

articles.title: Deviation from Hardy–Weinberg proportions
articles.statement:
The deviation `D = P(AA) - p²` of a biallelic genotype law from Hardy–Weinberg
proportions, where `p` is the frequency of allele `A` (`true`).

articles.title: Hardy–Weinberg proportions
articles.statement:
**Hardy–Weinberg proportions** (Hardy 1908, Weinberg 1908): after one generation of random
mating the genotype law is the product `p ⊗ p` of the parental allele frequencies
`p = gamete G`.

articles.title: Hardy–Weinberg frequency $q^2$ of the aa homozygote
articles.statement: After one generation of random mating the homozygote `aa` has frequency `q²`.

articles.title: Hardy–Weinberg frequency $2pq$ of the heterozygote
articles.statement:
After one generation of random mating the (unordered) heterozygote `Aa`, i.e. the two
ordered genotypes `(A, a)` and `(a, A)`, has frequency `2pq`.

articles.title: Hardy–Weinberg equilibrium
articles.statement:
The Hardy–Weinberg proportions reached after one generation
of random mating are a fixed point of random mating.

articles.title: Hardy–Weinberg frequency $p^2$ of the AA homozygote
articles.statement: After one generation of random mating the homozygote `AA` has frequency `p²`.

articles.title: Offspring genotype law under random union of gametes
articles.statement:
The offspring genotype law under random union of gametes: the maternal and paternal
alleles are independent gametes of the parental generation.

articles.title: Allele transmission law of a parental genotype
articles.statement:
`transmit g` puts mass `1/2` on each of the two alleles of `g` (mass `1` on `a` for a
homozygote `g = (a, a)`).

articles.title: Mendel's law of segregation
articles.statement:
Mendel's law of segregation: a parent with genotype `g` transmits its maternal allele `g.1`
or its paternal allele `g.2`, each with probability `1/2`.

articles.title: Equilibrium homozygosity in the infinite-alleles model
articles.statement:
The equilibrium homozygosity `F* = (1 - u)² / (M - (M - 1)(1 - u)²)`. Biologically meaningful
for `2 ≤ M`; its denominator is positive for `1 ≤ M` and `0 < u ≤ 1`, the hypotheses of the
theorems below (`M = 1` being an algebraic extension).

articles.title: Equilibrium homozygosity is a fixed point of the recursion
articles.statement: `F*` is a fixed point of the homozygosity recursion.

articles.title: Uniqueness of the equilibrium homozygosity
articles.statement: For `0 < u ≤ 1`, `F*` is the unique fixed point of the homozygosity recursion.

articles.title: Homozygosity recursion in the infinite-alleles model
articles.statement:
One generation of drift and mutation in the infinite-alleles model with `M` gene copies and
mutation probability `u` per copy: `F' = (1 - u)² (1/M + (1 - 1/M) F)`. The model domain is
`2 ≤ M` (two distinct copies must exist) and `0 ≤ u ≤ 1`; the theorems below assume only
`1 ≤ M`, and `M = 1` is an algebraic extension with no biological meaning. For `M = 0` the
definition uses the junk value `1/0 = 0`.

articles.title: Kimura–Crow limit
articles.statement:
With `M = 2N` gene copies and mutation probability `u = θ/(4N)`
(so that `θ = 4Nu`), the equilibrium homozygosity tends to `1/(1 + θ)` as `N → ∞`.

articles.title: Convergence of homozygosity to equilibrium
articles.statement: For `0 < u ≤ 1` the homozygosity converges to `F*` from every initial value `F₀`.

articles.title: Limit $\theta/(1+\theta)$ of the equilibrium heterozygosity
articles.statement:
The equilibrium heterozygosity `H* = 1 - F*` tends to `θ/(1 + θ)` as `N → ∞` with
`M = 2N` and `u = θ/(4N)`.

articles.title: Recombination preserves first-locus allele frequencies
articles.statement:
Allele frequencies at the first locus are unchanged by random mating (for every real
`r`).

articles.title: Allele frequency at the first locus
articles.statement: The frequency `∑ b, x (a, b)` of allele `a` at the first locus.

articles.title: Recombination preserves second-locus allele frequencies
articles.statement:
Allele frequencies at the second locus are unchanged by random mating (for every real
`r`).

articles.title: Allele frequency at the second locus
articles.statement: The frequency `∑ a, x (a, b)` of allele `b` at the second locus.

articles.title: Haldane's recombination fraction is below one half
articles.statement: The recombination fraction is always below `1/2` (for every real `d`).

articles.title: Every recombination fraction below one half is attained
articles.statement:
Every `r < 1/2` is the recombination fraction at the distance `-½ log(1 - 2r)`. The
hypothesis keeps `log` on positive arguments: at `r = 1/2` the right side would use the junk
value `log 0 = 0`. The distance is nonnegative exactly when `0 ≤ r`.

articles.title: Nonnegativity of Haldane's map function
articles.statement: Haldane's map function is nonnegative at nonnegative distances.

articles.title: Haldane's map function
articles.statement:
Haldane's map function `r(d) = (1 - e^{-2d}) / 2`: the recombination fraction between two
loci at map distance `d` Morgans when crossovers form a Poisson process (no interference).

articles.title: Series for the probability of an odd Poisson count
articles.statement:
The probability that a Poisson count of mean `d` is odd, as a series:
`∑_{k odd} e^{-d} d^k / k! = (1 - e^{-2d}) / 2` (Haldane 1919). The series identity holds for
every real `d`; it is a probability for `0 ≤ d`.

articles.title: Linkage disequilibrium after $t$ generations
articles.statement: After `t` generations, `D_t = (1 - r)^t D_0`.

articles.title: Linkage disequilibrium decays by the factor $1 - r$
articles.statement:
Linkage disequilibrium decays by the factor `1 - r` per generation: `D' = (1 - r) D`
(for every real `r`).

articles.title: Linkage disequilibrium of a two-locus gamete law
articles.statement: The linkage disequilibrium `D = x_AB x_ab - x_Ab x_aB`.

articles.title: Inverse Haldane map function recovers map distance
articles.statement: The inverse map function `d = -½ log(1 - 2r)` recovers the map distance.

articles.title: Haldane's map function from Poisson crossovers
articles.statement:
Haldane's map function (Haldane 1919): if the number of crossovers in an interval of map
length `d` Morgans is Poisson with mean `d`, the probability of an odd number of crossovers,
i.e. of recombination between the ends of the interval, is `(1 - e^{-2d}) / 2`.

articles.title: Classical form of the recombination recursion
articles.statement:
The classical form of the recursion: coupling gametes (`AB`, `ab`) lose `r D` and repulsion
gametes (`Ab`, `aB`) gain `r D`. This identity holds for every real `r`; the biological domain
is `0 ≤ r ≤ 1/2`.

articles.title: Recombination preserves nonnegativity of gamete frequencies
articles.statement: Recombination keeps gamete frequencies nonnegative for `0 ≤ r ≤ 1`.

articles.title: Random mating with recombination
articles.statement:
One generation of random mating with recombination fraction `r`:
`recombine r x g = (1 - r) x_g + r p_{g.1} q_{g.2}`.

articles.title: Recombination preserves total gamete frequency
articles.statement: Recombination keeps gamete frequencies summing to `1`.

articles.title: Distant loci are unlinked in the limit
articles.statement: Loci far apart are unlinked in the limit: `r → 1/2` as `d → ∞`.

articles.title: Linkage disequilibrium tends to zero
articles.statement:
Linkage disequilibrium tends to `0` whenever `0 < r ≤ 1`; this contains the biological
range `0 < r ≤ 1/2`. For `r = 0` (complete linkage) `D` is constant.

articles.title: Closed form of the clone-size generating function
articles.statement: The clone-size generating function `h(z) = 1 + (1 / z - 1) log (1 - z)`.

articles.title: Lea–Coulson clone-size law
articles.statement:
The **Lea–Coulson clone-size law** `P(size = j) = 1 / (j (j + 1))` for `j ≥ 1`
(`P(size = 0) = 0`).

articles.title: Convolution power of a sequence on the naturals
articles.statement:
The `k`-fold convolution power of a sequence on `ℕ`: `p^{*0} = δ₀` and
`p^{*(k+1)}(n) = ∑_{i ≤ n} p(i) p^{*k}(n - i)`.

articles.title: Power form of the Lea–Coulson generating function
articles.statement:
The Lea–Coulson generating function in power form:
`exp (m (1 / z - 1) log (1 - z)) = (1 - z)^{m (1 - z) / z}` for `z < 1`, `z ≠ 0`.

articles.title: Clone-size generating function
The clone-size law sums to one
articles.statement: The clone-size law sums to `1`.

articles.title: Lea–Coulson generating function
articles.statement:
For `m ≥ 0` and `0 < z < 1`,
`∑ₙ pₙ zⁿ = exp (m (h(z) - 1)) = exp (m (1 / z - 1) log (1 - z))`.

articles.title: The Luria–Delbrück probabilities sum to one
articles.statement: The Luria–Delbrück probabilities sum to `1` (for `m ≥ 0`).

articles.title: Clone-size law from the founding-time density
articles.statement:
A clone founded `τ` before the end has
geometric size `e^{-τ} (1 - e^{-τ})^{j-1}`; mixing over the founding-time density `e^{-τ}` on
`(0, ∞)` gives `1 / (j (j + 1))` for `j ≥ 1`.

articles.title: Nonnegativity of Luria–Delbrück probabilities
articles.statement: The Luria–Delbrück probabilities are nonnegative for `m ≥ 0`.

articles.title: Ma–Sandri–Sarkar recursion
articles.statement:
For `n ≥ 1`,
`pₙ = (m / n) ∑_{i < n} pᵢ / (n - i + 1)` (all real `m`).

articles.title: `p₀`
articles.statement: The probability of no mutants is `e^{-m}`.

articles.title: Luria–Delbrück distribution
articles.statement:
The **Luria–Delbrück probability** of `n` mutants with expected mutation number `m`: the
compound-Poisson law `∑_k e^{-m} m^k / k! · cloneProb^{*k}(n)`. Since clones have size at
least `1`, only `k ≤ n` contribute.

articles.title: The `p₀` method
articles.statement:
**The `p₀` method** (Luria–Delbrück 1943): the expected number of mutations is recovered
from the proportion of cultures with no mutants, `m = -log p₀`.

articles.title: Uniqueness of the fixation probability
articles.statement:
Any `ψ` with `ψ 0 = 0`, `ψ N = 1` that satisfies
the first-step equation `ψ i = a_i ψ (i+1) + b_i ψ (i-1) + (1 - a_i - b_i) ψ i` at every
`0 < i < N` equals `moranFixation r N` on `0 ≤ i ≤ N`.

articles.title: Closed form of Kimura's fixation probability
articles.statement:
Kimura's diffusion fixation probability at scaled selection `σ / 2` is
`(1 - e^{-σ x}) / (1 - e^{-σ})` (for `σ ≠ 0`).

articles.title: Nonnegativity of the Moran down-step probability
articles.statement: The down-step probability is nonnegative on the states `0 ≤ i ≤ N`.

articles.title: No down-step from the empty state of the Moran process
articles.statement: No mutant can be removed when the mutant type is absent.

articles.title: Down-step probability of the Moran process
articles.statement:
Probability that one step of the Moran process takes the mutant count from `i` to `i - 1`:
a wild type is chosen to reproduce (probability `(N - i) / (r i + N - i)`) and a mutant is
chosen to die (probability `i / N`). Meaningful for `0 < r` and `i ≤ N`.

articles.title: First-step equation (Moran 1958)
articles.statement:
The fixation probability satisfies
`φ_i = a_i φ_{i+1} + b_i φ_{i-1} + (1 - a_i - b_i) φ_i`. This is the first-step equation of the
chain for the interior states `0 < i < N`; the identity is algebraic (it follows from
`r · b_i = a_i`), so it is stated for every `i ≥ 1`.

articles.title: A fixed mutant stays fixed
articles.statement: A mutant that is already fixed stays fixed: `φ_N = 1` (for `N ≠ 0`).

articles.title: An absent mutant is never fixed
articles.statement: A mutant that is absent is never fixed: `φ_0 = 0`.

articles.title: Fixation probability of the Moran process
articles.statement:
The fixation probability of the Moran process started from `i` mutants out of `N`:
`(1 - r⁻¹ ^ i) / (1 - r⁻¹ ^ N)` for `r ≠ 1`, and `i / N` in the neutral case `r = 1`.
The model's domain is `0 < r`, `N ≥ 1`, `i ≤ N`; outside it the value is the closed formula
evaluated with Lean's total division (e.g. `x / 0 = 0`) and carries no meaning.

articles.title: Moran process as a stochastic matrix
articles.statement:
The Moran process with `N` individuals and mutant relative fitness `r > 0`, as a stochastic
matrix on the mutant counts `Fin (N + 1)`.

articles.title: One-step transition probabilities of the Moran process
articles.statement:
One-step transition probabilities of the Moran process on the states `Fin (N + 1)`:
`a_i` to `i + 1`, `b_i` to `i - 1`, `1 - a_i - b_i` to `i`, and `0` elsewhere.

articles.title: Moran up- and down-step probabilities sum to at most one
articles.statement:
On the states `0 ≤ i ≤ N` the up- and down-step probabilities sum to at most `1`, so
the probability `1 - a_i - b_i` of staying is nonnegative.

articles.title: No up-step from the fixed state of the Moran process
articles.statement: No mutant can be added when the mutant type is fixed.

articles.title: Nonnegativity of the Moran up-step probability
articles.statement: The up-step probability is nonnegative on the states `0 ≤ i ≤ N`.

articles.title: Up-step probability of the Moran process
articles.statement:
Probability that one step of the Moran process with `N` individuals and mutant relative
fitness `r` takes the mutant count from `i` to `i + 1`: a mutant is chosen to reproduce
(probability `r i / (r i + N - i)`) and a wild type is chosen to die (probability
`(N - i) / N`). Meaningful for `0 < r` and `i ≤ N` (the real subtraction `N - i` is negative
for `i > N`).

articles.title: Ratio of Moran down- and up-step probabilities
articles.statement: The ratio of the down- and up-step probabilities is `1 / r`: `r · b_i = a_i`.

articles.title: One-step expectation under the Moran process
articles.statement:
One-step expectation of a function `f` of the mutant count from state `i`:
`∑ j, P i j f j = a_i f (i + 1) + b_i f (i - 1) + (1 - a_i - b_i) f i` (the boundary terms
vanish at `i = 0` and `i = N`).

articles.title: Fixation probability of the chain
articles.statement:
For `N ≠ 0`, the probability that the Moran chain
started at `i` is in state `N` after `t` steps tends to `φ_i` as `t → ∞`. Since `N` absorbs,
this `t`-step probability is the probability of fixation by time `t`, so its limit is the
probability of eventual fixation.

articles.title: Loss probability of the chain
articles.statement:
For `N ≠ 0`, the probability that the Moran chain
started at `i` is in state `0` after `t` steps tends to `1 - φ_i`; together with
`tendsto_matPow_moranMatrix_last`, absorption at `0` or `N` is certain.

articles.title: Diffusion limit of the Moran fixation probability
articles.statement:
With relative fitness
`r_N = 1 + σ / N` and initial count `i_N = ⌊x N⌋`, the fixation probability `φ^{(N)}_{i_N}`
tends to Kimura's `kimuraFixation (σ / 2) x`, which is `(1 - e^{-σ x}) / (1 - e^{-σ})` for
`σ ≠ 0` (`kimuraFixation_half`) and `x` for `σ = 0`. The initial frequency `x` is meaningful in
`[0, 1]`; the limit of the closed formula holds for every `x ≥ 0`, so only `0 ≤ x` is assumed
(for negative `x`, `⌊x N⌋₊ = 0` is a junk value of the truncated floor).

articles.title: At equilibrium the de novo fraction is `s_het`
articles.statement: **At equilibrium the de novo fraction is `s_het`.**

articles.title: Fraction of de novo loss-of-function alleles
articles.statement:
The fraction of LoF alleles in the next generation that are new mutations, from
frequency `x`: `U / ((1 - s) x + U)`.

articles.title: `U / s` is an equilibrium
articles.statement:
**`U / s` is an equilibrium** of the multiplicative diploid model (an algebraic identity for
`s ≠ 0`, `U ≠ 1`; a frequency in `[0, 1]` when `0 ≤ U ≤ s`).

articles.title: One diploid generation of selection and mutation
articles.statement: One generation: selection, then mutation of wild-type alleles at rate `U`.

articles.title: Transition kernel entries are probabilities
articles.statement: The kernel entries are probabilities when the sampling probability is in `[0, 1]`.

articles.title: Binomial transition kernel for loss-of-function counts
articles.statement:
The transition probability from `i` LoF copies among `N` to `j` copies among `N'`: binomial
sampling of `N'` copies with success probability `(1 - s)(i / N) + U`.

articles.title: Law of the loss-of-function count under any demography
articles.statement:
The law of the LoF count in generation `t` for population sizes `N t` (any demography),
started from `μ₀`.

articles.title: Equilibria lie at or below `U / s`
articles.statement:
**Equilibria lie at or below `U / s`** when homozygotes are at least multiplicatively unfit
(`2s - s² ≤ t`, which includes recessive lethality `t = 1`): every fixed point `q ∈ [0, 1)` of
the diploid map satisfies `q ≤ U / s`.

articles.title: Unique fixed point $U/s$ of the linear recursion
articles.statement: `U / s` is the unique fixed point.

articles.title: Closed-form orbit of the linear mutation–selection recursion
articles.statement: Closed-form orbit: `x_t = U / s + (1 - s)^t (x_0 - U / s)`.

articles.title: Linear mutation–selection recursion
articles.statement: One generation of the linear model: `x ↦ (1 - s) x + U`.

articles.title: Haldane–Muller load
articles.statement:
`1 - w̄ = 2U - U²` at the multiplicative equilibrium
(`U ≠ 1`, so `U / s` is a fixed point).

articles.title: Mean fitness at the multiplicative mutation–selection equilibrium
articles.statement:
At the multiplicative equilibrium the mean fitness is `(1 - U)²`, independent of `s`.
Requires `U ≠ 1`, so that `U / s` is genuinely a fixed point (`diploidStep_mult_fixed`):
for `U = 1` the point `U / s` is not an equilibrium.

articles.title: Mean fitness under multiplicative fitness
articles.statement: With multiplicative fitness, `w̄ = (1 - s q)²` for every `q`.

articles.title: Positivity of mean fitness for allele frequencies below one
articles.statement: Mean fitness is positive for `0 ≤ q < 1` and `s, t ≤ 1` (nonnegative fitnesses).

articles.title: Mean fitness under Hardy–Weinberg proportions
articles.statement:
Mean fitness under Hardy–Weinberg with LoF frequency `q` and fitnesses `1, 1 - s, 1 - t`:
`1 - 2 q (1 - q) s - q² t`.

articles.title: Demography-free mean
articles.statement:
For every sequence of positive population sizes, `E[X_t]` follows
the deterministic linear recursion (derived from the binomial mean). The identity holds for all
real `s, U`; `law` is a probability law when `0 ≤ U ≤ s ≤ 1` and `μ₀` is one.

articles.title: Demography-free mean, one step
articles.statement:
For any sizes `N`, `N' > 0` and any distribution `μ`
of total mass one, the mean frequency after one generation is `(1 - s) m + U`.

articles.title: Mean loss-of-function frequency of a distribution
articles.statement: The mean LoF frequency `∑ μ_i (i / N)` of a distribution `μ` on `Fin (N + 1)`.

articles.title: One generation of the chain on distributions
articles.statement: One generation of the chain acting on distributions.

articles.title: Loss-of-function frequency after selection
articles.statement: LoF frequency after selection: `q (1 - s (1 - q) - t q) / w̄`.

articles.title: Binomial mean of the transition kernel
articles.statement: The binomial mean: `∑_j kernel(i, j) (j / N') = (1 - s)(i / N) + U` for `N' > 0`.

articles.title: Rows of the transition kernel have total mass one
articles.statement: The kernel rows have total mass one (for every real sampling probability).

articles.title: Pushing a distribution forward preserves total mass
articles.statement: Pushing a distribution forward preserves total mass.

articles.title: Global attraction
articles.statement: For `0 < s < 2` every orbit converges to `U / s`.

articles.title: Expected loss-of-function frequency converges to $U/s$
articles.statement: The expected LoF frequency converges to `U / s` under any demography.

articles.title: Positivity of diploid mean fitness
articles.statement: Diploid mean fitness is positive on the simplex when every genotype fitness is positive.

articles.title: Diploid mean fitness under Hardy–Weinberg proportions
articles.statement:
