The mean fitness `w̄ = ∑ i, ∑ j, p i * p j * w i j` of a population in Hardy–Weinberg
proportions with allele frequencies `p` and genotype fitnesses `w`.

articles.title: Diploid selection preserves nonnegative allele frequencies
articles.statement: Diploid viability selection keeps allele frequencies nonnegative.

articles.title: One generation of diploid viability selection
articles.statement:
One generation of diploid viability selection under random mating, followed by Mendelian
transmission of either allele of each survivor:
`diploidSelect p w i = p i * (∑ j, (w i j + w j i) / 2 * p j) / w̄`.

articles.title: Variance of fitness
articles.statement:
The variance of fitness `Var_p(w) = ∑ i, p i * (w i - w̄) ^ 2` under the type frequencies
`p`.

articles.title: Marginal fitness for symmetric genotype fitnesses
articles.statement:
For symmetric genotype fitnesses the marginal fitness is the row marginal
`∑ j, w i j * p j`.

articles.title: Marginal fitness of an allele
articles.statement:
The marginal fitness `∑ j, (w i j + w j i) / 2 * p j` of allele `i`: the mean fitness of a
genotype carrying `i` whose other allele is drawn from the frequencies `p`, averaging the two
positions at which `i` can sit in the ordered genotype.

articles.title: Mean fitness never decreases under haploid selection
articles.statement: Mean fitness never decreases under haploid selection (corollary of Fisher's theorem).

articles.title: Positivity of mean fitness on the simplex
articles.statement: Mean fitness is positive on the simplex when every fitness is positive.

articles.title: Fisher's fundamental theorem of natural selection
articles.statement:
Fisher's fundamental theorem of natural selection in its exact haploid, discrete-generation
form: the change in mean fitness over one generation of selection is the variance of fitness
divided by the mean fitness, `w̄(p') - w̄(p) = Var_p(w) / w̄(p)` (cf. Fisher 1930, who states the
theorem for the additive genetic variance). The identity needs only `∑ p = 1` and `w̄ ≠ 0`; the
model domain is the simplex with `w > 0` (`meanFitness_pos`).

articles.title: Mean fitness of a population
articles.statement:
The mean fitness `w̄ = ∑ i, p i * w i` of a population with type frequencies `p` and
fitnesses `w`.

articles.title: Price equation
articles.statement:
The Price equation (exact, finite population). Individual `i` has fitness `w i` (number of
offspring), trait value `z i`, and mean offspring trait value `z' i`. With population means
`w̄ = 𝔼 i, w i`, `z̄ = 𝔼 i, z i` and offspring mean trait `z̄' = ∑ i, w i * z' i / ∑ i, w i`,
`w̄ (z̄' - z̄) = Cov(w, z) + E[w (z' - z)]`, where `Cov` is the population covariance
(Price 1970). Nonnegativity of `w` is not needed; only a nonzero total offspring number.

articles.title: Haploid selection preserves nonnegative frequencies
articles.statement: Haploid selection keeps frequencies nonnegative.

articles.title: One generation of haploid selection
articles.statement: One generation of haploid selection: `select p w i = p i * w i / w̄`.

articles.title: Diploid selection preserves total allele frequency one
articles.statement: Diploid viability selection keeps allele frequencies summing to `1`.

articles.title: Haploid selection preserves total frequency one
articles.statement:
Haploid selection keeps the frequencies summing to `1` whenever `w̄ ≠ 0` (for `w̄ = 0`
the division by zero would give `0`).

articles.title: Allele frequency of a Wright–Fisher state
articles.statement:
The frequency of allele `A` in state `i` is `bernstein.z i = i / M` (for `M = 0` it is
Lean's junk value `i / 0 = 0`).

articles.title: Heterozygosity of a Wright–Fisher state
articles.statement:
The heterozygosity `H(j) = 2 (j/M) (1 - j/M)` of state `j`: the probability that two
gene copies drawn with replacement carry different alleles.

articles.title: Almost-sure absorption of the Wright–Fisher chain
articles.statement:
Almost-sure absorption: a Wright–Fisher chain is almost surely eventually absorbed in `0`
or `M` (Ewens 2004, ch. 3).

articles.title: Finite Wright–Fisher chain is absorbed almost surely
articles.statement:
The finite Wright–Fisher chain under the canonical Markov law almost surely
reaches an endpoint. The law and chain are not premises supplied by a caller.

articles.title: Fixation probability of a Wright–Fisher chain
articles.statement:
Path-level fixation probability (Ewens 2004, ch. 3): a Wright–Fisher chain started from `i`
copies ever reaches `M` (fixation of `A`) with probability `i / M`.

articles.title: Loss probability of a Wright–Fisher chain
articles.statement:
Path-level loss probability: a Wright–Fisher chain started from `i` copies ever reaches `0`
(loss of `A`) with probability `1 - i / M`.

articles.title: Loss probability of an allele in the finite Wright–Fisher chain
articles.statement:
Under the canonical finite Wright–Fisher law, the probability of ever losing
the allele at `0` equals `1 - i / M`.

articles.title: Fixation probability of the finite Wright–Fisher chain
articles.statement:
Under the canonical finite Wright–Fisher law, the probability of ever fixing
at `M` equals the initial allele frequency `i / M`.

articles.title: Geometric decay of heterozygosity under Wright–Fisher drift
articles.statement:
Heterozygosity decays geometrically (Ewens 2004, ch. 3):
`∑ j, P^t(i, j) H(j) = (1 - 1/M)^t H(i)`. For `M = 0` both sides are `0` because `H ≡ 0`
(the factor `1 - 1/0 = 1` is then irrelevant).

articles.title: Multi-step martingale property of the Wright–Fisher allele count
articles.statement: Martingale property of the allele count (`t` steps): `∑ j, P^t(i, j) j = i`.

articles.title: One-step decay of heterozygosity under Wright–Fisher drift
articles.statement:
Heterozygosity decays by the factor `1 - 1/M` per generation (one step). For `M = 0` both
sides are `0` because `H ≡ 0`.

articles.title: One-step martingale property of the Wright–Fisher allele count
articles.statement: Martingale property of the allele count (one step): `∑ j, P(i, j) j = i`.

articles.title: Interior Wright–Fisher states vanish in the limit
articles.statement: The probability of sitting in an interior state `0 < j < M` at time `t` tends to `0`.

articles.title: Fixation probability in the Wright–Fisher chain
articles.statement:
Fixation probability (Ewens 2004, ch. 3): started from `i` copies, allele `A` is fixed with
limiting probability `i / M`, i.e. `P^t(i, M) → i / M`.

articles.title: Limiting loss probability of the Wright–Fisher transition matrix
articles.statement:
Loss probability: started from `i` copies, allele `A` is lost with limiting probability
`1 - i / M`, i.e. `P^t(i, 0) → 1 - i / M`.

articles.title: Limiting fixation probability of a Wright–Fisher chain
articles.statement:
Path-level fixation probability: if `X` is a Wright–Fisher chain (in the sense of
`IsFiniteMarkovChain`) started from `i` copies, then `P(X_t = M) → i / M`.

articles.title: Wright–Fisher rows are binomial laws
articles.statement: The rows of the Wright–Fisher matrix are Mathlib's binomial laws `Bin(M, i/M)`.

articles.title: Fixation of an allele is absorbing in the Wright–Fisher chain
articles.statement: The state `M` (allele `A` fixed) is absorbing.

articles.title: Loss of an allele is absorbing in the Wright–Fisher chain
articles.statement: The state `0` (allele `A` lost) is absorbing.

articles.title: Entries of the Wright–Fisher matrix
articles.statement: Entries of the Wright–Fisher matrix.

articles.title: Neutral Wright–Fisher transition matrix
articles.statement:
The neutral Wright–Fisher transition matrix on `M` gene copies (Ewens 2004, ch. 3):
`P(i, j) = (M choose j) (i/M)^j (1 - i/M)^(M - j)`, the binomial law `Bin(M, i/M)` of the
number of `A` copies among `M` draws with replacement. The model needs `M ≥ 1`; for `M = 0`
(where `i / M` is Lean's junk value `0`) the matrix is the one-state chain, which is
`Bin(0, p) = δ₀` for every `p`.

articles.title: Uniqueness of the island-model fixed point
articles.statement: `F*` is the only fixed point of the island-model recursion.

articles.title: Positivity of the island-model equilibrium denominator
articles.statement:
The denominator `M - (M - 1) (1 - m) ^ 2` of the equilibrium is positive (at least `1`) for
`M ≥ 1` and `0 ≤ m ≤ 1`.

articles.title: Island-model equilibrium lies in (0, 1)
articles.statement: The equilibrium identity-by-descent probability lies in `[0, 1]`.

articles.title: Island-model equilibrium is below one under migration
articles.statement:
With migration (`0 < m ≤ 1`) the equilibrium identity-by-descent probability lies in
`[0, 1)`.

articles.title: Complete identity by descent in isolated demes
articles.statement: Isolated demes (`m = 0`): the equilibrium is complete identity by descent, `F* = 1`.

articles.title: Equilibrium $F_{ST}$ of Wright's island model
articles.statement:
The equilibrium identity-by-descent probability (Wright's `F_ST`) of the island model:
`F* = (1 - m) ^ 2 / (M - (M - 1) (1 - m) ^ 2)`. Biologically meaningful for `M ≥ 2` and
`0 ≤ m ≤ 1`; the denominator is positive already for `M ≥ 1` (`islandEquilibrium_denom_pos`),
where `M = 1` is an algebraic extension.

articles.title: Island-model contraction factor lies in (0, 1)
articles.statement:
For `M ≥ 1` and `0 ≤ m ≤ 1`, the per-generation contraction factor
`(1 - m) ^ 2 (1 - 1 / M)` lies in `[0, 1)`.

articles.title: Island-model equilibrium is a fixed point of the recursion
articles.statement: `F*` is a fixed point of the island-model recursion.

articles.title: Geometric approach to equilibrium
articles.statement:
After `t` generations,
`F_t - F* = ((1 - m) ^ 2 (1 - 1 / M)) ^ t (F_0 - F*)`.

articles.title: Identity-by-descent recursion in Wright's island model
articles.statement:
One generation of Wright's island-model identity-by-descent recursion for a deme of `M`
gene copies (`M = 2N` for `N` diploids) receiving a fraction `m` of migrants from an infinite
pool: `F' = (1 - m) ^ 2 * (1 / M + (1 - 1 / M) * F)`. Biologically meaningful for `M ≥ 2`
and `0 ≤ m ≤ 1`; `M = 1` is an algebraic extension (no pair of distinct copies exists), and at
`M = 0` Lean's `1 / 0 = 0` gives a junk value.

articles.title: Wright's `F_ST = 1 / (1 + 4 N m)` (Wright 1931)
articles.statement:
For demes of `N` diploids (`M = 2N`
gene copies) and migration fraction `m = κ / (4N)`, so that `4 N m = κ` is held fixed, the
equilibrium `F*` tends to `1 / (1 + κ)` as `N → ∞`.

articles.title: Convergence to equilibrium
articles.statement:
For `M ≥ 1` and `0 ≤ m ≤ 1`, the island-model recursion
converges to `F*` from every initial value `F₀`.

articles.title: Polarized ABBA site-pattern indicator
articles.statement:
Polarized `ABBA` indicator (Durand et al. 2011): `P1` and `O` ancestral, `P2` and `P3`
derived.

articles.title: Unpolarized ABBA site-pattern indicator
articles.statement:
Unpolarized `ABBA` indicator for populations `(P1, P2, P3, O)`: `P1` agrees with `O`, `P2`
with `P3`, and `P1` differs from `P2` (the patterns `ABBA` and `BAAB`).

articles.title: Polarized BABA site-pattern indicator
articles.statement:
Polarized `BABA` indicator (Durand et al. 2011): `P1` and `P3` derived, `P2` and `O`
ancestral.

articles.title: ABBA–BABA site-pattern identity
articles.statement:
The site-pattern identity: `1[BABA] - 1[ABBA] = (x₁ - x₂) (x₃ - x₄)` for every
configuration of derived-allele indicators.

articles.title: Unpolarized BABA site-pattern indicator
articles.statement:
Unpolarized `BABA` indicator for populations `(P1, P2, P3, O)`: `P1` agrees with `P3`, `P2`
with `O`, and `P1` differs from `P2` (the patterns `BABA` and `ABAB`).

articles.title: Probability of a derived-allele configuration
articles.statement:
Probability of the derived/ancestral configuration `x` when haplotype `i` is sampled
independently and carries the derived allele with probability `q i`.

articles.title: Unbiased f2 estimator
articles.statement:
The unbiased `f2` estimator of Patterson et al. (2012), Appendix:
`(â - b̂)² - â (1 - â) / (m_A - 1) - b̂ (1 - b̂) / (m_B - 1)` with `â = x_A / m_A`,
written as `(x_A / m_A - x_B / m_B)² - x_A (m_A - x_A) / (m_A² (m_A - 1)) - …`.

articles.title: Unbiased f3 estimator
articles.statement:
The unbiased `f3` estimator of Patterson et al. (2012), Appendix:
`(ĉ - â) (ĉ - b̂) - ĉ (1 - ĉ) / (m_C - 1)`.

articles.title: qpAdm model equation in the drift model
articles.statement:
If the lineage weights of `T` are an affine
combination `∑ k, w k • weight (S k)` of those of the sources (`∑ k, w k = 1`, weights of any
sign), then `f4 T X Y Z = ∑ k, w k * f4 (S k) X Y Z`.

articles.title: qpAdm model equation
articles.statement:
**qpAdm model equation** (Haak et al. 2015, Supplementary Information): if the target `T`
is an admixture of sources `S k` with weights `w k` summing to `1` (`p T = ∑ k, w k * p (S k)`
pointwise; the weights may be negative, as in fitted qpAdm models), then for all `X`, `Y`, `Z`,
`f4 T X Y Z = ∑ k, w k * f4 (S k) X Y Z`. The merged `DriftModel.f4_admixture_right` is a
two-source drift-model instance (mixture in the second pair, one source as fourth argument).

articles.title: Linearity of the f4-statistic in its first pair
articles.statement:
Linearity of `f4` in its first pair: if `p A - p B = ∑ l, c l * (p (C l) - p (D l))`
pointwise, then `f4 A B Y Z = ∑ l, c l * f4 (C l) (D l) Y Z`.

articles.title: f4 estimator
articles.statement:
The `f4` estimator `(â - b̂) (ĉ - d̂)`; it needs no correction for four distinct
populations.

articles.title: qpWave matrix of f4-statistics
articles.statement:
The qpWave matrix of left populations `L 0, …, L n` and right populations
`R 0, …, R r`: entry `(i, j)` is `f4 (L (i + 1)) (L 0) (R (j + 1)) (R 0)`.

articles.title: Unbiased heterozygosity estimator
articles.statement:
Unbiased estimator of `p (1 - p)` from `x` derived copies among `m` sampled copies:
`x (m - x) / (m (m - 1))` (meaningful for `m ≥ 2`).

articles.title: Estimator of Hudson's F_ST denominator
articles.statement:
Hudson's `F_ST` denominator estimator `â (1 - b̂) + b̂ (1 - â)` (Bhatia et al. 2013); the
numerator estimator is `f2Hat`.

articles.title: Hudson's F_ST denominator at one site
articles.statement:
Hudson's `F_ST` denominator at one site: `p_A (1 - p_B) + p_B (1 - p_A)`, the probability
that two copies, one from each population, differ. The numerator is `(p_A - p_B) ^ 2`.

articles.title: Hudson's F_ST lies between 0 and 1
articles.statement:
Hudson's `F_ST` lies in `[0, 1]` for frequencies in `[0, 1]`. (When the denominator vanishes
the junk value `0` also lies in `[0, 1]`, so no positivity hypothesis is needed.)

articles.title: Hudson's F_ST (ratio of averages)
articles.statement:
Hudson's `F_ST` over sites `s` in the ratio-of-averages form of Bhatia et al. (2013):
`∑ s, (p_A s - p_B s) ^ 2 / ∑ s, hudsonDen (p_A s) (p_B s)`. It is defined when the denominator
is positive (it vanishes only if every site is fixed for the same allele in both populations);
otherwise Lean's value `0` is a junk value.

articles.title: Sample allele frequency is unbiased
articles.statement:
The sample frequency is unbiased: for `X ~ Bin(m, p)` with `m ≥ 1`, `E[X / m] = p`. (For
`m = 0`, `X / 0 = 0` is a junk value, hence `m ≥ 1`.)

articles.title: Sampling expectation is an expectation of independent indicators
articles.statement:
`sampleExpect` is the expectation under independent sampling: if the derived-allele
indicators `X i` are independent random variables with `P(X i = true) = q i`, then
`E[g (X 0, …, X (n - 1))] = sampleExpect g q`.

articles.title: Unbiased `f2`
articles.statement:
**Unbiased `f2`** (Patterson et al. 2012, Appendix): with independent binomial samples
`X_A ~ Bin(m_A, p_A)`, `X_B ~ Bin(m_B, p_B)`, `m_A, m_B ≥ 2`,
`E[f2Hat] = (p_A - p_B) ^ 2`, the population `f2` at the site.

articles.title: Unbiased `f3`
articles.statement:
**Unbiased `f3`** (Patterson et al. 2012, Appendix): with pairwise independent binomial
samples, `m_C ≥ 2` and `m_A, m_B ≥ 1`, `E[f3Hat] = (p_C - p_A) (p_C - p_B)`.

articles.title: Unbiased `f4`
articles.statement:
For four populations sampled independently across the two pairs
(`m ≥ 1` each), `E[f4Hat] = (p_A - p_B) (p_C - p_D)`; no correction is needed.

articles.title: Unbiased heterozygosity
articles.statement:
For `X ~ Bin(m, p)` with `m ≥ 2`,
`E[X (m - X) / (m (m - 1))] = p (1 - p)`.

articles.title: Hudson's denominator is unbiased
articles.statement:
**Hudson's denominator is unbiased** (Bhatia et al. 2013): with independent binomial samples
(`m ≥ 1` each), `E[hudsonDenHat] = hudsonDen p_A p_B`.

articles.title: The unpolarized D-statistic numerator vanishes on a tree
articles.statement:
In the drift model, if no edge
lies on both the `P1–P2` and the `P3–O` path (as on the tree `((P1, P2), P3), O`), then the
expected unpolarized `ABBA` and `BABA` counts are equal. Thus `BABA - ABBA` and its sign reversal
have expectation `0`. The integrability hypotheses make both expectations meaningful.

articles.title: ABBA–BABA equals `f4`
articles.statement:
When the frequencies `p X ω` are themselves random (drift, and
the choice of locus) and one haplotype is sampled from each population independently given the
frequencies, the expected `BABA - ABBA` difference is `f4 P1 P2 P3 O`.

articles.title: Hudson's `F_ST`, ratio of averages
articles.statement:
**Hudson's `F_ST`, ratio of averages** (Bhatia et al. 2013): the ratio of the expected
summed numerator and denominator estimators is the population `hudsonFst`. This is a statement
about the ratio of expectations; the expectation of the ratio of the estimated sums is in
general not `hudsonFst`.

articles.title: Unbiasedness of the summed f2 estimator
articles.statement:
Summed over sites, Hudson's numerator estimator `∑ s, f2Hat` is unbiased for
`∑ s, (p_A s - p_B s) ^ 2` (independence is needed only within each site).

articles.title: Unbiasedness of the summed Hudson denominator estimator
articles.statement:
Summed over sites, Hudson's denominator estimator is unbiased for
`∑ s, hudsonDen (p_A s) (p_B s)`.

articles.title: qpWave rank bound
articles.statement:
**qpWave rank bound** (Reich et al. 2012, Supplementary Information; Patterson et al.
2012): if the frequency of every left population `L i` is an affine combination
`∑ l, a i l * p (S l)` (`∑ l, a i l = 1`, coefficients of any sign) of the frequencies of
`k + 1` source populations, then the matrix `f4 (L i) (L 0) (R j) (R 0)` (`i, j ≥ 1`) has rank
at most `k`; with `k` sources, at most `k - 1`. The right populations are arbitrary. The
converse (rank `k` forces `k + 1` streams) and the statistical rank test are not covered.

articles.title: Additivity of the sampling expectation
articles.statement: `sampleExpect` is additive in the function.

articles.title: Expected polarized ABBA–BABA difference
articles.statement:
Polarized form (Durand et al. 2011, with `q 3` the derived-allele frequency in the
outgroup): `E[BABA_pol - ABBA_pol] = (q₁ - q₂) q₃ (1 - q₄)`. When the outgroup is fixed for the
ancestral allele (`q 3 = 0`) this is `(q₁ - q₂) (q₃ - q₄)`, as in the unpolarized identity.

articles.title: ABBA–BABA identity
Sampling expectation of a product factorizes
articles.statement:
`sampleExpect` of a product of functions of single coordinates factorizes:
`E[∏ i, g i (x i)] = ∏ i, (g i true * q i + g i false * (1 - q i))`.

articles.title: Sampling expectation commutes with subtraction
articles.statement: `sampleExpect` commutes with subtraction of functions.

articles.title: Expectation under independent haplotype sampling
articles.statement:
Expectation of a function `g` of the configuration under independent sampling of one
haplotype per population at derived-allele frequencies `q`.

articles.title: Hudson's numerator is at most the denominator
articles.statement:
At each site Hudson's numerator is at most the denominator for frequencies in `[0, 1]`: the
difference is `p_A (1 - p_A) + p_B (1 - p_B) ≥ 0`.

articles.title: Configuration probabilities sum to one
articles.statement: The configuration probabilities sum to `1`.

articles.title: Admixture graph
articles.statement:
An admixture graph on the nodes `V` (Patterson et al. 2012): a rooted directed acyclic
graph in which every non-root node has one or two parents, with admixture proportions.

* `parents X` are the parents of `X`, the root has none, every other node has one or two;
* `prop X Y` is the probability that a lineage in `X` descends from parent `Y`: nonnegative,
  summing to `1` over the parents of a non-root node, and `0` off the parent set;
* the parent relation is well founded, i.e. the graph is acyclic (`V` is finite in all
  results).

articles.title: Drift model of an admixture graph
articles.statement:
The drift model of an admixture graph: the populations are the nodes, the root frequency is
`root`, the edge increments are `incr` (square integrable and pairwise uncorrelated), the drift
length of an edge is the second moment of its increment, and the weights are the lineage
weights of the graph.

articles.title: Edges of an admixture graph
articles.statement: The edges `(child, parent)` of the graph.

articles.title: Three-population statistic at an admixture node without edge drift
articles.statement:
With no drift on the admixture edges, an admixture node `X` with parents `A ≠ B` and
proportion `α = prop X A` has `f3 X A B = -α (1 - α) f2 A B` (the hypothesis of the seed's
`DriftModel.f3_admixture`, here derived from the graph).

articles.title: Three-population statistic at an admixture node
articles.statement:
The three-population statistic at an admixture node `X` with parents `A ≠ B`, proportions
`α = prop X A` and `β = prop X B` (`α + β = 1`), in a drift model with the graph's weights:
`f3 X A B = α² ℓ_{XA} + β² ℓ_{XB} - α β f2 A B`, where `ℓ_{XA}`, `ℓ_{XB}` are the drift
lengths of the two admixture edges.

articles.title: Three-population test is nonnegative on a tree
articles.statement: The three-population test on a tree-shaped admixture graph: `f3 C A B ≥ 0`.

articles.title: A tree-shaped admixture graph has binary loadings
articles.statement:
A tree-shaped admixture graph induces a drift model with binary loadings (all weights `0` or
`1`).

articles.title: Tree-shaped admixture graph
articles.statement: The graph is a tree: no node has two parents.

articles.title: Probability of a root-ward path in an admixture graph
articles.statement:
The probability of a root-ward path `[v₀, v₁, …, v_k]`: the product of the proportions
`prop vᵢ vᵢ₊₁`.

articles.title: First-step equation for root-ward paths
articles.statement: First-step equation for `paths`.

articles.title: Root-ward paths from a node of an admixture graph
articles.statement:
The root-ward paths from `X`: the lists `[X = v₀, v₁, …, v_k = root]` with each `vᵢ₊₁` a
parent of `vᵢ`.

articles.title: Admixture proportions are at most one
articles.statement: Admixture proportions are at most `1`.

articles.title: A lineage from a parent never passes through its child
articles.statement: Acyclicity: a lineage from a parent `Y` of `X` never passes through `X`.

articles.title: Visit probabilities on a tree are zero or one
articles.statement: On a tree every visit probability is `0` or `1`.

articles.title: First-step equation for visit probabilities
articles.statement: First-step equation for `visit`.

articles.title: Visit probabilities are at most one
articles.statement: Visit probabilities are at most `1`.

articles.title: Nonnegativity of visit probabilities
articles.statement: Visit probabilities are nonnegative.

articles.title: Every lineage reaches the root
articles.statement: Every lineage reaches the root.

articles.title: A lineage visits its own node with probability one
articles.statement: A lineage passes through its own node with probability `1`.

articles.title: Probability that a lineage passes through a node
articles.statement:
`visit X c` is the probability that the lineage of a gene sampled in `X`, traced toward the
root with parents chosen according to the admixture proportions, passes through `c`.

articles.title: Lineage weight recursion at an admixture node
articles.statement:
The recursion at an admixture node `X` with parents `A ≠ B`: with `α = prop X A`,
`w X = α w A + (1 - α) w B + w₀`, where `w₀` puts weight `α` on the edge `(X, A)`,
`1 - α` on `(X, B)` and `0` elsewhere.

articles.title: Path-sum formula for lineage weights
articles.statement:
Path-sum form of the lineage weights (Patterson et al. 2012): `weight X e` is the sum, over
the root-ward paths from `X` that traverse `e`, of the products of the admixture proportions
along the path.

articles.title: Lineage weights on a tree are zero or one
articles.statement: On a tree every lineage weight is `0` or `1`.

articles.title: First-step recursion for lineage weights
articles.statement:
First-step recursion for lineage weights: a lineage from `X` traverses `e` either as its
first step (if `e` starts at `X`) or after moving to a parent `Y`, chosen with probability
`prop X Y`.

articles.title: Lineage weights are at most one
articles.statement: Lineage weights are at most `1`.

articles.title: Nonnegativity of lineage weights
articles.statement: Lineage weights are nonnegative.

articles.title: Lineage weight recursion at a tree node
articles.statement: The recursion at a tree node `X` with the single parent `Y`: `w X = w Y + 1_{(X, Y)}`.

articles.title: Lineage weight of an edge in an admixture graph
articles.statement:
`weight X e` is the probability that the lineage of a gene sampled in `X` traverses the edge
`e = (c, p)`: it reaches `c` and then descends from `p`.

articles.title: Allele count of a gamete at one locus
articles.statement: The `0/1` count of the `'1'` allele carried by a gamete at one locus.

articles.title: Local-ancestry covariance in Morgans
articles.statement:
Local-ancestry covariance in Morgans:
`Cov(I_x, I_y) = α (1 - α) e^{-n d} (cosh d)^n` for loci `d` Morgans apart.

articles.title: Covariance of local-ancestry indicators after pulse admixture
articles.statement:
Pulse admixture: after `n` generations of random mating the local-ancestry indicators at
two loci with recombination fraction `r` have covariance `Cov(I_x, I_y) = α (1 - α) (1 - r)^n`
(for every real `α`, `r`; the biological domain is `0 ≤ α ≤ 1`, `0 ≤ r ≤ 1/2`). The
ancestry labels obey the two-locus random-mating recursion of `Linkage.recombine`
(Chakraborty and Weiss 1988).

articles.title: Gamete allele covariance equals linkage disequilibrium
articles.statement:
The covariance of the allele counts of one gamete is the linkage disequilibrium
`D = x_AB x_ab - x_Ab x_aB` (frequencies summing to `1`).

articles.title: Covariance of allele counts within a gamete
articles.statement:
The covariance of the allele counts at the two loci of one gamete drawn from the gamete
frequencies `x`: `∑ g, x g a(g.1) a(g.2) - (∑ g, x g a(g.1)) (∑ g, x g a(g.2))`.

articles.title: Joint law of local ancestry after an admixture pulse
articles.statement:
Joint law of the local-ancestry labels at the two loci right after the pulse
(`true` = descends from `A`): every gamete is entirely from `A` (probability `α`) or entirely
from `B`. This is `sourceMix` with perfectly differentiated markers (`pA = qA = 1`,
`pB = qB = 0`).

articles.title: Bernoulli allele frequency
articles.statement: The frequency `p` of the `'1'` allele (`b = true`) or `1 - p` of the `'0'` allele.

articles.title: Continuous decay is a lower bound for the exact factor under Haldane's map
articles.statement:
The continuous decay `e^{-n d}` used by Chakraborty and Weiss (1988) and Loh et al.
(2013) is a lower bound for the exact factor `(1 - r)^n` under Haldane's map (all real
`d`; the biological domain is `0 ≤ d`).

articles.title: f4 equals f2 for references branching off the path
articles.statement:
Branch points on the `A–B` path. Suppose that `A = A″ + uA`, `A′ = A″ + uA'`,
`B = B″ + uB`, `B′ = B″ + uB'` at the level of lineage weights, where `w A″ - w B″` is
disjoint in support from each of `uA`, `uB`, `uA'`, `uB'`, and each of `uA`, `uB` is disjoint
from each of `uA'`, `uB'`. On a tree this says that the paths `A″–B″`, `A″–A`, `B″–B`,
`A″–A′`, `B″–B′` share no edge (the vectors may be signed, so every rooting is allowed).
Then `f4 A B A′ B′ = f2 A″ B″`.

articles.title: Diploid genotype covariance in an admixed population
articles.statement:
The diploid genotype covariance in the admixed population `n` generations after the
pulse: `z(x, y) = 2 α (1 - α) (1 - r)^n δ(x) δ(y)` (Loh et al. 2013, Eq. 3, with the exact
discrete-generation factor `(1 - r)^n` in place of `e^{-n d}`).

articles.title: Diploid genotype covariance is twice the linkage disequilibrium
articles.statement:
The diploid genotype covariance is twice the haplotype one, `z = 2 D`: the two
same-gamete terms each contribute `D` and the two cross-gamete terms vanish by independence
(Loh et al. 2013, Eqs. 2–3).

articles.title: Covariance of unphased diploid genotypes
articles.statement:
The covariance of the unphased diploid genotypes `X = X₁ + X₂ ∈ {0, 1, 2}` at the first
locus and `Y = Y₁ + Y₂` at the second, for an individual made of two gametes `g`, `h` drawn
independently from `x` (random union of gametes). This is `z(x, y)` of Loh et al. (2013),
Eq. 1.

articles.title: Decay of admixture linkage disequilibrium over generations
articles.statement:
Admixture LD after `n` generations of random mating with recombination fraction `r`:
`D_n = (1 - r)^n α (1 - α) δ(x) δ(y)`.

articles.title: Admixture linkage disequilibrium right after the pulse
articles.statement:
Admixture LD right after the pulse: `D₀ = α (1 - α) δ(x) δ(y)`, with
`δ(x) = pA - pB`, `δ(y) = qA - qB` (Chakraborty and Weiss 1988).

articles.title: Haldane's map function: $1 - r = e^{-d}\cosh d$
articles.statement: With Haldane's map function, `1 - r = e^{-d} cosh d` for map length `d`.

articles.title: Exact decay factor under Haldane's map function
articles.statement: Exact decay in Morgans: `(1 - r)^n = e^{-n d} (cosh d)^n` when `r = haldane d`.

articles.title: Gamete frequencies after an admixture pulse
articles.statement:
Gamete frequencies right after the pulse: with probability `α` the gamete comes from `A`,
where the loci are in linkage equilibrium with `'1'` frequencies `pA` and `qA`, and otherwise
from `B` (frequencies `pB`, `qB`). The biological domain is `α, pA, qA, pB, qB ∈ [0, 1]`;
the identities below hold for all reals.

articles.title: Recombination preserves total gamete frequency
articles.statement: Recombination keeps gamete frequencies summing to `1` over any number of generations.

articles.title: Pulse gamete frequencies sum to one
articles.statement: The pulse gamete frequencies sum to `1`.

articles.title: Weighted LD amplitude with the admixed population as reference
articles.statement:
One reference `A` and the admixed population `C` itself, with no drift in `C` after the
pulse (`w C = α w A + (1 - α) w B`): the weights are `p A - p C = β δ` and the amplitude is
`2 α β^3 F2(A, B)^2` (Loh et al. 2013, Eq. 7).

articles.title: Weighted LD amplitude with two diverged references
articles.statement:
Two diverged references `A′`, `B′` branching off the `A–B` path at `A″` and `B″`: the
amplitude is `2 α β F2(A″, B″)^2` (Loh et al. 2013, Eq. 6).

articles.title: Weighted linkage disequilibrium in terms of the f4 statistic
articles.statement:
The expected weighted LD factors as `2 α (1 - α) (1 - r)^n (f4 A B R S)^2`: by
independence of the loci, `𝔼[δ(x) w(x) δ(y) w(y)] = 𝔼[δ w]^2` and `𝔼[δ w] = f4 A B R S`.
The identity holds with the Bochner-integral conventions as stated; it is meaningful when the
frequencies are square integrable, as in every `DriftModel`.

articles.title: Weighted LD amplitude with one diverged reference
articles.statement:
One diverged reference `R′` branching off the `A–B` path at `R″` (so `A = R″ + uA`,
`B = R″ + uB`, `R′ = R″ + uR` with pairwise disjoint supports) and the admixed population `C`
with no post-pulse drift: the weights `p R′ - p C` give the amplitude
`2 α β (α F2(A, R″) - β F2(B, R″))^2` (Loh et al. 2013, Eq. 8).

articles.title: Weighted LD amplitude with the true source populations
articles.statement:
Weights from the true mixing populations (`R = A`, `S = B`): the amplitude is
`2 α β F2(A, B)^2` (Loh et al. 2013, Eq. 4).

articles.title: Expected ALDER weighted linkage disequilibrium
articles.statement:
The expected ALDER two-site weighted-LD statistic `𝔼[z(x, y) w(x) w(y)]` (Loh et al.
2013, Appendix A, without distance binning). The loci `x` and `y` drift independently: `ω.1`
and `ω.2` are independent draws from `μ`, and `p X ω` is the frequency of the `'1'` allele in
population `X`. The covariance `z(x, y)` is that of the population formed `n` generations ago
as an `α : 1 - α` mixture of `A` and `B` (`genotypeCov_admixed`), and the weights are the
frequency differences `w = p R - p S` between two reference populations `R` and `S`.

articles.title: The admixture log-likelihood is monotone along the FRAPPE EM iterates
articles.statement: **The admixture log-likelihood is monotone along the FRAPPE EM iterates.**

articles.title: The admixture log-likelihood is monotone along the iterates
articles.statement:
**The admixture log-likelihood is monotone along the iterates** of any M-step `M` with
`Q(M θ | θ) ≥ Q(θ | θ)`.

articles.title: Each FRAPPE EM step does not decrease the admixture log-likelihood
articles.statement: **Each FRAPPE EM step does not decrease the admixture log-likelihood.**

articles.title: The EM theorem for the admixture model
articles.statement:
A step that does not decrease `Q(· | θ)` does
not decrease the admixture log-likelihood.

articles.title: Admixture log-likelihood
articles.statement:
The admixture log-likelihood
`ℓ(Q, F) = ∑ i, ∑ j, (g i j * log (qf θ i j) + (2 - g i j) * log (1 - qf θ i j))`.

articles.title: Positivity of expected alternative counts on polymorphic data
articles.statement: On polymorphic data the expected alternative counts are positive.

articles.title: Expected alternative-allele count of a SNP per population
articles.statement: The expected number of alternative copies of SNP `j` from population `k`.

articles.title: Positivity of the expected ancestry counts
articles.statement: The expected ancestry counts are positive when there is at least one SNP.

articles.title: Expected ancestry count of an individual
articles.statement: The expected number of allele copies of individual `i` from population `k`.

articles.title: Observation of one allele copy of a genotype
articles.statement: The observation `(i, j, a)` of copy `c` of genotype `g i j`.

articles.title: Allele-copy observations of a genotype matrix
articles.statement: The `2 |I| |J|` allele-copy observations of the genotype matrix `g`, indexed by `Fin`.

articles.title: Decomposition of the admixture EM objective
articles.statement:
`Q(θ' | θ)` splits into an ancestry term per individual and a two-point term per population
and SNP.

articles.title: The FRAPPE update maximizes `Q(· | θ)`
articles.statement:
No parameter `θ'` in the strictly
positive parameter set has a larger `Q(θ' | θ)` than the closed-form update `emStep g hg θ`.

articles.title: The FRAPPE EM step
articles.statement:
**The FRAPPE EM step** `θ ↦ (Q', F')`, with `Q' = mStepQ` and `F' = mStepF`; it
lies in the strictly positive parameter set when `J` is nonempty and every SNP is
polymorphic.

articles.title: Reference-allele indicator for a genotype copy
articles.statement:
Whether copy `c` of the genotype `g i j` (with `g i j` reference copies) carries the
reference allele: copies `c < g i j` do.

articles.title: Positivity of the admixture joint weight
articles.statement: The joint weight is positive (the standing hypothesis of the generic EM).

articles.title: Joint weight of an allele copy and its ancestral population
articles.statement:
The joint weight of an allele copy `(i, j, a)` and its ancestral population `k`:
`Q i k * (if a then F k j else 1 - F k j)`.

articles.title: The EM log-likelihood of the allele copies is the admixture log-likelihood
articles.statement: **The EM log-likelihood of the allele copies is the admixture log-likelihood.**

articles.title: Updated allele frequencies are less than one
articles.statement: On polymorphic data the updated allele frequencies are below one.

articles.title: Positivity of the updated allele frequencies
articles.statement: On polymorphic data the updated allele frequencies are positive.

articles.title: FRAPPE update of the allele frequencies
articles.statement:
The FRAPPE update of the allele frequencies,
`F' k j = (∑ i, ∑ c reference, r) / (∑ i, ∑ c, r)`.

articles.title: Positivity of the updated ancestry proportions
articles.statement: The updated ancestry proportions are positive.

articles.title: Updated ancestry proportions sum to one
articles.statement: The updated ancestry proportions of each individual sum to one.

articles.title: FRAPPE update of the ancestry proportions
articles.statement:
The FRAPPE update of the ancestry proportions,
`Q' i k = (∑ j, ∑ c, r) / (2 J)`.

articles.title: The marginal of an allele copy
articles.statement:
Reference with probability `qf θ i j`, alternative with
probability `1 - qf θ i j`.

articles.title: Parameters of the admixture model
articles.statement:
Parameters `θ = (Q, F)` of the admixture model: positive ancestry proportions `Q i k` summing
to one over `k`, and reference-allele frequencies `F k j` strictly between `0` and `1`.

articles.title: Polymorphic genotype data
articles.statement:
Every SNP is polymorphic in the sample: some individual carries a reference allele and some
individual carries an alternative allele. Without it the M-step frequency is `0` or `1`.

articles.title: Positivity of expected population counts on polymorphic data
articles.statement: On polymorphic data the expected population counts are positive.

articles.title: Expected population count of a SNP
articles.statement: The expected number of allele copies of SNP `j` from population `k`.

articles.title: Reference-allele probability is less than one
articles.statement: The reference-allele probability is below one.

articles.title: Positivity of the reference-allele probability
articles.statement: The reference-allele probability is positive.

articles.title: Reference-allele probability in the admixture model
articles.statement:
The reference-allele probability `qf θ i j = ∑ k, Q i k * F k j` of a copy of SNP `j` in
individual `i`.

articles.title: Reference and alternative counts add to the population count
articles.statement: Reference plus alternative expected counts give the population's expected count.

articles.title: Positivity of expected reference counts on polymorphic data
articles.statement: On polymorphic data the expected reference counts are positive.

articles.title: Expected reference-allele count of a SNP per population
articles.statement: The expected number of reference copies of SNP `j` from population `k`.

articles.title: Positivity of the admixture responsibilities
articles.statement: The responsibilities are positive.

articles.title: Ancestry responsibility of an allele copy (E-step)
articles.statement: The responsibility `r = P(z = k | copy c of (i, j))` (the E-step).

articles.title: Expected ancestry counts sum to the number of allele copies
articles.statement: The expected ancestry counts of an individual sum to its `2 J` allele copies.

articles.title: Sum over allele-copy data as a triple sum
articles.statement: A sum over the indexed data is a sum over individuals, SNPs and copies.

articles.title: Admixture responsibilities sum to one
articles.statement: The responsibilities of a copy sum to one over the populations.

articles.title: Symmetry of the per-locus f2 form
articles.statement: `f2Form` is symmetric.

articles.title: Per-locus f2 form in terms of f3 forms with a base population
articles.statement: `f2Form` in terms of the `f3` forms with base `o`.

articles.title: Per-locus f2 form as a special f4 form
articles.statement: `f2Form A B = f4Form A B A B`.

articles.title: Every f2 form lies in the f-statistic space
articles.statement: Every `f2Form` lies in `V_F`.

articles.title: Per-locus f2 form of a population with itself is zero
articles.statement: `f2Form A A = 0`.

articles.title: Per-locus f2 form
articles.statement: The per-locus `f2` form `x ↦ (x A - x B) ^ 2`.

articles.title: Per-locus f3 form is symmetric in its sources
articles.statement: `f3Form` is symmetric in its last two arguments.

articles.title: Every f3 form lies in the f-statistic space
articles.statement: Every `f3Form` lies in `V_F`.

articles.title: Per-locus f3 form vanishes when target equals first source
articles.statement: `f3Form C C B = 0`.

articles.title: Per-locus f3 form
articles.statement: The per-locus `f3` form `x ↦ (x C - x A) * (x C - x B)`.

articles.title: f4 statistic as the integral of the f4 form
articles.statement: The `f4` statistic is the integral of the `f4` form of the frequency vector.

articles.title: Polarization identity for the per-locus f4 form
articles.statement: `f4Form` in terms of `f2Form`: the polarization identity behind `f4_eq_f2`.

articles.title: Every f4 form lies in the f-statistic space
articles.statement: Every `f4Form` lies in `V_F`.

articles.title: Per-locus f4 form
articles.statement: The per-locus `f4` form `x ↦ (x A - x B) * (x C - x D)` on frequency vectors `x : P → ℝ`.

articles.title: Space spanned by the per-locus f-statistics
articles.statement:
The space `V_F` spanned by all per-locus f-statistics (all `f4Form`; `f2Form` and `f3Form`
are special cases).

articles.title: Dimension of the f-statistic space is n choose 2
articles.statement:
The f-statistics of `n` populations span a space of dimension `n choose 2`. (A linear order
on the populations, used to index the `f2` basis, is chosen in the proof.)

articles.title: Integral of a linear combination of f2 forms
articles.statement:
A linear combination of `f2` forms integrates to the same linear combination of `f2`
statistics, for square-integrable frequencies.

articles.title: Linear independence of Patterson's f2 basis
articles.statement: Patterson's `f2` basis: the forms `f2Form i j`, `i < j`, are linearly independent.

articles.title: Linear independence of Patterson's f3 basis
articles.statement:
Patterson's `f3` basis with base population `o`: the forms `f3Form o i j` with
`i ≤ j`, `i ≠ o`, `j ≠ o` are linearly independent.

articles.title: Patterson's f2 basis spans the f-statistic space
articles.statement:
Patterson's `f2` basis: the forms `f2Form i j`, `i < j`, span `V_F`, i.e. every
f-statistic is a linear combination of the `f2 Pᵢ Pⱼ`, `i < j`.

articles.title: Patterson's f3 basis spans the f-statistic space
articles.statement:
Patterson's `f3` basis with base population `o`: the forms `f3Form o i j` with
`i ≤ j`, `i ≠ o`, `j ≠ o` span `V_F`.

articles.title: Admixed population's weights in the admixture model
articles.statement:
In the admixture model, `C` is the `α : 1 - α` mixture of `A` and `B` plus its private
edge.

articles.title: Lineage weights of the three-population admixture model
articles.statement:
Lineage weights of the admixture model: `A` and `B` sit on edges `0` and `1`, and `C` is an
`α : 1 - α` mixture of `A` and `B` followed by drift on its private edge `2`.

articles.title: Centred leaf covariance as the double centring of f2
articles.statement:
The centred leaf covariance from `f2`: `K` is half the double centring of the `f2` matrix,
`K X Y = (f̄2 X· + f̄2 ·Y - f2 X Y - f̄2 ··) / 2`.

articles.title: Centred leaf covariance
articles.statement:
The centred leaf covariance `K X Y = 𝔼[(p X - p̄) * (p Y - p̄)]`: the second moments of the
frequencies centred across populations (not over `Ω`).

articles.title: f2 from the centred leaf covariance
articles.statement: `f2` from the centred leaf covariance: `f2 X Y = K X X + K Y Y - 2 K X Y`.

articles.title: f-statistics determine exactly the centred leaf covariance
articles.statement:
**f-statistics determine exactly the centred leaf covariance.** f-statistics see a model only through its centred leaf covariance: two square-integrable
frequency models have the same `f2` at every pair (hence the same `f3` and `f4`, by `f3_eq_f2`
and `f4_eq_f2`) if and only if they have the same centred leaf covariance.

articles.title: Star tree and admixture model have equal f2
articles.statement: The star tree and the admixture model have the same `f2` at every pair of populations.

articles.title: Star tree and admixture model have equal f4
articles.statement:
The star tree and the admixture model have the same `f4` (hence the same `f3`) at every
quadruple of populations.

articles.title: Star-tree model has binary loadings
articles.statement: The star-tree model has binary loadings.

articles.title: Admixture model lacks binary loadings
articles.statement: For `α ∉ {0, 1}` the admixture model does not have binary loadings.

articles.title: Mean frequency across populations
articles.statement: The mean frequency `p̄ ω = (1 / n) ∑ X, p X ω` across the `n` populations.

articles.title: Nonnegativity of the matching star-tree edge lengths
articles.statement:
The matching star tree has nonnegative edge lengths when `0 ≤ α ≤ 1`, `a, b ≥ 0`, and the
private drift of `C` is at least `α (1 - α)(a + b)`, i.e. when `f3 C A B ≥ 0` in the admixture
model.

articles.title: Edge lengths of the star tree matching an admixture model
articles.statement:
Edge lengths of the star tree matching the admixture model with edge lengths `a`, `b`, `c`:
`(1 - α)(a + b)`, `α (a + b)` and `c - α (1 - α)(a + b)`.

articles.title: Lineage weights of the three-population star tree
articles.statement:
Lineage weights of the star tree on three populations `0 = A`, `1 = B`, `2 = C`: edge `e`
is the leaf edge of population `e`.

articles.title: Column-centred genotype matrix
articles.statement: The genotype matrix with columns centred over the samples.

articles.title: Coalescent model linking heterozygosity and coalescence times
articles.statement:
The relation between allele frequencies and coalescence times under neutral
infinite-sites mutation, taken as the model assumption: the expected heterozygosity between
populations `X` and `Y` is `θ` times the expected coalescence time `coalTime X Y` of a gene
from `X` and a gene from `Y` (two genes drawn independently, so with replacement, when
`X = Y`). Time is in units of `2N` generations and `θ = 4Nu`. The measure `μ` is finite: it
ranges over the evolutionary randomness and, in practice, over a finite set of loci. For
`θ = 0` the coalescence times are not determined by the frequencies, and the identities below
then say that the f-statistics vanish.

articles.title: Column mean of a genotype matrix
articles.statement: The column mean `(1 / n) ∑ i, Z i s` of locus `s` over the `n` samples.

articles.title: Double centring of a square matrix
articles.statement:
The double centring `t̄ i· + t̄ ·j - t i j - t̄ ··` of a square matrix `t` (row, column and
grand means over the `n` indices).

articles.title: Peter's formula for $f_2$ via expected heterozygosity
articles.statement: Peter (2016): `f2 A B = π A B - (π A A + π B B) / 2`.

articles.title: $f_2$ in terms of expected coalescence times
articles.statement: `f2 A B = θ (𝔼 T_AB - (𝔼 T_AA + 𝔼 T_BB) / 2)`.

articles.title: $f_3$ in terms of expected coalescence times
articles.statement: `f3 C A B = θ / 2 * (𝔼 T_CA + 𝔼 T_CB - 𝔼 T_AB - 𝔼 T_CC)`.

articles.title: $f_4$ in terms of expected coalescence times
articles.statement: `f4 A B C D = θ / 2 * (𝔼 T_AD + 𝔼 T_BC - 𝔼 T_AC - 𝔼 T_BD)`.

articles.title: Genotype covariance as double-centred pairwise differences
articles.statement:
McVean (2009), deterministic form: the covariance of the centred genotype matrix is the
double centring of the pairwise-difference matrix, divided by `2 L`.

articles.title: Sample covariance of the centred genotype matrix
articles.statement:
The sample covariance `C i j = (1 / L) ∑ s, X i s * X j s` of the centred genotype matrix
`X` over the `L` loci.

articles.title: Probability that two genes differ at a biallelic site
articles.statement:
The probability `a (1 - b) + b (1 - a)` that a gene from a population with allele frequency
`a` and a gene from a population with allele frequency `b` differ at a biallelic site.

articles.title: Integrability of pairwise heterozygosity
articles.statement: `hetPair` of square-integrable frequencies is integrable on a finite measure space.

articles.title: McVean's theorem on expected genotype covariance
articles.statement:
McVean (2009): the expected genotype covariance is `θ / (2 L)` times the double centring of
the expected pairwise coalescence times,
`𝔼[C i j] = θ / (2 L) * (t̄ i· + t̄ ·j - t i j - t̄ ··)`.

articles.title: McVean's genealogical model for PCA
articles.statement:
McVean's genealogical setting for PCA, taken as the model assumption: random genotypes
`Z i s` (sample `i`, locus `s`), square integrable, whose expected numbers of pairwise
differences are `θ` times the expected pairwise coalescence times `coalTime i j` (neutral
infinite sites, time in units of `2N` generations, `θ` the total scaled mutation rate of the
`L` loci). For `θ = 0` the coalescence times are not determined by the genotypes.

articles.title: Expected heterozygosity between populations
articles.statement:
The expected heterozygosity `π X Y = 𝔼[hetPair (p X) (p Y)]` between populations `X` and
`Y` (within population `X` when `Y = X`).

articles.title: Number of pairwise differences between samples
articles.statement:
The number of pairwise differences `d i j = ∑ s, (Z i s - Z j s) ^ 2` (for `0`/`1`
haplotypes, the number of loci at which samples `i` and `j` differ).

articles.title: Squared frequency difference via pairwise heterozygosity
articles.statement: `(a - b) ^ 2 = hetPair a b - (hetPair a a + hetPair b b) / 2`.

articles.title: qpGraph design matrix of basis f4 statistics
articles.statement:
The qpGraph design matrix of basis statistics `f4 (A i) (B i) (C i) (D i)` for lineage
weights `w`: entry `(i, e)` is `(w Aᵢ e - w Bᵢ e) * (w Cᵢ e - w Dᵢ e)`.

articles.title: Uniqueness of the generalized least-squares maximizer
articles.statement:
Uniqueness of the GLS maximizer: for positive definite `Q` and a design matrix of full
column rank (`B.mulVec` injective), a vector `ℓ` with the same score as a solution `ℓ̂` of the
normal equations equals `ℓ̂`.

articles.title: The qpGraph score S2 depends on the basis
articles.statement:
`S2` is not basis independent (Patterson et al. 2012, after eq. 7): there are a positive
definite covariance `Q`, an invertible change of basis `A` and statistics `f`, `g` such that,
for every `λ`, the score changes.

articles.title: Predicted f4 statistics are linear in the edge lengths
articles.statement:
In the drift model, with the admixture weights fixed, the predicted statistics are linear in
the edge lengths: `g = B ℓ` for the design matrix `B`.

articles.title: Invertibility of the generalized least-squares Gram matrix
articles.statement:
For positive definite `Q` and a design matrix of full column rank, the GLS Gram matrix
`Bᵀ Q⁻¹ B` is invertible.

articles.title: Closed-form generalized least-squares estimate of edge lengths
articles.statement:
The closed-form GLS estimate `ℓ̂ = (Bᵀ Q⁻¹ B)⁻¹ Bᵀ Q⁻¹ f` solves the normal equations when the
Gram matrix is invertible.

articles.title: Basis independence of the qpGraph score S1
articles.statement:
`S1` is basis independent: under an invertible change of basis `A` of the statistics, with
the covariance transformed to `A Q Aᵀ`, the score is unchanged. (The identity holds for every
`Q`; for singular `Q` both sides are `0` by Mathlib's convention `Q⁻¹ = 0`.)

articles.title: Solutions of the normal equations maximize the score S1
articles.statement:
GLS maximizes `S1`: for positive definite `Q`, a solution `ℓ̂` of the normal equations
`Bᵀ Q⁻¹ B ℓ̂ = Bᵀ Q⁻¹ f` maximizes `ℓ ↦ S1(B ℓ)` over all `ℓ`.

articles.title: Generalized least-squares qpGraph score S1
articles.statement:
The qpGraph score `S1(g) = -½ (g - f)ᵀ Q⁻¹ (g - f)` (Patterson et al. 2012, eq. 6) of
predicted statistics `g` against estimated statistics `f` with error covariance `Q`.

articles.title: Score S2 as score S1 with a diagonal covariance
articles.statement:
`S2` is twice `S1` with the covariance replaced by the diagonal matrix of the
`Qᵢᵢ + λ`, when these are nonzero.

articles.title: Least-squares qpGraph score S2
articles.statement:
The least-squares qpGraph score `S2(g) = -∑ᵢ (gᵢ - fᵢ)² / (Qᵢᵢ + λ)` (Patterson et al.
2012, eq. 7). A term with `Qᵢᵢ + λ = 0` is `0` by the convention `x / 0 = 0`.

articles.title: Pair count as autocorrelation of cell occupancy counts
articles.statement: The pair count is the zero-padded autocorrelation of the cell occupancy counts.

articles.title: Zero-padded circular autocorrelation equals linear autocorrelation
articles.statement:
Zero-padded circular autocorrelation equals the linear one: if `U k = 0` for `k ≥ K`,
`2 K ≤ N + 1` and `j < K`, then `𝓕⁻(|𝓕 Ũ|^2)(j) = ∑_{k < K} U k U (k + j)`.

articles.title: Autocorrelation via the discrete Fourier transform
articles.statement:
The transform computation of the lag-`j` autocorrelation: the inverse discrete Fourier
transform of the power spectrum `|𝓕 Ũ|^2` of the zero-padded sequence, read at `j`.

articles.title: Brute-force weighted linkage disequilibrium sum
articles.statement:
The brute-force weighted-LD sum at cell offset `j`:
`∑_{x, y : c y = c x + j} ẑ(x, y) w(x) w(y)`, costing a pass over all pairs.

articles.title: Total of a per-SNP quantity over a grid cell
articles.statement: The total `U k = ∑_{x : c x = k} u x` of a per-SNP quantity `u` over grid cell `k`.

articles.title: Centred weighted genotype
articles.statement: The centred weighted genotype `(g i x - ḡ x) w x` of individual `i` at SNP `x`.

articles.title: ALDER's transform algorithm equals the brute-force weighted LD
articles.statement:
The transform algorithm computes the brute-force weighted-LD sum exactly, for every lag
`j < K`, when all SNPs lie in cells `c x < K` and the transform length satisfies
`2 K ≤ N + 1`.

articles.title: ALDER's Fourier-transform weighted LD computation
articles.statement:
ALDER's transform algorithm: for each individual, the zero-padded autocorrelation of the
cell totals of its centred weighted genotypes, computed through `𝓕`; summed over individuals
and divided by `m - 1`.

articles.title: Sample mean genotype at a SNP
articles.statement: The sample mean genotype `ḡ(x) = (1/m) ∑ i, g i x` at SNP `x` over `m` individuals.

articles.title: Zero padding of a sequence to $\mathbb{Z}/N\mathbb{Z}$
articles.statement:
Zero padding: the sequence `U` read on `ZMod N` through `k ↦ U k.val`. When `U` vanishes
from `K` on and `K ≤ N`, this is `U` followed by `N - K` zeros.

articles.title: Number of SNP pairs at a cell offset
articles.statement:
The number of ordered SNP pairs at cell offset `j`, by which ALDER divides the weighted
sum.

articles.title: Pair sum as cross-correlation of cell totals
articles.statement:
Grouping pairs by cell offset: if every SNP lies in a cell `c x < K`, the pair sum at
offset `j` is the lag-`j` cross-correlation of the cell totals.

articles.title: Brute-force pair sum at a cell offset
articles.statement:
The brute-force sum `∑_{x, y : c y = c x + j} u x v y` over ordered SNP pairs whose grid
cells differ by `j`.

articles.title: Unbiased sample covariance of genotypes
articles.statement:
The unbiased sample covariance `ẑ(x, y) = (1/(m - 1)) ∑ i, (g i x - ḡ x) (g i y - ḡ y)`
of the genotypes at SNPs `x` and `y` (Loh et al. 2013, Eq. 5; meaningful for `m ≥ 2`).

articles.title: Biallelic emission probabilities sum to one
articles.statement:
With biallelic sites, the two emission probabilities at a site sum to `1` over the target
allele, for each fixed panel column `col` (the emissions are conditional on the panel).

articles.title: Li–Stephens emission probability
articles.statement:
The emission probability: `1 - ε` if the target allele equals the allele of the copied
haplotype `k`, and the mismatch probability `ε` otherwise.

articles.title: The collapsed forward recursion computes the forward variables
articles.statement: **The collapsed forward recursion computes the forward variables** of the Li–Stephens HMM.

articles.title: Tabulated recursion computes the Li–Stephens forward variables
articles.statement: The tabulated `O(K)` recursion computes the forward variables of the Li–Stephens HMM.

articles.title: Tabulated O(K) forward variables
articles.statement: The `O(K)` forward variables, tabulated site by site: `O(t K)` operations in total.

articles.title: Forward variables of the collapsed recursion
articles.statement:
The forward variables of the collapsed recursion, as a function of site and state. This is
the untabulated specification (it re-evaluates earlier sites inside each sum); `fastForwardTab`
is the `O(t K)` implementation.

articles.title: Tabulated O(K) forward step
articles.statement: One tabulated `O(K)` step: the total of the previous table is computed once.

articles.title: One step of the collapsed forward recursion
articles.statement:
One step of the collapsed forward recursion on the previous site's forward variables `v`,
at output state `k`: `e_k ((1 - ρ) v k + ρ (∑ j, v j) / K)`. This is the pointwise
specification; each call evaluates the length-`K` sum, so use `fastStepTab` for the `O(K)`
per-site step.

articles.title: The Li–Stephens copying model
articles.statement:
**The Li–Stephens copying model** with `K` reference haplotypes, switch probability `ρ` and
mismatch probability `ε`, as a hidden Markov model with a uniform initial copied haplotype.

articles.title: Uniform initial law over haplotypes sums to one
articles.statement: The initial law (uniform over the `K` haplotypes) sums to `1`.

articles.title: The likelihood of the target haplotype
articles.statement:
**The likelihood of the target haplotype** (given the panel) is the sum of the collapsed
forward variables.

articles.title: Tabulated recursion computes the haplotype likelihood
articles.statement: The tabulated `O(K)` recursion computes the likelihood of the target haplotype.

articles.title: The tabulated Li–Stephens likelihood
articles.statement: **The tabulated Li–Stephens likelihood** in `O(t K)` operations.

articles.title: Observation sequence of a reference panel and target haplotype
articles.statement:
The observation sequence for the reference panel `H` (haplotype `k` carries allele
`H k t` at site `t`) and the target haplotype `x`.

articles.title: Site observation in the Li–Stephens model
articles.statement: The observation at a site: the column of reference alleles and the target allele.

articles.title: Collapse of the sum over predecessor haplotypes
articles.statement: The sum over predecessors collapses: `∑ j, v j * trans ρ j k = (1 - ρ) v k + ρ (∑ v) / K`.

articles.title: Li–Stephens transition rows sum to one
articles.statement: Each transition row sums to `1` (when `K` is invertible in `R`, e.g. `K ≠ 0` over `ℝ`).

articles.title: Li–Stephens copying transition probability
articles.statement:
The copying transition probability: switch with probability `ρ` to a uniformly random
reference haplotype (possibly the same one), otherwise keep copying `k`:
`(1 - ρ) [k = k'] + ρ / K`.

articles.title: Identifiability of the admixture proportion from f2 statistics
articles.statement:
Identifiability of the mixture proportion (our formulation): with the split points `A`, `B`
given, two references `X₁`, `X₂` satisfying the hypotheses of `f2_admixedBranch` and with
different contrasts `f2 A Xᵢ - f2 B Xᵢ` determine `α` from `f2` statistics.

articles.title: Admixed-branch identity for f2 statistics
articles.statement:
The admixed-branch identity (Lipson et al. 2013): if `Mx` is an `α : 1 - α` mixture of the
endpoints of the edges `a` (below `A`) and `b` (below `B`), followed by drift on `c`, and `A`,
`B`, `X` do not use `a`, `b`, `c`, then
`f2 Mx X = α f2 A X + (1 - α) f2 B X - α (1 - α) f2 A B + mixedDrift α ℓ_a ℓ_b ℓ_c`.

articles.title: f3 statistic as shared drift on a tree
articles.statement:
With binary loadings, `f3 O A B` is the total drift length of the edges shared by the paths
`O–A` and `O–B` (on a tree, the path from `O` to the `A–B` path).

articles.title: Outgroup f3 ranks populations by shared drift
articles.statement:
For a fixed outgroup `O` and population `A`, the outgroup `f3` ranks candidates `B` by the
drift they share with `A`.

articles.title: Outgroup f3 statistic
articles.statement:
Outgroup `f3` (Raghavan et al. 2014): with binary loadings, if the lineage of `O` shares no
edge with the lineages of `A` and `B`, then `f3 O A B` is the drift from the outgroup to the root
plus the drift shared by `A` and `B`.

articles.title: Mixed drift determined by f2 statistics
articles.statement: Given `α`, the mixed drift is determined by the `f2` statistics of one reference `X`.

articles.title: MixMapper mixed drift
articles.statement:
MixMapper's mixed drift `α² ℓ_a + (1 - α)² ℓ_b + ℓ_c`: the only combination of the terminal
drift lengths that enters the `f2` statistics of an admixed population.

articles.title: Admixture-graph drift model
articles.statement:
The admixture-graph drift model, stated at the level of second moments.

The allele frequency of population `X` is `root + ∑ e, weight X e * incr e` (see
`DriftModel.freq`), where `E` is the (finite) set of edges of the graph.

* `root` is the ancestral (root) allele frequency;
* `incr e` is the drift increment (frequency change) along edge `e`;
* `len e` is the drift length of edge `e`, i.e. the second moment `𝔼[incr e ^ 2]`;
* `weight X e` is the probability that a lineage sampled in `X` traverses `e`: on an
  admixture graph it is the sum, over root-to-`X` paths through `e`, of the product of the
  admixture proportions on the path; on a tree it is the `0`/`1` indicator that `e` lies on
  the root-to-`X` lineage.

f-statistics depend only on second moments of frequency differences, in which the root
cancels, so only these are assumed: the increments are square integrable, pairwise
uncorrelated (the mixed second moments `𝔼[incr e * incr f]`, `e ≠ f`, vanish, as they do for
independent mean-zero drift on distinct edges), and `𝔼[incr e ^ 2] = len e`.

articles.title: Symmetry of the f2 statistic
articles.statement: `f2` is symmetric.

articles.title: f2 as a special case of f4
articles.statement: `f2` is the special case `f4 A B A B`.

articles.title: f2 as a symmetric-difference drift length under binary loadings
articles.statement:
With binary loadings `f2 X Y` is the total drift length of the edges in exactly one of the
weight-`1` edge sets of `X` and `Y`. On a tree, where these sets are the root-to-`X` and
root-to-`Y` paths, this is the additive tree distance between `X` and `Y`.

articles.title: f2 in the drift model
articles.statement: `f2` in the drift model: `f2 X Y = ∑ e, (w X e - w Y e) ^ 2 * len e`.

articles.title: Nonnegativity of the f2 statistic
articles.statement: `f2` is nonnegative.

articles.title: f2 of a population with itself is zero
f2 statistic
articles.statement:
The statistic `f2 X Y = 𝔼[(p X - p Y) ^ 2]`, the expected squared allele-frequency
difference between populations `X` and `Y`.

articles.title: f3 of an admixture followed by drift
articles.statement:
Admixture followed by drift: if `C` is an `α : 1 - α` mixture of `A` and `B` that then
drifts along a private edge `c` (not traversed by `A` or `B`), then
`f3 C A B = len c - α (1 - α) f2 A B`; post-admixture drift can mask the admixture signal.

articles.title: f3 of a pure admixture
articles.statement:
If `C` is a mixture of `A` and `B` in proportions `α : 1 - α` (with no subsequent drift),
then `f3 C A B = -α (1 - α) f2 A B`.

articles.title: f3 in terms of f2
articles.statement: `f3` in terms of `f2`: `f3 C A B = (f2 C A + f2 C B - f2 A B) / 2`.

articles.title: f3 as a special case of f4
articles.statement: `f3` is the special case `f4 C A C B`.

articles.title: f3 in the drift model
articles.statement: `f3` in the drift model: `f3 C A B = ∑ e, (w C e - w A e) * (w C e - w B e) * len e`.

articles.title: Nondegenerate pure admixture gives negative f3
articles.statement:
Three-population test, converse direction: a nondegenerate pure admixture
(`0 < α < 1`, `f2 A B > 0`) yields a negative `f3 C A B`.

articles.title: f3 is nonnegative under binary loadings
articles.statement:
With binary loadings `f3` is nonnegative; on a tree it is the drift length of the path from
`C` to the `A–B` path.

articles.title: f3 statistic
articles.statement:
The statistic `f3 C A B = 𝔼[(p C - p A) * (p C - p B)]` of a target population `C` against
two source populations `A` and `B`.

articles.title: f4 of an admixed population scales with the mixture proportion
articles.statement:
If `X` is an `α : 1 - α` mixture of `Y` and `C`, then `f4 A O X C = α * f4 A O Y C`
(bilinearity of `f4`, together with `f4 A O C C = 0`).

articles.title: f4 is symmetric under exchanging the two pairs
articles.statement: `f4` is symmetric under exchanging the two pairs.

articles.title: f4 in terms of f2
articles.statement: `f4` in terms of `f2`: `f4 A B C D = (f2 A D + f2 B C - f2 A C - f2 B D) / 2`.

articles.title: f4 vanishes for edge-disjoint paths
articles.statement:
`f4 A B C D = 0` when no edge contributes to both the `A–B` and the `C–D` path. On a tree
with split `AB | CD` the paths `A–B` and `C–D` share no edge, so this hypothesis holds.

articles.title: f4 in the drift model
articles.statement:
`f4` in the drift model: the root cancels, and `f4 A B C D` is the drift length shared by
the paths `A–B` and `C–D`, weighted by `(w A e - w B e) * (w C e - w D e)`.

articles.title: f4-ratio estimation of the admixture proportion
articles.statement:
**f4-ratio estimation of the admixture proportion.** f4-ratio estimation (Patterson et al. 2012). Let `X` be an `α : 1 - α` mixture of a
source lineage `Y` and of `C`, where `Y` is unsampled but sister to the sampled population `B`
relative to the `A–O` path, so that `f4 A O Y C = f4 A O B C`. If this value is nonzero, the
ratio `f4 A O X C / f4 A O B C` of two estimable statistics recovers the admixture
proportion `α`.

articles.title: f4 changes sign when the first pair is swapped
articles.statement: `f4` changes sign when the first pair is swapped.

articles.title: f4 changes sign when the second pair is swapped
articles.statement: `f4` changes sign when the second pair is swapped.

articles.title: f4 statistic
articles.statement: The statistic `f4 A B C D = 𝔼[(p A - p B) * (p C - p D)]`.

articles.title: Allele frequency of a population in the drift model
articles.statement:
The allele frequency of population `X`: the root frequency plus the weighted sum of the
drift increments of the edges traversed by lineages from `X`.

articles.title: Nonnegativity of the fixation index $F_{ST}$
articles.statement:
`F_ST = (H_T - H_S) / H_T` is nonnegative for nonnegative weights summing to `1`. The ratio
is defined only when `H_T > 0` (at a fixed allele `H_T = H_S = 0`), so that is assumed.

articles.title: Binary loadings of a drift model
articles.statement:
The model has binary loadings if every lineage weight is `0` or `1`.

Every tree model has binary loadings: there `weight X e` is the indicator of `e` lying on the
root-to-`X` path. The converse fails, since nothing forces the weight-`1` edge sets to be
compatible root-to-leaf paths: two edges of length `1` and four populations with weight
vectors `00`, `10`, `01`, `11` have binary loadings, but their `f2` distances form a square,
which violates the four-point condition of tree metrics. The results below use only the binary
values, so they apply to every tree.

articles.title: Wahlund effect
articles.statement:
The Wahlund effect: with nonnegative weights summing to `1`, subdivision lowers
heterozygosity, `H_S ≤ H_T`.

articles.title: Mean within-subpopulation heterozygosity
articles.statement: Mean within-subpopulation (Hardy–Weinberg) heterozygosity `H_S = ∑ i, c i * 2 q i (1 - q i)`.

articles.title: Total heterozygosity of the pooled population
articles.statement:
Total heterozygosity `H_T = 2 q̄ (1 - q̄)` expected under random mating of the pooled
population.

articles.title: Square of a difference of square-integrable frequencies is integrable
articles.statement: A difference of square-integrable frequencies has integrable square.

articles.title: Bilinearity of the second moment of drift increments
articles.statement:
Bilinearity of the second moment of increments:
`𝔼[(∑ e, a e * incr e) * (∑ f, b f * incr f)] = ∑ e, a e * b e * len e`.

articles.title: Drift lengths are nonnegative
articles.statement: Drift lengths are nonnegative.

articles.title: Lineage of a population in the drift model
articles.statement: The edges of weight `1` for population `X`; on a tree, the root-to-`X` lineage.

articles.title: Mean allele frequency of a subdivided population
articles.statement:
Mean allele frequency `q̄ = ∑ i, c i * q i` of a population made of subpopulations with
weights `c i` and allele frequencies `q i`.

articles.title: Population frequencies are square integrable
articles.statement: Population frequencies are square integrable.

articles.title: Weighted sum of drift increments is square integrable
articles.statement: A weighted sum of increments is square integrable.

articles.title: Three-population test: negative f3 rules out a tree
articles.statement:
Three-population test: a negative `f3 C A B` is incompatible with binary loadings, hence
with every tree model.

articles.title: Wahlund identity
articles.statement:
Wahlund identity: for weights summing to `1`, `H_T - H_S = 2 ∑ i, c i * (q i - q̄) ^ 2`,
twice the weighted variance of subpopulation frequencies.

articles.title: Linear parent–offspring regression model
articles.statement:
The linear parent–offspring model on a population described by a probability measure `μ`:
the parental (mid-parent) value `parent` and the offspring value `offspring` are integrable,
`mean` is the population mean of the parental value, and the offspring value regresses linearly
on the parental value, `𝔼[O | P] = mean + h2 * (P - mean)` (equivalently
`O = mean + h2 (P - mean) + e` with `𝔼[e | P] = 0`). Here `h2` is the heritability.

articles.title: Breeder's equation
articles.statement:
The breeder's equation (Lush 1937): if the selected group `s` is determined by the parental
value (an event of `σ(P)`) and has positive mass, the response to selection is the heritability
times the selection differential, `R = h² S`.

articles.title: Selecting the whole population gives zero response
articles.statement: Selecting the whole population gives no response, `R = 0`.

articles.title: Response to selection
articles.statement:
The response to selection `R = 𝔼[O | selected] - μ`: the mean offspring value of the
selected parents, relative to the population mean.

articles.title: Selecting the whole population gives zero selection differential
articles.statement: Selecting the whole population gives no selection differential, `S = 0`.

articles.title: Selection differential
articles.statement: The selection differential `S = 𝔼[P | selected] - μ` of the selected group `s`.

articles.title: Fisher's average effect of an allele at a single locus
articles.statement: Fisher's average effect of allele `a`: `α a = ∑_b p_b g(a, b) - μ`.

articles.title: Cockerham–Kempthorne variance components
articles.statement:
Cockerham–Kempthorne variance components up to order `n`: `V i j = V_{A^i D^j}` is the
component of `i` additive and `j` dominance factors (`V 1 0 = V_A`, `V 0 1 = V_D`,
`V 2 0 = V_AA`, …). They are nonnegative, there is no `(0, 0)` component, and the genetic
covariance of relatives with `2φ` and `Δ` is `∑_{i, j ≤ n} (2φ)^i Δ^j V i j`. This structure
is the stated representation; it is proved for one locus by `LocusModel.relCov_eq`.

articles.title: Genetic covariance of relatives in Cockerham form
articles.statement: The genetic covariance of relatives with coefficients `2φ = twoPhi` and `Δ = Δ`.

articles.title: Dominance deviation at a single locus
articles.statement: The dominance deviation `δ a b = g(a, b) - μ - α a - α b`.

articles.title: One-locus phantom heritability, unconditional
articles.statement:
With monozygotic twins
(`k₂ = 1`), dizygotic twins (`k = (1/4, 1/2, 1/4)`) and a common environment `C`,
`2 (Cov_MZ - Cov_DZ) = V_A + (3/2) V_D`.

articles.title: Equality case of the phantom heritability inequality
articles.statement: Equality holds iff every non-additive component of order `≤ n` vanishes.

articles.title: Falconer's estimator in terms of Cockerham components
articles.statement:
Falconer's estimator is `V_A` plus the non-additive components weighted by
`2 (1 - 2^{-i} 4^{-j})` (derived from Cockerham's coefficients).

articles.title: Falconer's estimator
articles.statement:
**Falconer's estimator** under the ACE model, in covariance form: monozygotic twins have
`2φ = Δ = 1`, dizygotic twins (full sibs) `2φ = 1/2`, `Δ = 1/4`, and both share the same
common-environment covariance `C`; the estimator is `2 (Cov_MZ - Cov_DZ)`.

articles.title: Single-locus model under random union of gametes
articles.statement:
A single locus under random union of gametes: allele frequencies `p` on a finite allele
set and symmetric genotypic values `g a b` (the mean phenotype of genotype `{a, b}`).

articles.title: Population mean genotypic value at a single locus
articles.statement: The population mean genotypic value `μ = ∑ p_a p_b g(a, b)`.

articles.title: Phantom heritability
articles.statement:
**Phantom heritability** on the correlation scale (Zuk et al. 2012): with phenotypic
variance `V_P > 0`, the narrow-sense heritability `V_A / V_P` is at most the ACE estimate
`2 (r_MZ - r_DZ)`, where `r = Cov / V_P`.

articles.title: Single-locus covariance between relatives in Cockerham form
articles.statement: The one-locus covariance between relatives is the Cockerham form of `toComponents`.

articles.title: Covariance between relatives
articles.statement:
**Covariance between relatives** at one locus (Fisher 1918; in the IBD form of Falconer and
Mackay ch. 9): for IBD probabilities summing to one,
`E[G_X G_Y] - μ² = (k₁ / 2 + k₂) V_A + k₂ V_D`, i.e. `2φ V_A + Δ V_D` with kinship
`φ = k₁ / 4 + k₂ / 2` and `Δ = k₂`.

articles.title: Mean product of genotypic values of two relatives
articles.statement:
The mean product of genotypic values of two non-inbred relatives that share `0`, `1`, `2`
alleles identical by descent with probabilities `k₀, k₁, k₂`: given the IBD state, the
non-shared alleles are independent draws from `p`.

articles.title: Average effects are centred
articles.statement: Average effects are centred: `∑ p_a α_a = 0`.

articles.title: Dominance deviations are orthogonal to every allele
articles.statement: Dominance deviations are orthogonal to every allele: `∑_b p_b δ_{ab} = 0`.

articles.title: Single-locus model as Cockerham components
articles.statement:
The one-locus model as Cockerham components of order `1`: `V 1 0 = V_A`, `V 0 1 = V_D`,
`V 1 1 = 0`.

articles.title: Additive variance of the Cockerham components
articles.statement: The additive variance `V_A = V 1 0` (zero if `n = 0`).

articles.title: Phantom heritability inequality
articles.statement: The phantom-heritability inequality in covariance form: `V_A ≤ 2 (Cov_MZ - Cov_DZ)`.

articles.title: Nonnegativity of the single-locus additive variance
articles.statement: The additive variance is nonnegative.

articles.title: Additive variance at a single locus
articles.statement: The additive variance `V_A = 2 ∑ p_a α_a²`.

articles.title: The additive fit is least squares
articles.statement:
**The additive fit is least squares** (Fisher definition of average effects): every
additive fit `c + h a + h b` has mean squared error at least `V_D`, the error of
`μ + α a + α b`.

articles.title: Nonnegativity of the single-locus dominance variance
articles.statement: The dominance variance is nonnegative.

articles.title: Dominance variance at a single locus
articles.statement: The dominance variance `V_D = ∑ p_a p_b δ_{ab}²`.

articles.title: Fisher decomposition
articles.statement: **Fisher decomposition** of the genetic variance: `V_G = V_A + V_D`.

articles.title: Genetic variance at a single locus
articles.statement: The genetic variance `V_G = ∑ p_a p_b (g(a, b) - μ)²`.

articles.title: Additive coding at the first locus
articles.statement: The additive coding `a_A = (X₁ - p) + (X₂ - p)` (centred allele count) at locus `A`.

articles.title: Additive coding at the second locus
articles.statement: The additive coding `a_B = (Y₁ - q) + (Y₂ - q)` at locus `B`.

articles.title: Correlation of additive codings equals the gametic correlation
articles.statement:
The correlation of the additive codings is the gametic correlation
`r = D / √(V_A V_B)`.

articles.title: Dominance coding at the first locus
articles.statement: The dominance coding `d_A = (X₁ - p) (X₂ - p)` at locus `A`.

articles.title: Dominance coding at the second locus
articles.statement: The dominance coding `d_B = (Y₁ - q) (Y₂ - q)` at locus `B`.

articles.title: Dominance coding of allele indicators equals the dominance encoding
articles.statement:
For `0`/`1` allele indicators the dominance coding `(X₁ - p) (X₂ - p)` depends only on the
genotype `X₁ + X₂` and equals its dominance encoding.

articles.title: Dominance LD is the square of additive LD
articles.statement:
**Dominance LD is the square of additive LD** (Palmer et al. 2023, graphical abstract): the
correlation of the dominance codings at two loci is the square of the correlation of their
additive codings.

articles.title: Dominance encoding of a biallelic genotype
articles.statement:
The dominance encoding of a biallelic genotype `g ∈ {0, 1, 2}` (count of the allele with
frequency `p`): `p²`, `-p (1 - p)`, `(1 - p)²`. Dividing by `-p (1 - p)` gives the encoding
`-p / (1 - p)`, `1`, `-(1 - p) / p` of Palmer et al. (2023).

articles.title: Allele frequency at the first locus
articles.statement: The allele frequency (mean coding) `p = E X₁` at locus `A`.

articles.title: Allele frequency at the second locus
articles.statement: The allele frequency (mean coding) `q = E Y₁` at locus `B`.

articles.title: Additive linkage disequilibrium is twice the gametic one
articles.statement: Additive LD: `E(a_A a_B) = 2 D`.

articles.title: Additive and dominance codings at different loci are uncorrelated
articles.statement:
The additive coding at `A` and the dominance coding at `B` are uncorrelated:
`E(a_A d_B) = 0`.

articles.title: Second moment of the additive coding at the first locus
articles.statement: The additive coding has second moment `E(a_A²) = 2 V_A`.

articles.title: Second moment of the additive coding at the second locus
articles.statement: The additive coding has second moment `E(a_B²) = 2 V_B`.

articles.title: Dominance linkage disequilibrium is the square of the gametic one
articles.statement: Dominance LD: `E(d_A d_B) = D²`.

articles.title: Second moment of the dominance coding at the first locus
articles.statement: The dominance coding has second moment `E(d_A²) = V_A²`.

articles.title: Second moment of the dominance coding at the second locus
articles.statement: The dominance coding has second moment `E(d_B²) = V_B²`.

articles.title: Gametic linkage disequilibrium
articles.statement: The gametic linkage disequilibrium `D = E (X₁ - p) (Y₁ - q)`.

articles.title: Two-locus diploid genotype under random union of gametes
articles.statement:
A diploid two-locus genotype under random union of gametes: the haplotypes
`(X₁, Y₁)` and `(X₂, Y₂)` are independent and identically distributed, with square-integrable
allele codings.
